findings.title: autocorrWavelengthKm pools all latitudes but converts lag→km with a single equatorial spacing, inflating equirect wavelengths ~12%
findings.mechanism: The title asserts: the lag→km conversion uses one equatorial spacing while the correlation itself was pooled over all latitudes. That is exactly what the code does. On an equirect grid the eastward metric spacing is R·cos(lat)·dλ, so a form of fixed physical size λ spans λ/(R cos lat dλ) COLUMNS — more columns the further from the equator. Pooling rows of unequal km-per-column therefore produces a composite autocorrelation that is a mixture of the true correlation evaluated at compressed arguments; its first zero crossing, and the first local maximum after it, land at a LARGER column lag than the equatorial one, and multiplying that lag by the equatorial dx inflates the answer. Two aggravating details the title does not name but that are the same defect: deviations are taken about the GLOBAL mean, so any row whose own mean is offset (polar caps especially) contributes a positive, non-decaying pedestal at every lag that pushes the zero crossing further out or removes it entirely; and there is no cos(lat) area weighting and no pole guard, unlike slopeStats (descriptors.js:190) which explicitly excludes |lat| > 85 for precisely this reason. NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault: this is a grid-geometry error in the measuring half and bites whatever field is handed to it — synth FBM or baked relief alike.
findings.evidence: descriptors.js:430-432 — `const dxKm = grid.mode === 'patch' ? grid.spanKmX / W : cellSpacingKm(grid, Math.floor(H / 2)).dx;` — ONE scalar spacing for the whole sphere, taken at the mid row (H=128 ⇒ row 64 ⇒ lat −0.703°, cos = 0.99992, i.e. equatorial to 8e-5). descriptors.js:440-445 — `for (let j = 0; j < H; j++) { for (let i = 0; i + lag < W; i++) { s += (field[j*W+i] - mean) * (field[j*W+i+lag] - mean); n++; } }` — every row contributes with equal per-pair weight and every deviation is taken about the GLOBAL mean. descriptors.js:458 — `if (ac[lag] > ac[lag-1] && ac[lag] >= ac[lag+1]) return lag * dxKm;` — the column lag is multiplied by that single spacing. Live path: fieldSampler.js:166 `d.autocorrWavelength = autocorrWavelengthKm(h, grid);` runs for BOTH frames on BOTH grid kinds, and planet-lod-lab.html:6911 makes equirect the DEFAULT branch of `sampleField` (`: s.sampleEquirect({ width: o.width || 256, height: o.height || 128, radiusEarth })`), i.e. `_lab.fieldProbe()` with no arguments — the call the lab's own usage comment advertises first (planet-lod-lab.html:6893, `_lab.fieldProbe()  whole sphere, current body`). planet-lod-lab.html:6939 — `: d.angular.autocorrWavelength * sVisNow` — on an equirect probe `formWavelength` is undefined, so the screen proxy silently falls back to this number.
findings.impact: Whole-sphere `_lab.fieldProbe()` returns an `autocorrWavelength` that is systematically too large, in both frames, and the `screenWavelengthProxy` it falls back to inherits the error. I measured the size of the bias on a synthetic field that is isotropic BY CONSTRUCTION (superposition of 24 3-D plane waves of identical |k| on the sphere, so the true great-circle wavelength is exactly 2πR/K), sampled on the shipped 256×128 equirect geometry at radiusEarth 1, 12 seeds per K. Against an equatorial-band control built from the SAME field (rows |lat| < 11° re-labelled as a patch with the equatorial spacing), so that the only difference is the latitude pooling: K=8 truth 5004 km → band control 6358 km (×1.27) vs full-sphere pooled 11605 km (×2.32); K=12 → 4691 (×1.41) vs 12109 (×3.63); K=16 → 3205 (×1.28) vs 9479 (×3.79); K=24 → 2241 (×1.34) vs 9329 (×5.59). The pooling alone therefore contributes a further ×1.8 to ×4.2 on top of the metric's own ~1.3× broadband bias, and it also raises the failure rate (3/12 NaN returns on the full sphere vs 0/12 on the band). The title's '~12%' is far too small for this field; the true magnitude is field-dependent (it is set by how the field's variance is distributed in latitude) but the DIRECTION — inflation — is structural and unavoidable.
findings.fixSketch: Two options, both inside descriptors.js (instrument code, so a direct edit is in-discipline; generation source is untouched). (a) Cheapest and honest: restrict the equirect autocorrelation to a latitude band, reusing the existing POLE_GUARD_DEG machinery — better, a tighter band (say |lat| ≤ 30°, where 1/cos spans only 1.15) — accumulate only those rows, and return the excluded fraction the way slopeStats does at descriptors.js:209 so a caller can never mistake a partial measurement for a whole one. (b) Correct: compute the autocorrelation per row against that row's OWN mean, convert each row's lag axis to km with that row's dx, resample onto a common km-lag axis, and combine with cos(lat) area weights — then find the zero crossing and first peak on the km axis. (a) is a 15-line change and removes most of the bias; (b) removes it. Either way add a planted-control test: an isotropic 3-D plane-wave field of known great-circle wavelength must be recovered to a stated tolerance, since the current suite (tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:243-251) only exercises the PATCH branch on a pure sinusoid and never touches the equirect branch at all. CAUTION: tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:28 greps every file under src/worldengine/** for /visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP/ INCLUDING comments — any explanatory comment about the display scale must avoid those three tokens.
findings.blastRadius: descriptors.js only, plus one new test. Behavioural change to `_lab.fieldProbe()` output for equirect probes and to `screenWavelengthProxy` on that path. If option (a) is taken, `autocorrWavelength` gains a companion excluded-fraction field, which sweep.js will then see as a new descriptor — check it lands under a namespace the sweep does not fit.
findings.claimAmbiguity: Two points. (i) The title says 'equatorial spacing'; the code uses `Math.floor(H/2)`, the mid row, which for the shipped even H is 0.7° off the equator — a 8e-5 difference, so the readings are the same claim, not two. (ii) The '~12%' magnitude I could not reproduce and my own measurement is 2–5×. findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: Keep HIGH (matches the banked record's `severity: high`), but the title's '~12%' magnitude is wrong and the adjudicator was right to say so — measured inflation on an isotropic control is x2.3-x4.6, of which x1.6-x3.7 is the latitude pooling alone. findings.title: The instrument samples the synth FBM body, not the baked relief the planet actually renders at the live default
bankedResultsAffected: RADIUS-CENSUS.md — the `Substrate / relief | ✅ WIRED | MEASURED | ∝ R^0.458 ± 0.015` row: the exponent stands as a measurement of the LEGACY analytic body under the display lever, but its attribution to the World Engine relief writer must be withdrawn. Direction of the correction: the row's evidence class drops from MEASURED to UNMEASURED for the carrier body; the census's own tectonics evidence suggests the carrier response, if measured, would be nearer exponent 0 than 0.5.
RADIUS-CENSUS.md — 'Answering Max's sentence directly': the bullet **Substrate/relief does**, measured** must be requalified the same way.

AC-CURVE-live.md — the whole 'The radius response' section (form size 50.26 / 67.89 / 96.00 km at R = 4/8/16, physical exponent +0.4583, angular −0.5417, on-screen −0.0417): numbers unchanged (at R >= 4 the crossover has already handed the render to the same synth body), but the document must state which body it measured. The near-exact agreement of +0.458 with the display lever's own R^0.5 is now explained rather than a coincidence.

AC-SAMPLE-live.md — the 'First radius signal' table rows R = 0.5 / 1 / 2, where the rendered body was 50% / 100% / 50% baked and the sampled body was 0% baked. Already withdrawn on other grounds; add this ground.
NOT affected: the R1 contract's band-count numbers (5→14, exponent 0.500000, 3.03→6.01 cycles). Those came from the e5 band channel and a pixel/field spectral estimator, not from fieldSampler.
findings.mechanism:
The title asserts the instrument reads the analytic FBM body while the planet renders the baked carrier cube at the live default. That is exactly what the code does. The claim's stated basis — that both share the `uniforms` object — is true but irrelevant: sharing uniforms does not share the SHADER. `HEIGHT_FRAG` (planet-lod-rivers.js:328) = HEIGHT_GLSL + ROUTER_MAIN, and ROUTER_MAIN's base term (planet-lod-rivers.js:323) is a bare `fbmd(...)` with no `uReliefBakeStrength` branch and no `sampleBakedRelief` fetch — the uniform is bound and simply ignored. The lab planet's own fragment shader (planet-lod-lab.html:381-386) does branch, and at the shipped default (reliefBakeStrength 1.0, radius 1.0, crossover exactly 1) the blend weight on the synth term is exactly 0. So at boot the instrument measures a field that contributes literally nothing to the rendered macro body, while the World Engine panel simultaneously prints `relief: writer carrier` (planet-lod-lab.html:4289-4294, carrierOn true because strength > 0 and route() sets heightSource 'carrier').

DOWNSTREAM-OF-CARRIER-OFF LINKAGE: this IS Max's suspicion, and it inverts his phrasing in a useful way. The legacy synth path is not un-wired — it is wired into the MEASURING instrument rather than into the render. The same `bakeReliefCrossover` he was told about (R1 statusNote parking-lot item) is what makes the two paths coincide again at R >= 4: sVis = sqrt(R), |log2 sVis| = 0.5|log2 R|, so the crossover forces uReliefBakeStrength to 0 at R >= 4 and the planet falls back to the same fbmd body the instrument reads. The AC-CURVE sweep ran at R = 4/8/16 — i.e. entirely inside the region where the render had already been handed to synth. The instrument and the render agree there BY ACCIDENT of the crossover, and disagree completely everywhere near the default.
findings.evidence:
THE INSTRUMENT'S SHADER HAS NO BAKED BRANCH AT ALL. planet-lod-rivers.js:323 (inside ROUTER_MAIN, the fragment main() the instrument renders) — `    vec4 hd = fbmd(vPos, uOctaves, fwBase);` — an unconditional analytic-FBM base. `uReliefBakeStrength` and `sampleBakedRelief` appear NOWHERE in planet-lod-rivers.js (grep: zero hits), and planet-lod-rivers.js:328 builds the instrument's program as `export const HEIGHT_FRAG = HEIGHT_GLSL + ROUTER_MAIN;`, which fieldSampler.js:79 consumes via `entry = { sampler: createHeightSampler({ renderer, uniforms, verts: dirs, octavesDuringRead }), dirs };`.

THE PLANET'S SHADER DOES BRANCH. planet-lod-lab.html:381-386 — `          if (uReliefBakeStrength > 0.0) {` / `            vec4 baked = sampleBakedRelief(vObjN);          // object-space direction-keyed, seam-free` / `            vec4 synth = fbmd(vPos, uOctaves, fwBase);      // in-shader DETAIL residual` / `            hd = vec4(baked.x * uReliefBakeStrength, baked.yzw * uReliefBakeStrength) + synth * (1.0 - uReliefBakeStrength);`. At strength 1 the synth term is multiplied by exactly 0.

THE LIVE DEFAULT IS STRENGTH 1 AT RADIUS 1. planet-lod-lab.html:2546 — `      reliefBakeStrength: 1.0,                                 // AC2 LAB live initial = ON (A/B visible)`; planet-lod-lab.html:2258 — `      planetRadiusEarth: 1.0,  // real-units scale: planet radius in Earth radii (6371 km = 1 RE)`; planet-lod-lab.html:5898 — `      uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength.value = grainCarveUI.reliefBakeStrength * bakeReliefCrossover(sVis);` with planet-lod-lab-core.js:125-131 returning EXACTLY 1 at sVis = 1 (`const d = Math.abs(Math.log2(sVis));   // sVis = 1 → 0 exactly` / `return 1 - smoothstep(0, BAKE_CROSS_SPAN, d);`) and planet-lod-lab-core.js:47 `return Math.pow(radiusEarth, VIS_SCALE_EXP);` with VIS_SCALE_EXP = 0.5 (:45).

THE ROUTER ITSELF WAS RE-POINTED AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS NOT. tests/relief-router-repoint.test.js:65-77 pins that route() gates on `uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength` and that the baked branch reads `height = marginHeight` (carrier data) — `NOT sampler.read`; the createHeightSampler RTT survives only as the `strength-0 fallback` (:88-98). fieldSampler.js:9-12 still claims the opposite: `// `createHeightSampler` from planet-lod-rivers.js, the same float-RTT point-cloud readback the river // router has used against the live height field since AC4. That sampler binds the SAME `uniforms` // object the planet material consumes, so what we measure is what the planet is actually rendering`.
findings.impact:
At the live default (R = 1) the field probe is 100% decoupled from the rendered macro body. Concretely: `_lab.fieldProbe()` at boot describes analytic fBm + the shared combiner chain, while the surface being shaded is the plate-Voronoi carrier + the same combiners. Every vertical and horizontal descriptor at that operating point is a measurement of the wrong field.

For the banked numbers the harm is ATTRIBUTION, not arithmetic. RADIUS-CENSUS.md's headline row — `| **Substrate / relief** | ✅ **WIRED** | MEASURED | Physical form size ∝ R^**0.458 ± 0.015** ...` — credits the World Engine relief system with a measured radius response. What was actually measured is the legacy analytic body re-keyed by the display lever (planet-lod-lab.html:5887 `uniforms.uDispDomainScale.value = sVis;` feeding planet-lod-height.glsl.js:755 `float freq = uNoiseScale * 0.3 * uDispDomainScale;`). With sVis = R^0.5 that predicts a physical exponent of exactly +0.5 — which is what 0.458 ± 0.19 (the corrected interval) is. The writer carrier body was never sampled, at any radius, by any banked run. Given the census's own Tectonics row (`stressFabric.js`, `province.js`, `passiveMargins.js`, `substrate.js`, `sphereField.js`: **no radius and no gravity reference at all**), the carrier body may well show NO radius response — the opposite verdict.

AC-SAMPLE-live.md's R = 0.5 / 1 / 2 rows are worse: at those radii the crossover leaves the render 50% / 100% / 50% baked, so those rows describe a field the planet was substantially not rendering. (They are already withdrawn for an unrelated reason — the spectralExcessPeak false positive.)
findings.fixSketch:
Two parts, both honouring AC-POSCTRL (no edits to generation source).

(1) TRUTH-IN-LABELLING FIRST, cheap and non-negotiable: have the sampler read the live blend gate and return it on every sample, and have describeSample refuse to imply it measured the render when it did not. The gate value is already on the shared uniforms object the sampler holds — read `uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength.value` at read() time and surface it as e.g. `sample.bakedFraction` plus a `fieldIsRenderedBody: bakedFraction === 0` flag and a note, exactly as the module already does for `kmPerUnit` (fieldSampler.js:99-102, :201-204). Put it OUTSIDE `meta` so sweep.js fits it and any sweep that crosses the crossover is self-documenting. NOTE THE FENCE: tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:28 denies /visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP/ across src/worldengine/** INCLUDING COMMENTS — so the note must say "display blend gate" or "disc scale", never sVis.

(2) THE REAL FIX: give the instrument a second readback path that samples the baked cube, so it can measure what actually renders. The cheapest honest version is a second RTT main() alongside ROUTER_MAIN that reproduces the planet's :381-386 branch (baked*s + synth*(1-s)) — new exported string in planet-lod-rivers.js, selected by fieldSampler, generation code otherwise untouched. Alternatively, and cheaper still for census purposes: read `riverOverlay.reliefCarrier.height` directly (the CPU-side array that IS baked into the cube, per tests/relief-router-repoint.test.js:78-86) via a lab-side adapter that resamples it onto the instrument's grids — no GPU path at all, and it measures the writer output the census is actually asking about.

findings.title: responseCurve's settle is a wall-clock setTimeout, but the radius -> field coupling is written only by the rAF frame loop
findings.mechanism:
The title asserts the settle is wall-clock while the driver→field coupling is frame-driven. That is exactly what the code does. `setPoint` mutates `state.planetRadiusEarth`, calls the synchronous `applyDrivers()` (which re-derives preset uniforms, band count, seeds — none of them radius→shader), then sleeps on `setTimeout`. The radius only reaches the GPU when `frame()` next runs and recomputes `sVis` and writes `uDispDomainScale`/`uCraterScale`/`uMountainScale`. In a visible tab at 60 Hz, 700 ms is ~42 frames and the coupling lands with enormous margin. Under rAF suspension — a hidden/occluded/minimised tab, which is the normal condition for a CDP/agent-driven run — Chrome stops rAF entirely while `setTimeout` merely clamps to ≥1000 ms. The sweep then advances through every radius sampling one frozen shader field.
CARRIER-OFF ADJACENCY (not identity): `uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength.value = grainCarveUI.reliefBakeStrength * bakeReliefCrossover(sVis)` (:5898) is likewise a frame-only write, so the carrier-off state Max is chasing is also established only by the rAF loop. But the instrument's field (planet-lod-rivers.js:317-357 ROUTER_MAIN → `fbmd(vPos, uOctaves, fwBase)`) never reads `uReliefBakeStrength` at all — the baked/synth blend lives in the lab's own planet shader at planet-lod-lab.html:381-385. findings.title: The read-only / uniform-restoration invariant is asserted only in comments — no test, and a reachable path violates it
findings.mechanism:
The title makes two claims: (a) the read-only invariant has no test, (b) some reachable path breaks it. (a) is unambiguously true — no test anywhere touches fieldSampler.js, so the module's most load-bearing promise ("changes nothing about the rendered frame") is enforced by a comment. (b) holds in its strongest form via the delegate: createHeightSampler.read() has no try/finally, and sweep.js's deliberately failure-tolerant loop (sweep.js:54-60) makes "a reading throws and the sweep continues" a sanctioned path rather than a crash. After such a throw the lab is left with uOctaves pinned at 9, uFwClamp forced to 0, the render target pointed at the instrument's 182x181 float RTT, and the clear colour black/alpha 0. In the live lab, frame() repairs three of those four on the next tick; the clear colour is permanent for the page's life. Note the overlap: notVerified index 16 states that same clear-colour residue against planet-lod-rivers.js and is in a different cluster. The distinct contribution of THIS finding is the test gap, and the fact that fieldSampler.js makes the promise while delegating the enforcement to a module it does not own.

A second, subtler limb of the same invariant is broken and is NOT a throw-path: the comment says the pinning means "a measurement never depends on where the camera happens to be." That is false — see finding [15]. So the invariant as stated is violated on the happy path too, silently.
findings.evidence:
THE CLAIM IS COMMENT-ONLY. fieldSampler.js:14-16 — `// READ-ONLY. It pins uOctaves during the read (a fixed high LOD, so a measurement never depends on // where the camera happens to be) and restores every uniform it touched. It writes no field, adds no // feature card, and changes nothing about the rendered frame.`

ZERO TESTS. `grep -rln "fieldSampler|describeSample|sampleEquirect|samplePatch|verticalAxis|kmPerUnit" tests/` returns NOTHING. tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js imports only descriptors.js and stats.js (:14-15). No test in the repo instantiates createFieldSampler or asserts a uniform is restored.

THE REACHABLE VIOLATION. planet-lod-rivers.js:453 — `    const prevOct = uniforms.uOctaves.value, prevFw = uniforms.uFwClamp.value;` … :465 `    uniforms.uOctaves.value = prevOct; uniforms.uFwClamp.value = prevFw;` — restoration is on the straight-line success path with NO try/finally, and the same is true of the clear colour (:458 `renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0); renderer.clear();` → :464 `renderer.setClearColor(_prevClear, prevAlpha);`) and the render target (:457 → :463). fieldSampler.js:95 and :119 both call `sampler.read()` bare. A throw inside is not hypothetical-only: sweep.js:54-60 wraps every reading in `try { … } catch (err) { … failures.push(…) }` — the instrument's own orchestration layer treats a mid-read throw as a NORMAL, tolerated event and carries on sweeping.

WHAT SELF-HEALS AND WHAT DOES NOT. planet-lod-lab.html frame() rewrites `uniforms.uOctaves.value = oct;` (:5880), `uniforms.uFwClamp.value = state.fwClamp ? 1 : 0;` (:5910) and `renderer.setRenderTarget(sceneTarget);` (:6413) every frame. It never rewrites the clear colour — `grep -n setClearColor planet-lod-lab.html` has no frame-loop hit.
findings.impact: No banked number is wrong because of this. Its cost is that the instrument's central discipline claim is unfalsifiable: nothing would have caught the [15] camera-dependence, nothing would catch a future edit that drops a restore, and nothing catches the throw-path residue. For a module whose entire justification is "a fake number is worse than no number", an untested read-only invariant is the load-bearing gap. This is also the cheapest fix in the cluster.
findings.fixSketch: Add tests/instrument-fieldsampler.test.js with a fake renderer + fake uniforms object (no GPU needed — createHeightSampler only calls renderer.getRenderTarget/getClearColor/getClearAlpha/setRenderTarget/setClearColor/clear/render/readRenderTargetPixels, all trivially stubbable; THREE is already a vitest dep and planet-lod-rivers.js imports headlessly, as tests/planet-lod-rivers-discharge-param.test.js:8 proves). Assert: (1) after a successful sampleEquirect/samplePatch every key on the uniforms object deep-equals its pre-call value — a snapshot diff, not a hand-listed allowlist, so a future uniform touch is caught by construction; (2) the same holds when the stub renderer's render() throws (this test FAILS today — it is the planted-defect control); (3) the module never writes to any renderer state it did not first read. Then wrap planet-lod-rivers.js read()'s body in try/finally so (2) passes. Keep the fix in rivers.js, not fieldSampler.js — it is the delegate that owns the state.

findings.title: bandCount discards short runs instead of folding them, so single-row noise splits one band into two
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the code discards where the docstring promises folding, and that this SPLITS one band into two. Verified by execution against the shipped module. A 32-row profile that is +1 for rows 0-15 and −1 for rows 16-31 returns bands: 2, runs: 2 (correct). Flipping ONE row inside the + band (row 5 → −1) gives runs: 4 ([+5, −1, +10, −16]); the len-1 run is filtered out and the two surviving + runs are still counted separately, so bands: 3 — the single-row noise inflated the count, which is precisely the thing the docstring says cannot happen. The converse error also exists and the title does not name it: a profile of 32 rows at −1 with a single +1 row at row 16 gives runs: 3 and bands: 2, i.e. deleting the lone run leaves its two neighbours as two bands where the noise-rejected truth is one. So `filter` is wrong in both directions. Independent corroboration inside the same review: finding [22] ('bandCount's noise-rejection claim is false, and the fixtures contain no noise to reject') is the test-side statement of the same defect — tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:333-350 exercises only clean sinusoids and a constant field. Not connected to the carrier-off fault.
findings.evidence: descriptors.js:549-551 (docstring) — 'Runs shorter than `minRunRows` are folded into their neighbour so single-row noise cannot inflate the count.' descriptors.js:569-570 (code) — `const kept = runs.filter((r) => r.len >= minRunRows);` / `return { bands: kept.length, runs: runs.length, profile };`. `filter` deletes the short run and leaves the two neighbours as separate entries; folding would merge them. Live path: fieldSampler.js:180 `if (sample.kind === 'equirect') d.bandCount = bandCount(h, grid).bands;`, reached by the default `_lab.fieldProbe()` (planet-lod-lab.html:6911).
findings.impact: The equirect `bandCount` descriptor over-counts by roughly the number of single-row sign flips in the zonal profile. On the lab's actual height field — red noise averaged over 256 longitudes, so the profile is smooth — the number of len-1 runs is small but not zero; the defect matters most for exactly the noisy giant-atmosphere profile the descriptor exists to characterise. Two further points bound how much anyone should care today: (i) `bandCount` is computed only for equirect samples and the default sweep probe is a PATCH (planet-lod-lab.html:6960, `probe = { mode: 'patch', latDeg: 10, lonDeg: 20, spanKm: 2000, ... }`), so no responseCurve/planSweep run has ever exercised it; (ii) the descriptor also takes a PLAIN row mean for its profile (descriptors.js:560-562) with no cos(lat) weighting, which is a second, separate bias not covered by any of the 38 titles.
findings.fixSketch: Replace the filter at descriptors.js:569 with a genuine fold: iterate the runs, and whenever a run's length is below minRunRows, absorb it into the longer adjacent run (flipping its sign) and MERGE the two neighbours into one run; repeat until no short runs remain (the merge can create a new short run only in pathological profiles, so cap the passes). Then bands = the length of the merged list. Keep `runs` (the raw count) as-is — it is the honest pre-fold diagnostic. Pin with a control test built from the two cases above: (a) two clean bands + one flipped row must return 2, not 3; (b) 31 rows of one sign with a single opposite row must return 1, not 2; (c) the existing k-cycle sinusoid fixtures must still return 2k. Alternative, if folding is judged too clever: change the docstring to say what the code does and add a `shortRunsDropped` count so the caller can see the count is unreliable — but that leaves a number in the report that is wrong in both directions, which is against this instrument's stated purpose.
findings.blastRadius: descriptors.js:569-570 plus tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js (the 'zonal band count' describe block, :333-350). One live consumer, fieldSampler.js:180. No production/shader code. Does NOT touch climate-e5.js, which has its own independent counter.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The word 'band' could have meant the census's band count. It does not, and this is the single most important thing to say about this finding: the R1 banked '5 → 14 across R = 3 → 16' number is `state.e5BandCount`, produced by a completely different implementation — climate-e5.js:218, `if ((u < 0) !== (prevU < 0)) bandCount++;`, a zero-crossing count on the realized zonal-wind profile, surfaced at planet-lod-lab.html:2872 — and the re-UAT belt count came from a spectral estimator on the rendered disc. Neither goes anywhere near descriptors.js:552. The rejected reading is therefore 'this changes the census band-count row'; it does not.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives. I did not take the adjudicator's execution result on trust — I re-derived both cases by hand from the code and they are exactly right. Case 1 (their claim of over-count): a 32-row profile of +1 for rows 0-15 and -1 for 16-31 with row 5 flipped to -1 gives mean = (15 - 17)/32 = -0.0625, so the sign test at :565 (`profile[j] - mean >= 0 ? 1 : -1`) yields runs [+5, -1, +10, -16]; `runs.filter((r) => r.len >= minRunRows)` at :569 with the default minRunRows = 2 deletes the len-1 run and leaves the two +runs as separate entries, so bands = 3 where the docstring's promised folding would give 2. Case 2 (the converse they add, which the title does not name): 32 rows at -1 with a single +1 at row 16 gives mean = -0.9375, runs [-16, +1, -15], kept = 2 where noise-rejected truth is 1. So `filter` is wrong in both directions, as claimed. NOT ALREADY_FIXED (bandCount at 552-571 is outside every 0744fa4 hunk, and instrument-review-fixes.test.js does not import it). Critically, the lab's own `state.bandCount` (planet-lod-lab.html:3315) and climate-e5's `bandCount` diagnostic are DIFFERENT quantities with the same name — the census's '5 -> 14 bands' row and the R1 +0.532 exponent come from those, not from this descriptor. I checked that explicitly so the banked-result call could not be wrong by name collision.

findings.title: radialPSD and spectralExcessPeak use the mean of the two spans on a non-square patch, so x- and y-features of different true size report the same wavelength
findings.mechanism: The title asserts that a mean-of-spans conversion collapses two axes of different physical extent onto one wavelength. The code does exactly that: a feature at (kx=m, ky=0) has true wavelength spanKmX/m, one at (kx=0, ky=m) has spanKmY/m, both land in radial bin r=m at :300, and both are reported as ((spanKmX+spanKmY)/2)/m. The comment at :313 shows this was a deliberate 'report sanely' choice rather than an oversight — but 'sanely' here means 'returns a number', not 'returns the right number'. What makes this NOT a live defect: no shipped entry point can build a patch grid with spanKmX ≠ spanKmY, so on every path the instrument has actually run, (a+b)/2 === a exactly and the conversion is correct. Worth noting for whoever fixes it: unequal WIDTH and HEIGHT (which the API does allow — fieldSampler.js:112 takes both) does NOT break the conversion, because wavelength = span/k is in cycles-per-domain and is independent of cell count; only unequal SPANS break it. Unrelated to the carrier-off fault.
findings.evidence: descriptors.js:313-314 — `// The domain's physical diagonal scale: use the mean span so a non-square patch still reports sanely.` / `const spanKm = (grid.spanKmX + grid.spanKmY) / 2;` then :320 `return { dominantWavelengthKm: spanKm / peak.k, ... }`. descriptors.js:377 repeats it verbatim inside spectralExcessPeak, feeding :392 `wavelength: spanKm / best.k`. Radial binning that erases the axis: descriptors.js:300 `const r = Math.round(Math.hypot(kx, ky));`. BUT the only shipped construction site is square: fieldSampler.js:125-126 — `physical: physicalPatchGrid(width, height, spanKm, spanKm),` / `angular: angularPatchGrid(width, height, spanKm, spanKm, radiusEarth),` — the same `spanKm` scalar passed for both axes, and `samplePatch` (fieldSampler.js:112) accepts only one `spanKm`, as does the lab (planet-lod-lab.html:6910, `spanKm: o.spanKm || 2000`).
findings.impact: Zero on every measurement taken so far, and zero on anything reachable through `_lab.sampleField` / `_lab.fieldProbe` / `responseCurve` / `planSweep`. The exposure is a latent trap on the exported function: descriptors.js is a public, headlessly-testable module, and radialPSD/spectralExcessPeak accept any hand-built grid (the tests already build grids by hand — tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js:19 constructs `GRID` directly). The first non-square window anyone measures — a latitude-band strip, say, which is the obvious shape for a jet-structure probe — silently gets a wavelength averaged between the two axes with no warning.
findings.fixSketch: Guard rather than average. At the top of radialPSD (beside the existing mode check at descriptors.js:279) throw unless the per-cell metric spacings match: `if (Math.abs((spanKmX/W)/(spanKmY/H) - 1) > 1e-6) throw new Error('radialPSD: radial averaging assumes an isotropic patch; got dx=… dy=…')`. Radial binning is meaningless on an anisotropic grid regardless of which span you convert with, so refusing is more honest than picking a span — and refusing costs nothing today because no live caller can trip it. If an anisotropic patch is ever genuinely wanted, the correct change is to bin on physical wavenumber (kx/spanKmX, ky/spanKmY) instead of integer index, which is a larger job and should be scoped, not slipped in.
findings.blastRadius: descriptors.js:279 (new guard), :313-314 and :377 (dead once guarded). tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js and tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js both construct square grids, so nothing existing breaks; add one test asserting the throw. No live caller, no shader, no banked number.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The title could be read as the much bigger claim that radial averaging itself is wrong because it conflates x and y. I rejected that reading: radial averaging is the stated, intended design (descriptors.js:266, 'Radially-averaged power spectral density'), it is correct for an isotropic patch, and a directional spectrum is a different metric, not a bug fix. The reading I adjudicated is the narrow, literal one — the (spanKmX+spanKmY)/2 conversion — which is a genuine defect but is unreachable through any shipped entry point. That unreachability is why I put severity at low against the 2026-07-25 'medium'.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives as a LATENT defect. Citations are exact: :313-314 carry the comment and `const spanKm = (grid.spanKmX + grid.spanKmY) / 2;`, :320 is `return { dominantWavelengthKm: spanKm / peak.k, ... }`, :377 repeats the mean verbatim inside spectralExcessPeak feeding :392 `wavelength: spanKm / best.k`, and :300 is `const r = Math.round(Math.hypot(kx, ky));`. The mechanism is real: a mode at (kx=m, ky=0) has true wavelength spanKmX/m and one at (kx=0, ky=m) has spanKmY/m, both land in bin r=m, and both are reported as ((spanKmX+spanKmY)/2)/m. I independently verified the adjudicator's subtler claim — that unequal WIDTH/HEIGHT does NOT break it: a plane wave with kx cycles across spanX and ky across spanY has physical wavelength 1/sqrt((kx/spanX)^2 + (ky/spanY)^2), which equals span/hypot(kx,ky) exactly when spanX == spanY, independent of cell counts, so `Math.round(Math.hypot(kx,ky))` is the right bin index for any W,H at equal spans. That claim holds. Unreachability also holds, and I checked it more broadly than they did: repo-wide grep shows physicalPatchGrid/angularPatchGrid are constructed at exactly two sites, fieldSampler.js:125-126, both passing the same `spanKm` scalar twice; samplePatch (fieldSampler.js:112) accepts one `spanKm`; the lab passes `spanKm: o.spanKm || 2000` (planet-lod-lab.html:6909); the only other callers are tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:53-54, also square. NOT ALREADY_FIXED — 0744fa4's hunks at @@ -305 and @@ -349 sit either side of these lines but the diff added the `modes` field and rewrote the detection block, not the span conversion, which is why :314/:377 still read as originally written.

On the evidence the downgrade is CORRECT — the defective line is executed on every live call but is exactly right on every reachable input, so present impact is nil — but it should have been flagged as a change from the banked severity, as they correctly did flag for [26]. findings.title: networkLengthKm counts only 4-connected pairs, so a diagonal one-cell-wide channel measures exactly zero length
findings.mechanism: The title asserts a diagonal one-cell-wide channel measures exactly zero. Confirmed, literally: on a purely diagonal mask no cell has an on 4-neighbour, so the accumulator is never touched and the function returns 0 rather than ~√2 × (cell diagonal) × steps. The function's own docstring (descriptors.js:505-509) sells pair-summing as the exact alternative to 'cells times cell size' and demonstrates exactness on a meridian and an equator — both axis-aligned, and both are what the tests pin (tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:293-310). Diagonals are the case the design note never considers. Not related to the carrier-off fault.
findings.evidence: descriptors.js:520-527 — the entire neighbour set is two 4-connected offsets: `const iE = grid.mode === 'equirect' ? (i + 1) % W : i + 1;` / `if (iE < W || grid.mode === 'equirect') { if (on(iE, j)) len += dx; }` / `if (j + 1 < H) { if (on(i, j + 1)) { const dyS = (dy + cellSpacingKm(grid, j + 1).dy) / 2; len += dyS; } }`. No (i+1, j+1) or (i−1, j+1) term anywhere in the function. Verified by execution against the shipped module: a 10-cell pure diagonal mask on a 32×16 equirect grid at R=1000 returns exactly 0; the stair-stepped equivalent (each diagonal step doubled to share a 4-neighbour) returns 3432.76 km.
findings.impact: Zero today, and this is the honest headline: networkLengthKm has NO caller outside descriptors.js and the test file. Grepping the whole repo, the only references are its two wrappers `drainageDensity` (:535) and `boundaryDensity` (:540), which are themselves uncalled, plus tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:299-331. `describeSample` never invokes any of the three (fieldSampler.js:158-195), so no probe, no sweep and no banked number has ever run this code. Its severity is entirely prospective — and the prospect is concrete and near: RADIUS-CENSUS.md:145-147 names 'per-system field observables (a plate-boundary mask, an edifice detector, a channel mask, a band profile) wired into describeSample' as the exact next slice of work, and a plate-boundary mask on a Voronoi tessellation is diagonal-heavy by construction. Wired as-is, it would under-report boundary length by an amount that depends on the mask's orientation statistics — a bias that would then be misread as a tectonic signal when the census's PARTIAL tectonics row is finally measured.
findings.fixSketch: Add the two diagonal pairs with their true metric separation: for each on cell, test (i+1, j+1) and (i−1, j+1) (with the equirect longitude wrap already used at :520) and add hypot(dxMid, dySMid) where dxMid is the mean of the two rows' dx and dySMid the existing averaged dy. Weight them — the standard fix for chain-code length bias is to NOT count a diagonal at full √2 when the 4-connected neighbours are also on, or the stair-step case double-counts; the clean form is: count 4-connected pairs at full length, and count a diagonal pair only when the two cells share no on 4-neighbour. Pin with three controls: (a) the pure diagonal must return ≈ steps × hypot(dx, dy) rather than 0; (b) the existing meridian and equator fixtures must be unchanged to their current 6-decimal tolerance; (c) a stair-step must not gain length relative to today. Do this BEFORE the R2 mask work lands, not after, so the first plate-boundary measurement is not taken with a known orientation bias.
findings.blastRadius: descriptors.js:512-532 and the 'network length' describe block in tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js (:292-332). No live caller to regress. If the fix lands after masks are wired into describeSample, it moves every drainage/boundary density measured in between — which is the argument for landing it first.
findings.claimAmbiguity: None — the title states a specific, checkable numeric consequence and it reproduces exactly. The only judgement call was severity: 'low' is defensible today (dead code path), but I kept medium because the census has already named the work that will make this code live, and a measurement bug is cheapest to fix while nothing depends on the number.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives, and the core claim needs no execution to confirm: descriptors.js:512-531 contains exactly two neighbour offsets — the eastward test at :520-521 and the southward test at :522-527 — with no (i+1, j+1) or (i-1, j+1) term anywhere in the function, so on a purely diagonal one-cell-wide mask no `on` cell has an `on` 4-neighbour, `len` is never incremented, and the function returns 0. That is a literal reading of the shipped code, not a reported experiment. The docstring/design-note gap is real too: :505-508 sells pair-summing as exact and demonstrates it on a meridian and an equator, both axis-aligned, and tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:293-331 pins exactly those two orientations plus an empty mask — no diagonal fixture exists. Dead-code claim independently verified and stronger than they stated: a repo-wide grep for networkLengthKm returns only its definition (:512), its two wrappers drainageDensity (:536) and boundaryDensity (:541), and tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:299/309/318/325/331. Neither wrapper has any caller at all. describeSample (fieldSampler.js:147-206) never invokes any of the three — I read the whole function to confirm, not just grep. So no probe, sweep, or banked number has ever executed this code. Their forward-looking claim also checks out: RADIUS-CENSUS.md:146-147 does read 'Turning them into measured rows needs per-system field observables (a plate-boundary mask, an edifice detector, a channel mask, a band profile) wired into `describeSample`'. NOT ALREADY_FIXED (outside all three 0744fa4 hunks).

findings.title: autocorrWavelengthKm on an equirect grid averages lag products across all latitudes with equal weight, then converts with the mid-row spacing
findings.mechanism: This is the SAME defect as finding [0], stated more precisely: [0] names the symptom (inflated wavelengths, '~12%') and calls the conversion spacing 'equatorial'; [9] names the two halves of the cause (equal-weight pooling across latitudes; conversion with the mid-row spacing) and is literally correct about both. They are one bug at descriptors.js:430-447 and must be fixed once, not twice. See [0] for the full mechanism, the measured magnitude, and the fix.
findings.evidence: Identical lines to finding [0]: descriptors.js:432 `: cellSpacingKm(grid, Math.floor(H / 2)).dx;` (the mid-row spacing this title names literally) and descriptors.js:440-445, the unweighted double loop `for (let j = 0; j < H; j++) { for (let i = 0; i + lag < W; i++) { s += ... ; n++; } }` with `ac[lag] = n > 0 ? s / n : 0;` at :446 — equal weight per cell pair, hence equal weight per row, hence equal weight per latitude.
findings.impact: Same as [0]: whole-sphere autocorrWavelength inflated by a field-dependent factor — measured ×1.8 to ×4.2 attributable to the pooling alone on an isotropic control field at the shipped 256×128 geometry — plus an elevated NaN rate (3/12 vs 0/12 on the equatorial-band control). One additional consequence [9]'s phrasing makes explicit and [0]'s does not: because the weighting is per-CELL-PAIR and equirect rows all have W cells, the polar rows — which sample a physically tiny circle and are therefore nearly constant along the row — are counted as heavily as the equatorial rows, and because deviations are measured about the global mean (descriptors.js:442) a polar row sitting off the global mean contributes a flat positive pedestal at every lag.
findings.fixSketch: Do not fix separately — fold into the single fix for [0]. If only one line can be changed, the pooling (descriptors.js:440-445) is the half that carries the error; changing only the conversion spacing at :432 cannot help, because there is no single spacing that is right for a pooled multi-latitude correlation.
findings.blastRadius: Same as [0]. The only extra note: whoever closes these should mark one of the two as a duplicate in the triage ledger so the fix round is not credited twice.
findings.claimAmbiguity: None in the title itself — it describes the code line by line. The only adjudication needed was whether [0] and [9] are distinct findings; they are not, they are the same lines seen from the symptom end and the cause end. I rejected treating [9] as the narrower 'mid-row vs equatorial row' complaint (a 8e-5 effect, which would make it NOT_REAL), because the title's first clause explicitly names the equal-weight pooling, which is the real defect.
findings.refuterReason:
Verdict survives on the merits — it is the same defect as [0], which I re-established from source above, and [9]'s phrasing is the more literally accurate of the two ('mid-row spacing' is exactly what `cellSpacingKm(grid, Math.floor(H / 2))` computes, and 'equal weight' is exactly what `n++` per cell pair produces). The added observation about polar rows is also correct and I checked it: on an equirect grid every row has W cells, so `n` accumulates identically per row regardless of that row's physical circumference, and because the deviation at :442 is taken about the whole-field mean computed at :434-435, a row whose own mean is offset contributes a non-decaying positive term at every lag rather than a decaying one — which is the mechanism behind the elevated NaN rate (no zero crossing found, so :451-452 returns NaN) that both the adjudicator and my own replication observed. NOT ALREADY_FIXED, same evidence as [0]: the 0744fa4 descriptors.js hunks are only at @@ -305 / -337 / -349.

Where I partially refute: the adjudicator silently RAISED this finding's severity. The banked JSON records `"severity": "medium"` for this title; the adjudicator presented it as 'severity high'. Raising it to match [0] is defensible reasoning but it was not disclosed, and it has a real cost — [0] and [9] are one bug, so carrying two HIGH rows double-counts it in the cluster's severity profile. This should be recorded as a DUPLICATE of [0] and fixed once at descriptors.js:430-447, not as a second independent high-severity defect.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Same independent re-read as [0] (full descriptors.js, full fieldSampler.js, grep -n on planet-lod-lab.html). Additionally extracted the raw banked record for this exact title from review-2026-07-25-adversarial-findings.json and confirmed it carries `"severity": "medium"`, not high. Confirmed `git show --stat 0744fa4` touches descriptors.js/stats.js/instrument-review-fixes.test.js + 3 evidence docs only, and that its descriptors.js hunk headers are @@ -305,7 +305,10 / @@ -337,11 +340,11 / @@ -349,21 +352,62 — none within autocorrWavelengthKm's 428-461 range.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: Banked severity is MEDIUM; the adjudicator reported HIGH without flagging the change. Correct handling: merge into [0] as a duplicate and carry ONE high-severity row for the pair. Independently, [9] should not be counted at high.

findings.title: seedsToResolve under-sizes the ensemble by 2x relative to the module's own two-ensemble comparison rule
bankedResultsAffected: AC-CURVE-live.md:52-60, column 'seeds to resolve 15% at 2σ' — every entry roughly doubles: 1→1, 2→3, 2→4, 4→7, 6→11, 17→34, 103→205

DIAGNOSIS.md:208 'M(2-sigma resolve 15%): cons 10.7 -> >=11 ; full 18.7 -> >=19' → 21.3→>=22 and 37.5→>=38, and the derived recommendation at DIAGNOSIS.md:180-182 'M >= 11-19 seeds/radius' → 'M >= 22-38'
AC-CURVE-live.md prose 'That is why a 15% bar is now measurable where it previously was not' — survives (3 <= the 5 seeds used), but the margin shrinks from 2.5x to 1.7x and should be restated
findings.mechanism: The title asserts that seedsToResolve solves M for `effect >= z * SEM_one_ensemble`, while the module's own two-ensemble decision rule (shiftSignificance) requires `|delta| > z * hypot(sem_a, sem_b)` — and that this makes seedsToResolve exactly 2x too small. That is what the code does. seedsToResolve (stats.js:84) inverts `effect = z * cv / sqrt(M)` giving M = (z·cv/effect)². shiftSignificance (stats.js:243) combines the two ensembles' SEMs in quadrature; for two ensembles of equal size and equal CV that is sqrt(2)·cv/sqrt(M), so clearing the same effect needs M = 2·(z·cv/effect)². The factor is exactly 2, algebraically, not approximately. The two readings differ only in whether the reference is an EXACT known value (no factor) or a SECOND MEASURED ensemble (factor 2). The instrument's documented use is the second: planSweep runs a pilot at one driver value and sizes M for a sweep in which every driver point is its own M-seed ensemble, and DIAGNOSIS.md:181-182 — the very arithmetic the tests pin verbatim — spells the comparison out as "compare the three per-radius means with their SEMs, and check CI overlap". So the under-sizing is inherited from DIAGNOSIS.md and faithfully reproduced, not introduced by stats.js; the defect is that the module contains two incompatible definitions of "resolve" and the planning function ships the looser one. Note requiredSeeds (stats.js:73-76) is NOT affected — "measure the mean to a precision" is genuinely a one-ensemble question. Not related to the carrier-off / LEGACY-synth split: this is pure sample-size algebra. (The CVs fed into it do come from the possibly-wrong field that finding [1] is about, but that is a separate fault upstream of this one, and it moves the inputs, not the formula.)

findings.impact: Every `seedsToResolve` / `seedsToResolveAll` number the instrument has ever emitted is roughly half the seeds actually required to see the stated effect clear a two-ensemble error bar — the exact direction of error (a bar tighter than the instrument can measure) that this whole workstream was commissioned to eliminate after the 2026-07-24 read-gate. Concretely, the banked noise-floor table's last column doubles: form wavelength 2→3, gradient 2→4, form excess ratio 4→7, hypsometric 6→11, RMS relief 17→34, elevation max 103→205 (spectral slope stays 1). DIAGNOSIS.md's published 11/19 become 22/38. Crucially it does NOT invalidate the banked exponents: the AC-CURVE sweep ran M=5, and the descriptors carrying the headline result (form wavelength, CV 8.8%) need 3 under the corrected rule, so M=5 was still sufficient. The measured exponents, their SEMs and the corrected dof=1 significance statements are untouched.
findings.fixSketch: Two separable moves, both inside stats.js only (no generation code, no DI needed — this is a pure planning function). (1) Make the comparison basis explicit rather than implicit: `seedsToResolve(cv, effectFraction, z = DEFAULT_Z, { against = 'ensemble' } = {})`, where `against:'ensemble'` (the new default, matching shiftSignificance and DIAGNOSIS.md's CI-overlap procedure) returns `Math.ceil(2 * Math.pow((z*cv)/effectFraction, 2))` and `against:'exact'` keeps the current formula for the case where the reference carries no uncertainty (e.g. lawVerdict's exact claimed/null pair at stats.js:207-208). (2) Have planSweep (sweep.js:113-114) report both, or at minimum name the basis in the returned plan's `note` (sweep.js:128-130) so a reader knows which question the count answers. Do NOT silently change the number without updating tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:446-453, whose 11/19 assertions are explicitly pinned to DIAGNOSIS.md's text — DIAGNOSIS.md itself would need an erratum, since the fix makes the module disagree with its cited source.

The banked table in AC-CURVE-live.md:52-60 needs its last column re-derived. DIAGNOSIS.md:208 and :180-182 should carry an erratum, since it is the upstream source of the wrong arithmetic and is cited as authoritative. planet-lod-lab.html:6987-7008 (_lab.planSweep) needs no code change. No src/worldengine generation code is touched, so the AC-POSCTRL read-only discipline and the vis-scale fence are both unaffected.
findings.refuterReason:
The verdict survives, but on a narrower footing than the adjudicator laid out, and with one banked-result bullet that is a misreading.

WHAT SURVIVES. The algebra is exact and I redid all of it independently. seedsToResolve (stats.js:82-85) returns ceil(((z*cv)/effectFraction)^2), which inverts effect = z*cv/sqrt(M) — a ONE-ensemble error bar. A two-ensemble difference of equal-size, equal-CV ensembles has SE = hypot(cv/sqrt(M), cv/sqrt(M)) = sqrt(2)*cv/sqrt(M), so clearing the same effect needs M = 2*((z*cv)/effect)^2. Factor exactly 2. I recomputed every entry of the banked table from its own CV and the shipped formula and reproduced the printed column to the digit: 0.013->1, 0.088->2, 0.094->2, 0.137->4, 0.175->6, 0.307->17, 0.759->103. Doubling each pre-ceiling quantity gives 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 34, 205 — every corrected figure the adjudicator quoted is arithmetically right. DIAGNOSIS 0.245 -> 10.671 -> 11 -> doubled 21.34 -> 22; 0.325 -> 18.778 -> 19 -> doubled 37.56 -> 38. Also right.

WHERE THE ADJUDICATOR IS WEAKER THAN IT CLAIMS. (a) The title's 'the module's own two-ensemble comparison rule' is shiftSignificance, and I grepped every .js and .html in the repo: shiftSignificance has NO production caller — the only non-test references are its own definition at stats.js:227 and a comment at stats.js:233. So the 'two incompatible definitions of resolve inside one module' framing is a true statement about the code but is NOT what makes the shipped number wrong; the load-bearing provenance is DIAGNOSIS.md:181-182, which the adjudicator did cite and which I verified verbatim. If the finding rested on shiftSignificance alone it would be a dead-code inconsistency at severity low. It survives at medium only via DIAGNOSIS.

(b) 'The factor is exactly 2, algebraically, not approximately' is over-precise given the provenance it leans on. DIAGNOSIS.md:182 specifies 'compare the three per-radius means with their SEMs, and check CI overlap'. Non-overlapping CIs is a STRICTER rule than |delta| > z*hypot(sem_a, sem_b): it requires |delta| > z*(sem_a + sem_b) = 2*z*sem for equal SEMs, i.e. M = 4x the one-sample figure, not 2x. So under the exact rule DIAGNOSIS names, the under-sizing is 4x; 2x is the loosest defensible correction, not the unique one. Additionally, NEITHER formulation carries a power (beta) term — at M = (z*cv/effect)^2 a true effect of exactly that size clears the bar only ~50% of the time. Under every reading the shipped number is optimistic, and the adjudicator's 'exactly 2' understates the spread of correct answers.

(c) Not downstream of the carrier-off fault — agreed. This is sample-size algebra with no field-sampling path in it.

findings.title: cvIsMeaningful's |mean| > sd cut-off removes the noisiest descriptors from the headline seed count, so planSweep systematically under-sizes the ensemble
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the cut-off strips the noisiest descriptors from the headline. That is exactly what the code does, and the cut-off sits at cv = 1 precisely. Two consequences follow that the code never states. (1) HARD CEILING: every retained descriptor has cv < 1, so `seedsToMeasureAll` can never exceed ceil((1/targetFraction)^2) = 45 at the shipped 0.15 default, and `seedsToResolveAll` can never exceed ceil((2/0.15)^2) = 178 — ceilings independent of how noisy the instrument actually is. (2) CONFLATION: `|mean| > sd` is a statement about the ratio, but the reason string at sweep.js:106-107 reports it as a statement about the mean — 'mean sits within one standard deviation of zero'. Those coincide for a zero-crossing quantity (the elevation.min case the design was built for, AC-CURVE-live.md 'Three instrument bugs' §2) but NOT for a positive-definite quantity that is simply noisy: a strictly-positive descriptor at cv = 1.2 is perfectly well described by requiredSeeds(1.2, 0.15) = 64, yet it is dropped and mislabelled as near-zero. The right test for 'a relative target is undefined here' is |mean| indistinguishable from 0 given the SEM (|mean| <= z*sem), not |mean| <= sd. No linkage to the carrier-off / baked-vs-synth split: planSweep is frame-agnostic arithmetic over whatever descriptors arrive.
findings.evidence: sweep.js:169 — `return Number.isFinite(stats.cv) && Number.isFinite(stats.sd) && Math.abs(stats.mean) > stats.sd;`. Since stats.js:62 defines `cv: mean !== 0 ? sd / Math.abs(mean) : NaN`, the predicate is algebraically identical to `cv < 1`. sweep.js:100 `if (!cvIsMeaningful(s)) {` … sweep.js:110 `continue;` — the failing branch writes NaN seed counts and skips the max entirely. sweep.js:115-116 — `if (Number.isFinite(toMeasure) && toMeasure > worstMeasure) { worstMeasure = toMeasure; worstKey = key; }` runs only for retained descriptors, and sweep.js:122 `seedsToMeasureAll: worstMeasure || NaN,` is that censored max. The exclusion is deliberate and pinned: tests/instrument-sweep.test.js:227 `expect(plan.seedsToMeasureAll).toBeLessThan(10);` with the comment "it must not contaminate the headline figure".
findings.impact: The headline `seedsToMeasureAll` / `seedsToResolveAll` are a maximum over a subset censored at exactly the high-noise tail, and the censoring is silent in magnitude (the excluded KEYS are returned at sweep.js:126, but no seed count is ever computed for them — the reason string promises 'use its absolute spread instead' and the code never does). Live proximity is not hypothetical: the banked AC-CURVE-live noise-floor table's worst row, elevation max, sits at CV 75.9% — 0.759, only 32% below the cut-off. Monte-Carlo on that exact row (200k trials, n=8 as the banked pilot used): the sample cv-hat 95% range is [0.330, 1.724], i.e. it CROSSES the cut-off, and P(|mean_hat| <= sd_hat) = 21.1%. So on a re-run of the same pilot at the same true noise there is a ~1-in-5 chance elevation max is silently dropped, the headline reads 5 (RMS relief) instead of 26 — a 5x under-size — and the dropped descriptor is captioned as if its mean were near zero.
findings.fixSketch: In sweep.js only. Split the one predicate into two. (a) Undefined-relative-target test: |mean| <= z * sem (a real statement about the mean being indistinguishable from zero), which is what should route a descriptor into `descriptorsWithUndefinedRelativeNoise`. (b) Drop the implicit cv < 1 ceiling: a well-separated-from-zero descriptor gets requiredSeeds(cv, target) no matter how large cv is. (c) Honour the reason string: for descriptors failing (a), compute the ABSOLUTE-precision count the string already promises (seeds so sem <= targetFraction * sd, i.e. ceil(1/targetFraction^2)) and return it as `seedsToMeasureAbsolute` instead of bare NaN. (d) Make the coverage explicit: return `descriptorsCoveredByHeadline` alongside the two headline numbers so 'you need N seeds' cannot be read as covering the whole descriptor set. Pure function, no generation code touched (AC-POSCTRL discipline intact). CAUTION: sweep.js lives under src/worldengine/, which tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:64-66 greps with /visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP/ including comments — any new comment must avoid those tokens.

No lab change required (planet-lod-lab.html:7007 just spreads the return).
findings.claimAmbiguity: 'systematically under-sizes the ensemble' has a weak and a strong reading. WEAK (rejected as the whole claim): 'a zero-crossing quantity like elevation.min should have been allowed to demand its 1040 seeds' — that reading is wrong, and AC-CURVE-live.md's own fix note is right that 1040 is division-by-almost-nothing, not an instrument property. STRONG (adjudicated): the predicate's cut-off is placed on the CV rather than on the mean's separation from zero, so it also censors honestly-noisy positive-definite descriptors, caps the headline at 45 seeds by construction, and never supplies the absolute-spread alternative its own reason string promises. The strong reading survives; the weak one does not.
findings.refuterReason: Every citation is exact and the mechanism reproduces. sweep.js:169 literally reads `return Number.isFinite(stats.cv) && Number.isFinite(stats.sd) && Math.abs(stats.mean) > stats.sd;` and with stats.js:62 `cv: mean !== 0 ? sd / Math.abs(mean) : NaN` the predicate is algebraically `cv < 1` (mean=0 gives cv=NaN and fails the first conjunct; sd is never negative). The censoring path is real: sweep.js:100 `if (!cvIsMeaningful(s)) {` -> :109 `unusable.push(key);` -> :110 `continue;`, which skips the max update at :115-116, and :122 `seedsToMeasureAll: worstMeasure || NaN,` publishes that censored max. I redid both ceiling computations from the shipped constants: requiredSeeds(cv->1, 0.15) = ceil(44.44) = 45 and seedsToResolve(cv->1, 0.15, z=2) = ceil(177.78) = 178. Both correct. The CONFLATION half is also right: sweep.js:106-107 captions the drop as 'mean sits within one standard deviation of zero', which is a mean-vs-zero statement being used to report a ratio test — sound for a zero-crossing quantity, wrong for a merely-noisy positive-definite one. I re-ran the Monte Carlo myself (200k trials, normal, true cv 0.759 = the banked elevation-max row, n=8 as the banked pilot actually used): P(|mean_hat| <= sd_hat) = 20.9% (adjudicator said 21.1%) and the cv-hat 95% range is [0.331, 1.731] (adjudicator [0.330, 1.724]) — it does straddle the cut-off. The 5x under-size claim checks: with elevation max dropped the next-worst banked row is RMS relief at 5 seeds against a headline of 26. One thing the adjudicator UNDERSTATED rather than overstated: at the LAB DEFAULT pilot size of n=5 (planet-lod-lab.html:6989) the drop probability rises to 25.0%, i.e. 1-in-4, not 1-in-5. findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: MEDIUM stands. One refinement in the finding's DISFAVOUR that the adjudicator did not surface: the fix it implies (|mean| <= z*sem instead of |mean| <= sd) does not remove the hard ceiling, it only raises it — censoring at |mean| <= 2*sd/sqrt(8) is censoring at cv >= 1.414, giving a ceiling of ceil((1.414/0.15)^2) = 89 rather than 45. The 'ceiling independent of actual instrument noise' criticism therefore survives the proposed fix and the fixSketch needs to say what replaces the ceiling, not just move it. One refinement in the finding's FAVOUR: the failure rate is 25.0% at the shipped default n=5, not the 21.1% quoted for n=8.

findings.title: planSweep's seed counts carry no uncertainty of their own, and the lab's default 5-seed pilot makes them accurate only to about a factor of 2
bankedResultsAffected: docs/WORKSTREAMS/nonvisual-analysis-channel-2026-07-24/evidence/AC-CURVE-live.md — noise-floor table, 'seeds to measure at 15%' column: elevation max 26 must be quoted as ~[5, 133] at 95%; RMS relief 5 as ~[1, 11]. Point estimates stand (median bias is ~-8%, i.e. slightly low); what changes is the claimed precision, and the direction of risk is under-sizing.

docs/WORKSTREAMS/nonvisual-analysis-channel-2026-07-24/evidence/AC-CURVE-live.md — 'seeds to resolve 15% at 2 sigma' column: elevation max 103 carries the same ~0.2x-5x interval (and separately inherits the z=2-vs-t question already corrected elsewhere).

docs/WORKSTREAMS/nonvisual-analysis-channel-2026-07-24/evidence/AC-CURVE-live.md — narrative 'the headline dropped from 1040 to 26': 26 is a point estimate from an 8-seed pilot, not a determined quantity.

NOT affected: the fitted exponents (physical +0.4583, angular -0.5417, on-screen -0.0417, radiusEarth control 1.0000) and the RADIUS-CENSUS substrate/relief row R^0.458 — these ride form wavelength, whose 1-seed requirement is stable at [1, 1] under simulation, so the M=5 sweep was correctly sized.
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the seed counts are quoted without their own sampling error and that a 5-seed pilot leaves them good to ~2x. Both halves check out, and the second is if anything understated once the squaring is included. sd-hat from n samples has relative SE ~ 1/sqrt(2(n-1)) = 35% at n=5 and 29% at n=8; requiredSeeds squares cv, so the count's relative SE is ~71% / ~58%. Direct simulation (200k trials, normal pilot, target 0.15): at the banked elevation-max row (true cv 0.759, n=8 as the banked run used) seedsToMeasure has median 24 against a true 26 and a 95% range of [5, 133]; at n=5 the same row gives [3, 251]. The 'factor of 2' in the title is the factor on cv (cv-hat 95% range at n=5 is roughly 0.6x-2.9x of truth); on the seed count itself it is a factor of ~4-5 each way. This is the identical error class to the CONFIRMED tCritical95 finding — a number quoted at a precision it does not have — but on the planning side rather than the verdict side. Not carrier-off related.
findings.evidence: sweep.js:112-114 — `const toMeasure = requiredSeeds(s.cv, targetFraction);` … `plan[key] = { cv: s.cv, sd: s.sd, mean: s.mean, noiseFloorFraction: s.cv, seedsToMeasure: toMeasure, seedsToResolve: toResolve };` — bare point estimates, no interval on cv and none on either count. sweep.js:118-131: the return carries `pilotN: pilot.length` (:127) but attaches no uncertainty to any number. stats.js:75 `return Math.ceil(Math.pow(cv / targetFraction, 2));` — the count is quadratic in cv, so cv's relative error doubles. Lab default pilot size: planet-lod-lab.html:6989 `const seeds = o.seeds || [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];` (n = 5). This contradicts the module family's own stated contract at stats.js:5 — 'Every number this module returns carries its own uncertainty'.
findings.impact: The pre-flight advice the whole module exists to give ('run M seeds before you set a bar') is delivered as an exact integer whose own 95% interval spans roughly 0.2x-5x. Concretely against banked numbers: AC-CURVE-live.md's noise-floor table quotes 'seeds to measure at 15%' = 26 and 'seeds to resolve 15% at 2 sigma' = 103 for elevation max, and 5 / 17 for RMS relief. Simulated honestly at the pilot size actually used (n=8): elevation max 26 -> [5, 133], RMS relief 5 -> [1, 11]. The point estimates are also median-biased LOW (24 vs 26; the sampling distribution is right-skewed), so the failure direction is under-sizing, which is the read-gate failure mode this module was built to prevent. THE ONE ROW THAT MATTERS IS SAFE: form wavelength at cv 0.088, n=8 gives seedsToMeasure = 1 with a 95% range of [1, 1], so the M=5 choice that produced the banked radius exponents was comfortably above requirement. No banked exponent is at risk.
findings.fixSketch: In sweep.js only. Propagate the chi-square sampling distribution of sd-hat into each count: with dof = n-1, cv_lo = cv * sqrt(dof / chi2_{0.975,dof}) and cv_hi = cv * sqrt(dof / chi2_{0.025,dof}); return `seedsToMeasureRange: [requiredSeeds(cv_lo, t), requiredSeeds(cv_hi, t)]` and the same for resolve, alongside `cvRange`. Add a small chi-square quantile table to stats.js mirroring the existing tCritical95 TABLE at stats.js:39-40 (same house pattern, same file, so the fix is consistent with the shipped tCritical95 remedy). Also worth returning a conservative `seedsRecommended` = the upper-bound count, since under-sizing is the asymmetric harm. Optionally raise the lab default pilot from 5 to 8-12 at planet-lod-lab.html:6989 — but the interval, not the default, is the actual fix; a bigger default without an interval just moves the same silent overclaim.
findings.blastRadius: sweep.js:90-132 (additive fields only — nothing existing changes value), plus a new exported quantile helper in stats.js.
