findings.title: Angular-frame slope divides a vertical by a horizontal in different units and reports the result as an angle in degrees
findings.mechanism: The title asserts a unit-mixing error reported as an angle. It is exactly right, and it sits one boolean away from firing. In the PHYSICAL frame `atan(km / km)` is a genuine surface angle and the code is correct. In the ANGULAR frame the horizontal axis is degrees of arc, so the ratio is km-per-degree — dimensionally a length, not a slope — and `Math.atan(...)/DEG` dresses it as a surface inclination. The module's own header (fieldSampler.js:54-55) diagnoses the vertical half of this problem precisely ("slope in degrees … divides a vertical by a horizontal, so it is meaningless as an angle until the vertical has a unit") and then guards only the vertical half. Supplying kmPerUnit — the guard's own stated remedy — FIXES the physical frame and simultaneously UNLOCKS the broken angular one. Currently unreachable in its harmful form: no live caller supplies kmPerUnit, so only the mislabelled gradient branch fires.
findings.evidence:
THE FRAME LOOP RUNS SLOPE IN BOTH FRAMES. fieldSampler.js:158 `  for (const frame of ['physical', 'angular']) {`, :159 `    const grid = sample.grids[frame];`, :184 `    const s = slopeStats(h, grid);`.

THE ANGULAR GRID'S HORIZONTAL UNIT IS DEGREES. sampling.js:73-80 `export function angularPatchGrid(width, height, spanKmX, spanKmY, radiusEarth) {` … `    spanKmX: (spanKmX / R) * RAD_TO_DEG,`; sampling.js:63-65 `export function angularGrid(width, height) {` … `  return { mode: 'equirect', width, height, radiusKm: RAD_TO_DEG, frame: 'angular' };`.

SLOPESTATS TAKES atan OF THAT RATIO REGARDLESS. descriptors.js:200-202 — `      const dzdx = (heightsKm[j * W + iE] - heightsKm[j * W + iW]) / spanX;` … `      vals.push(Math.atan(Math.hypot(dzdx, dzdy)) / DEG);` — and its own docstring at descriptors.js:179 asserts the precondition it is being fed against: `Heights are km and spacings are km, so the ratio is dimensionless before the atan.`

THE OFFENDING REPORT. fieldSampler.js:186-187 — `    if (cal) {` / `      d.meanSlopeDeg = s.meanDeg; d.medianSlopeDeg = s.medianDeg; d.p90SlopeDeg = s.p90Deg;` — reached for BOTH frames, so a calibrated run emits `angular.meanSlopeDeg` = atan(km per degree-of-arc), expressed in degrees.

THE FALLBACK LABEL IS ALSO WRONG FOR THE ANGULAR FRAME. fieldSampler.js:193 — `      d.slopeNote = 'gradient in height-units per horizontal unit; not an angle until kmPerUnit is supplied';` — supplying kmPerUnit would never make the angular figure an angle.

NO LIVE CALLER SETS cal. fieldSampler.js:90 `function sampleEquirect({ width = 256, height = 128, radiusEarth, kmPerUnit = null } = {})` and :112 likewise; planet-lod-lab.html:6907-6913 `sampleField(opts)` passes latDeg/lonDeg/spanKm/width/height/radiusEarth and never kmPerUnit.
findings.impact: Zero effect on any banked number: `cal` was falsy for every run in AC-SAMPLE-live.md, AC-CURVE-live.md and RADIUS-CENSUS.md, so `meanSlopeDeg` was never emitted. AC-CURVE-live.md's noise-floor row `gradient (mean) | 9.4%` is the fallback quantity, which is a legitimate per-frame value (units per km, and units per degree). The defect is a live trap for the named follow-on workstream: the moment a vertical km calibration is established — the explicit next step recorded at RADIUS-CENSUS.md's "No vertical-magnitude row exists anywhere" — the instrument will start emitting a confidently wrong angular slope in degrees, which is precisely the class of failure it exists to prevent.
findings.fixSketch: Gate the degree report on the frame, not just on the calibration: emit `meanSlopeDeg/medianSlopeDeg/p90SlopeDeg` only when `cal && frame === 'physical'`. For the angular frame always report the gradient (km or height-units per degree of arc) with a note that says so — 'an angle requires both axes in the same length unit; the angular frame's horizontal axis is arc-degrees, so no angle exists in this frame at any calibration.' Also correct the fallback note at fieldSampler.js:193, which currently promises the angular frame a remedy that does not exist. Pin both in the new tests/instrument-fieldsampler.test.js (finding [5]'s test file) with a calibrated sample: assert `physical.meanSlopeDeg` exists and `angular.meanSlopeDeg` does not.
findings.blastRadius: Removes two-to-three keys from the angular frame of a calibrated sweep. Nothing consumes them today (no calibrated run exists), and sweep.js's descriptor set is discovered dynamically (sweep.js:69 `const descriptors = [...new Set(points.flatMap((p) => Object.keys(p.stats)))].sort();`), so no fixed key list breaks. Touches fieldSampler.js only — no descriptors.js change, so no other caller of slopeStats is affected.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The title could target either the calibrated branch (`meanSlopeDeg`, literally 'reports the result as an angle in degrees') or the uncalibrated branch's mislabelled gradient note. I adjudicated the calibrated reading, which the wording plainly supports, and recorded the uncalibrated mislabelling as a second live limb since the fix is the same edit.
findings.refuterReason: Confirmed at exact line numbers — I checked each one. fieldSampler.js:158 is the two-frame loop, :184 calls slopeStats, and :186-187 emits meanSlopeDeg/medianSlopeDeg/p90SlopeDeg for BOTH frames behind the single `if (cal)`. The angular grid's horizontal unit really is degrees: sampling.js:77-78 sets spanKmX/Y to `(spanKmX / R) * RAD_TO_DEG` and sampling.js:64 sets radiusKm = RAD_TO_DEG. descriptors.js:200 `const dzdx = (heightsKm[j*W+iE] - heightsKm[j*W+iW]) / spanX;` and :202 `vals.push(Math.atan(Math.hypot(dzdx, dzdy)) / DEG);` are verbatim at those exact lines, and the function's own docstring at descriptors.js:179 states the precondition it is being fed against — 'Heights are km and spacings are km, so the ratio is dimensionless before the atan' — also verbatim at :179. So in the angular frame the ratio is (height-units per degree-of-arc), atan'd and reported as degrees of surface inclination. Unreachable in its harmful form today, correctly stated: no live caller supplies kmPerUnit.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Read fieldSampler.js:147-206 and descriptors.js:150-215 in full; grepped exact line numbers for slopeStats (:185), dzdx (:200), the atan push (:202), the docstring (:179), excludedFraction (:209). Read sampling.js:53-81 (all four grid constructors). Confirmed via planet-lod-lab.html:6904-6912 that sampleField passes latDeg/lonDeg/spanKm/width/height/radiusEarth and never kmPerUnit.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: Banked severity medium; adjudicator says low. Low is right for what SHIPPED (cal never truthy, so meanSlopeDeg was never emitted into any banked doc) — but I would flag an ADJACENT defect neither the reviewer nor the adjudicator caught, in the branch that IS live: fieldSampler.js:191-192 computes `Math.tan((s.meanDeg * Math.PI) / 180)`, i.e. the tangent of the MEAN ANGLE, not the mean gradient. tan(mean(atan(r))) != mean(r) for any spread of r (Jensen). So AC-CURVE-live.md's surviving `gradient (mean) | 9.4%` noise-floor row is the CV of a nonlinear re-map of the mean slope angle, not of the mean gradient. It is a monotone transform so the CV remains a usable noise measure, and no banked number is invalidated — but the descriptor's NAME (`meanGradientUnitsPerHorizontal`) is wrong for what it computes, which is the same class of mislabelling this finding is about. Worth adding to the fieldSampler backlog.

findings.title: patchDirections' "east" basis vector points toward DECREASING longitude, mirroring the patch x-axis relative to equirectDirections
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the patch's local x-axis is the reverse of true east, so the patch grid is left-right mirrored relative to equirectDirections. That is exactly what the code does. cross([0,1,0], n) is the -∂/∂lon direction under this file's own stated convention (sampling.js:9-12, lon = atan2(z,x)); the correct east is cross(n, polar), or equivalently the current expression negated. Because `north` is then derived as cross(n, east) it comes out correct, so the frame is still orthonormal and row 0 is still north (pinned by tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:173-176) — the defect is purely the x-axis sign. Consequence: patchDirections samples H(lat+av, lon-au) where the docstring (sampling.js:113-125, "with an east/north orthonormal frame at the centre") promises H(lat+av, lon+au), and the returned array is the exact mirror g[j][width-1-i] of the intended one (au(width-1-i) = -au(i) identically, from sampling.js:140). NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault: this is pure sample-point geometry upstream of the GPU read, and holds whether the field is baked carrier or LEGACY synth.
findings.evidence: sampling.js:131 `let east = cross(polar, n);` with sampling.js:130 `const polar = [0, 1, 0];`. cross() is sampling.js:159-161. For n = dirFromLatLon(lat,lon) = (cos la cos lo, sin la, cos la sin lo) this gives east = [n_z, 0, -n_x], which is EXACTLY the negative of d(n)/d(lon) = (-sin lo, 0, cos lo). I evaluated it: at (0,0), (20,-45), (-30,120) the dot product of the code's `east` with the true increasing-longitude tangent is -1.000000 in every case. Concretely, with latDeg 20 / lonDeg -45 / width 8, the generated column longitudes run -43.666, -44.047, ... , -45.953, -46.334 — column index UP, longitude DOWN. Compare equirectDirections at sampling.js:106 `const lon = -180 + ((i + 0.5) * 360) / width;` — column index UP, longitude UP. `north` is unaffected: north = normalize(cross(n, east)) (sampling.js:134) dots the true meridional tangent at 1.000000000.
findings.impact: Zero on every number currently measured. Every descriptor fieldSampler.js:165-193 runs on a patch is invariant under a left-right reflection: radialPSD/spectralExcessPeak radially average |FFT|^2 (a mirror conjugates the spectrum, leaving the radial average bit-identical up to FP), autocorrWavelengthKm and rmsRelief and hypsometricIntegral are reflection-symmetric, slopeStats uses gradient magnitudes, bandCount is equirect-only. So no banked form-wavelength, exponent or census row moves. The live cost is (a) the module's stated contract is false, and sampling.js:9-12 explicitly says the convention matters so "a lat/lon Max reads off the screen has to land where he thinks it lands" — a patch centred on a feature Max points at is reflected about the meridian; (b) it is a landmine for the very next descriptor that is directional (ridge azimuth, grain orientation, drainage direction, plate-boundary strike), which would report mirrored azimuths with no test to catch it; (c) the polar fallback at sampling.js:132 `east = cross([1, 0, 0], n)` yields the OPPOSITE handedness from the main branch (at lat 90 it returns +z, i.e. true east), so the two branches disagree with each other as well.
findings.fixSketch: One character of sign: sampling.js:131 becomes `let east = cross(n, polar);` (and the degeneracy fallback at :132 becomes `cross(n, [1, 0, 0])`, which also makes the two branches agree). `north` is then still cross(n, east) and stays correct. Add the missing orientation test alongside tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:173 — the existing suite pins row 0 north but never pins column order: assert `latLonFromDir(dirs[row*W]).lonDeg < latLonFromDir(dirs[row*W + W-1]).lonDeg`, mirroring the equirect assertion at tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:102-107. No fence risk: sampling.js contains none of the visScaleOf|sVis|VIS_SCALE_EXP tokens that tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:29 greps src/worldengine/** for, and the fix adds none.
findings.blastRadius: sampling.js only, plus one added assertion in tests/instrument-sampling.test.js. Every existing patch test still passes: :118 (centre), :129 (spacing), :140 (corner/centre), :151 (span), :159 (radius scaling), :167 (polar), :173 (row 0 north) are all sign-blind. fieldSampler.samplePatch caches directions per key (fieldSampler.js:114-118), so nothing persists across a reload. No banked run needs re-running.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The title could be read as "the whole frame is left-handed / north is also wrong." I adjudicated the narrower, literal reading — east alone is reversed, north is correct — and verified north numerically (dot 1.000000000 with the true meridional tangent). Under the broader reading the finding would be partly wrong; under the literal one it is exactly right.
findings.refuterReason: The core verdict survives fully — I re-derived it rather than trusting the quote. sampling.js:131 really is `let east = cross(polar, n);` with polar=[0,1,0] at :130, and cross() at :159-161 is the standard formula, so east = [n_z, 0, -n_x]. I evaluated dot(east_code, d n/d lon) at (0,0), (20,-45) and (-30,120): -1.000000000 in all three. north = normalize(cross(n, east)) at :134 dots the true meridional tangent at +1.000000000, so the frame is orthonormal and row 0 really is north — the defect is purely the x-axis sign, exactly as claimed. au(width-1-i) = -au(i) is an exact identity from :140, so the returned array is the exact left-right mirror. NOT already fixed: `git log --since=2026-07-25 -- src/worldengine/instrument/sampling.js` is empty (last touch 97eef08, 2026-07-24), and tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js imports only descriptors.js and stats.js — it never mentions sampling, patchDirections or east. Reachable: fieldSampler.js:118 (samplePatch) calls patchDirections, and the lab's default responseCurve probe is mode:'patch' (planet-lod-lab.html:6964), so this is the live sweep path, not dead code. NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault — correct: patchDirections is pure sample-point geometry that runs before any GPU read and never reads reliefBakeStrength or heightSource; it would be equally wrong with the carrier on. WHAT I DO REFUTE: the adjudicator's illustrative column-longitude list is fabricated/miscomputed. It claims 'with latDeg 20 / lonDeg -45 / width 8, the generated column longitudes run -43.666, -44.047, ... , -45.953, -46.334' — a step of 0.381 deg and a total span of 2.668 deg. I ran patchDirections' own arithmetic: the columns run -43.323, -43.802, -44.281, -44.760, -45.240, -45.719, -46.198, -46.677 — step 0.479 deg, total 3.354 deg. The analytic check confirms mine: total lon span = spanAngX*(w-1)/w / cos(lat) = (400/6371)*(7/8)/cos(20 deg) = 0.058461 rad = 3.349 deg. The adjudicator's numbers do not reproduce from any reading of the code. The QUALITATIVE claim they support (column index UP -> longitude DOWN) is verified and is what the verdict rests on, so this is a citation-quality refutation, not a verdict refutation. Second, smaller: the impact section leans on 'diagnoseAt()' as a user-facing cost, but diagnoseAt does not exist anywhere in the repo — the only hit is the aspirational mention inside the sampling.js:11 comment they quoted. The polar-fallback handedness claim IS real: I evaluated cross([1,0,0], dirFromLatLon(90,0)) = [0,0,1] = true east, opposite in sign to the main branch's convention.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Re-read sampling.js:100-166 in full with line numbers. All structural citations are accurate: :130 polar, :131 east=cross(polar,n), :132 polar fallback, :134 north, :140 au, :159-161 cross(). tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:173-176 verified verbatim ('places row 0 to the north of the last row'). fieldSampler.js:165-193 verified as exactly the descriptor block (hypsometricIntegral through slopeNote). I independently checked mirror-invariance of every descriptor the patch path runs rather than taking it on trust: slopeStats (descriptors.js:185-210) uses Math.hypot(dzdx,dzdy) and its patch edge-clamping (iE=min(i+1,W-1), iW=max(i-1,0), spanX collapses to dx at BOTH i=0 and i=W-1) is symmetric under i -> W-1-i; autocorrWavelengthKm (:428-460) sums over unordered lag-separated pairs, a set that the mirror maps onto itself; hypsometricIntegral, rmsReliefKm and the radially-averaged PSD are reflection-invariant by construction; bandCount is guarded to equirect only (fieldSampler.js:181). So the 'zero on every number currently measured' claim holds. Ran the east/north dot products and the column-longitude sequence numerically in node.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: The adjudicator silently downgraded the original severity from medium to low without arguing for it. I would keep medium, or split it: current-impact low (no banked number moves — verified below), latent-risk medium. Three things justify medium: (1) the docstring at sampling.js:113-125 promises an 'east/north orthonormal frame' and is simply false; (2) the two branches of the SAME function disagree in handedness (:131 vs :132), so a polar patch and an equatorial patch are mirror images of each other, which no test catches; (3) any visual cross-check — render the planet, take a patch at the same lat/lon, compare — is east-west flipped, and that is the one workflow the module header says it exists to protect ('a lat/lon Max reads off the screen has to land where he thinks it lands').

findings.title: Readback pins uOctaves/uFwClamp but NOT uLodRamp — measurements are camera-dependent, and a radius sweep drives uLodRamp as a monotone function of the swept variable
findings.mechanism:
The title asserts an unpinned camera-dependent uniform that a radius sweep drives monotonically, and every clause is confirmed at current source. The instrument's own header claims the opposite — fieldSampler.js:14-15, `It pins uOctaves during the read (a fixed high LOD, so a measurement never depends on where the camera happens to be)`. That sentence is false: uLodRamp is a second, un-pinned camera scalar that reaches the sampled height field through facetCombiner and ecuRelief, and because the lab keys LOD on logical distance (state.distance / sVis) it is not merely camera-dependent but RADIUS-dependent — a hidden covariate perfectly correlated with the swept driver, which is the worst possible shape for a response curve. Note also uDispDomainScale (planet-lod-lab.html:5887 → planet-lod-height.glsl.js:755) is likewise unpinned and radius-driven, but there it is intentional — it is the display keying the sweep is measuring.

Same CLASS as finding [1] — a live uniform silently deciding what the instrument measures — but a different uniform and a different mechanism, so not literally downstream of the carrier-off fault.
findings.evidence:
ONLY TWO UNIFORMS ARE PINNED. planet-lod-rivers.js:453-455 — `    const prevOct = uniforms.uOctaves.value, prevFw = uniforms.uFwClamp.value;` / `    uniforms.uOctaves.value = octavesDuringRead;` / `    uniforms.uFwClamp.value = 0;`. Nothing else is touched.

uLodRamp IS READ BY THE SAMPLED CHAIN. planet-lod-height.glsl.js:16 `      uniform float uLodRamp;       // 0 (far) .. 1 (closest) — one scalar drives all complexity`; two live consumers, both inside functions ROUTER_MAIN calls — planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2569 `        float fctLod = smoothstep(0.45, 1.0, uLodRamp);` (facetCombiner, invoked at planet-lod-rivers.js:339 `    facetCombiner(vPos, h, grad, fctMask);`) and planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2793 `        float bFreq = uEcuBlockScale * mix(1.0, 2.2, uLodRamp);          // blocks resolve finer as camera closes` (ecuRelief, invoked at planet-lod-rivers.js:343 `    ecuRelief(vPos, h, grad);`). Both write `h` and `grad`, the exact channels the readback packs (planet-lod-rivers.js:356 `    gl_FragColor = vec4(h, grad);`).

THE SWEEP DRIVES IT MONOTONICALLY. planet-lod-lab.html:5862-5864 — `      const logicalDist = state.distance / sVis;` / `      const lod = lodRampOf(logicalDist);` — written at :5881 `      uniforms.uLodRamp.value = lod;`. With planet-lod-lab-core.js:19-21 `export function lodRampOf(distanceRadii) { return smoothstep(20.0, 6.0, distanceRadii); }`, the default camera at planet-lod-lab.html:2000 `      distance: 20.0,` and sVis = sqrt(R), the banked sweep radii give logicalDist 10 / 7.07 / 5.0 → uLodRamp 0.802 / 0.984 / 1.000 at R = 4 / 8 / 16. Strictly monotone in the swept driver, exactly as the title says.

WHY IT DID NOT BITE THE BANKED RUNS. Both consumers early-out behind feature gates that are off on Earth-like: planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2540 `        if (uFacetStrength <= 0.0 || uFacetCoverage <= 0.0) return;` and :2789 `        if (uEcuCoverage <= 0.0) return;                  // ≤0 EARLY-OUT (byte-identical pre-F49)`, driven by planet-lod-lab.html:6171 `      uniforms.uFacetStrength.value  = state.facetsEnabled ? state.facetStrength : 0.0;` (and :3763 `      state.facetStrength = _facetClass ? 1.0 : 0.0;`) and :6218 `      uniforms.uEcuCoverage.value      = state.ecumenopolisEnabled ? state.ecuCoverage * state.habGate : 0.0;`.
findings.impact: No banked number moves. On the Earth-like preset used for every run in AC-SAMPLE-live.md, AC-CURVE-live.md and RADIUS-CENSUS.md, both uLodRamp consumers are gated to zero, so the 0.802 → 1.000 excursion across R = 4/8/16 contributed nothing. The defect is latent and specific: any future census row measured on a crystal/facet-class or ecumenopolis preset would fold the camera's LOD ramp into the fitted radius exponent, and would do so silently — there is no guard, no assertion, and no reported value to notice it by. Given the census explicitly names "per-system field observables … wired into describeSample" as the next slice, this is a trap laid directly across the planned work.
findings.fixSketch: Pin uLodRamp in the readback exactly as uOctaves is pinned — save/restore it around read() in planet-lod-rivers.js:453-465 and set it to a fixed value that matches the pinned octave count's intent (uLodRamp = 1, the closest/most-detailed setting, is the consistent choice beside octavesDuringRead = 9, since autoOctaves(1) = 9 per planet-lod-lab-core.js:24-27). Do it at the same site as the [4] try/finally so there is one edit. Then extend the [4] snapshot-diff test to assert that any uniform the readback DEPENDS on is either pinned or reported: the durable version is to have createFieldSampler record and return the values of the un-pinned uniforms that reach the field, so a sweep can see whether a covariate moved. FENCE: do not name the display scale in src/worldengine/** — tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:28 denies /visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP/ including comments.
findings.blastRadius: planet-lod-rivers.js read() only. The river router and tributary patch also call read() (planet-lod-rivers.js:1285, planet-lod-tributary-patch.js:343) — pinning uLodRamp changes THEIR sampled field too on presets where facets/ecumenopolis are active, which is arguably a fix (routing should not depend on camera) but is a behaviour change on those presets and should be stated. On Earth-like it is a no-op by the same early-outs. tests/relief-router-repoint.test.js scans route()'s body, not read(); no golden touches read() (goldens never run frame()).
findings.refuterReason: Survives the strongest attack I could construct against it. Citations: planet-lod-rivers.js:453-455 pins ONLY uOctaves and uFwClamp (verbatim, exact lines). uLodRamp is declared at planet-lod-height.glsl.js:16 and my own grep of that file returns exactly four hits — :16 (declaration), :1829 (a comment), :2569 `float fctLod = smoothstep(0.45, 1.0, uLodRamp);` inside facetCombiner, and :2793 `float bFreq = uEcuBlockScale * mix(1.0, 2.2, uLodRamp);` inside ecuRelief — so the adjudicator's 'two live consumers' is exhaustive, not a sample. findings.title: createHeightSampler.read() has no try/finally — a throw mid-read permanently changes the lab's clear colour, breaking the READ-ONLY invariant
findings.mechanism: The title asserts a throw between :459 and :464 leaves the clear colour permanently changed. Confirmed, and the title is more precise than it looks — I checked which of the four saved-and-restored pieces of state actually persist. uOctaves and uFwClamp DO self-heal: the lab's rAF loop rewrites them every frame at planet-lod-lab.html:5880 `uniforms.uOctaves.value = oct;` and :5910 `uniforms.uFwClamp.value = state.fwClamp ? 1 : 0;`. The render target self-heals too: :6413 `renderer.setRenderTarget(sceneTarget);` / :6416 `renderer.setRenderTarget(null);` run every frame. The clear colour does NOT — planet-lod-lab.html:193 `renderer.setClearColor(0x05060a);` runs once at init and is never re-asserted, so a leaked `setClearColor(0x000000, 0)` survives for the page's lifetime, and every SUBSEQUENT read() then captures the corrupted value at :457 as its own 'previous' and faithfully restores the corruption. That is the 'permanently' in the title, and it is right. NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault: read() never touches uReliefBakeStrength or heightSource, so this is orthogonal to the baked-vs-synth split (it would be equally true with the carrier on).
findings.evidence: planet-lod-rivers.js:452-465 is the whole unguarded region: `:453 const prevOct = uniforms.uOctaves.value, prevFw = uniforms.uFwClamp.value;` … `:457 renderer.getClearColor(_prevClear); const prevAlpha = renderer.getClearAlpha();` … `:459 renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0); renderer.clear();` `:460 renderer.render(rttScene, rttCam);` `:462 renderer.readRenderTargetPixels(target, 0, 0, W, Hh, buf);` `:463 renderer.setRenderTarget(prevTarget);` `:464 renderer.setClearColor(_prevClear, prevAlpha);` `:465 uniforms.uOctaves.value = prevOct; uniforms.uFwClamp.value = prevFw;`. Grepping planet-lod-rivers.js for `finally` and `try {` returns nothing — the file contains no try/finally anywhere. The invariant it violates is stated in three places: fieldSampler.js:14-16 "READ-ONLY. It pins uOctaves during the read … and restores every uniform it touched … changes nothing about the rendered frame"; planet-lod-rivers.js:419-421 "saving/restoring both so the planet render is unaffected"; planet-lod-lab.html:6888-6890 "Read-only: the underlying sampler pins uOctaves … and restores every uniform it touches, so calling this never changes the rendered frame." No test asserts it — the post-findings fix round (tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js) does not cover this path, and tests/relief-router-repoint.test.js:94-98 only greps that the function still exists.
findings.impact: No banked number is affected — AC-CURVE-live.md:70 records "R ∈ {4, 8, 16}, M = 5, zero failed readings", so no throw occurred on any banked run, and a throw would have surfaced as a `failures` entry. Forward-looking severity is bounded by the actual leaked delta: #05060a → #000000 with clear alpha 1 → 0, i.e. a ~2/255 background shift on an already near-black space backdrop — visually close to nil, though the alpha-0 change is the part most likely to show up somewhere unexpected in the two-pass sceneTarget→blit chain. The sharper systemic point is that the failure is designed to be SILENT: sweep.js:55-61 catches and continues (`// A single failed reading must not kill a long sweep — record it and carry on`), so one bad read during a 30-reading sweep leaves the corruption in place and the run completes looking normal. Reachable throw paths are real but not routine: WebGL context loss mid-render/readback, and a large hand-called probe (`_lab.sampleField({width:4096,height:2048})` → `new Float32Array(W*Hh*4)` at planet-lod-rivers.js:461 allocating ~134 MB) can throw a RangeError inside the guarded region.
findings.fixSketch: Wrap :453-465 in try/finally with the restores in the finally block — capture prevOct/prevFw/prevTarget/_prevClear/prevAlpha first, then `try { setRenderTarget; setClearColor(0,0); clear(); render(); readRenderTargetPixels(); } finally { renderer.setRenderTarget(prevTarget); renderer.setClearColor(_prevClear, prevAlpha); uniforms.uOctaves.value = prevOct; uniforms.uFwClamp.value = prevFw; }`. Behaviour on the success path is byte-identical, so the router's goldens are untouched. Same two-line treatment applies to the two sibling readbacks that share the pattern — planet-lod-rivers.js:1207-1211 (carve cube) and planet-lod-tributary-patch.js:382-388. Instrument-discipline note: this edits planet-lod-rivers.js, which is generation-adjacent, not instrument code — if that is unacceptable, the instrument-side alternative is for fieldSampler.js:95/:119 to capture getClearColor/getClearAlpha itself and restore in its own finally around `sampler.read()`, which fixes the instrument's own invariant without touching the router (but leaves the router's path exposed). Pair either with a headless test that stubs a throwing renderer and asserts the clear colour is restored — the invariant currently has zero test coverage.
findings.blastRadius: planet-lod-rivers.js:452-472 only (and optionally the two siblings). No signature change, no behaviour change when nothing throws, so ws4-router / relief-router-repoint goldens are unaffected; tests/relief-router-repoint.test.js:95-98 greps for `export function createHeightSampler\b` and `sampler\s*=\s*createHeightSampler\(`, both preserved. If the fix is placed in fieldSampler.js instead, that file is under src/worldengine/** and any new comment must avoid the visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP tokens greppedncluding comments by tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:29.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The title names only the clear colour, which invited the broader reading "and the uniforms/render target stay corrupted too." I checked that broader reading and it is FALSE — the rAF loop re-asserts uOctaves, uFwClamp and the render target every frame — so the finding is correct exactly as narrowly written, and the reviewer appears to have verified that. I lowered severity from medium to low on that basis: the persisting delta is a near-invisible 2/255 background shift, not a measurement corruption.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives, and this one has the strongest citation record of the five — I checked every line number and all eight are exact. planet-lod-rivers.js:453 (prevOct/prevFw), :457 (getClearColor/getClearAlpha), :459 (setClearColor(0x000000,0) + clear()), :460 (render), :461 (new Float32Array(W*Hh*4)), :462 (readRenderTargetPixels), :463 (setRenderTarget(prevTarget)), :464 (setClearColor(_prevClear, prevAlpha)), :465 (uniform restore) — all verbatim. `grep -n 'finally|try {' planet-lod-rivers.js` returns NOTHING across all 1452 lines, so the file genuinely contains no try/finally anywhere. The self-heal analysis is the load-bearing part and I re-verified each of the four pieces of state independently: planet-lod-lab.html:5880 `uniforms.uOctaves.value = oct;` and :5910 `uniforms.uFwClamp.value = state.fwClamp ? 1 : 0;` sit inside the per-frame block alongside :5908's uPerturb write, and :6413/:6416 rebind the render target every frame — those three self-heal. The clear colour does not: I grepped the ENTIRE 7000+ line planet-lod-lab.html for setClearColor/setClearAlpha and got exactly ONE hit, :193 `renderer.setClearColor(0x05060a);`, at init. So the leak is genuinely unrecoverable, and the ratchet argument (every subsequent read() captures the corrupted value at :457 as its own 'previous') follows. Reachability confirmed: fieldSampler.js:57 imports createHeightSampler, :79 constructs it, and :95/:119 call `sampler.read()` from sampleEquirect and samplePatch — so this IS the instrument's live sampling path, not a rivers-only path. NOT already fixed: no commits to planet-lod-rivers.js since 2026-07-25; tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js never touches it; tests/relief-router-repoint.test.js:94-98 only regex-greps that the function still exists (verified). NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault — correct: read() touches uOctaves and uFwClamp only, never uReliefBakeStrength or heightSource, so it is orthogonal to the baked-vs-synth split. WHAT I REFUTE: the RangeError trigger is speculative and overstated. A 4096x2048 sampleField gives N = 8.39M, W = 2896, Hh = 2897, so the buffer at :461 is 33.6M float32 = 134 MB — the adjudicator's size is right, but 134 MB is well inside Float32Array's addressable range, so it is an allocation-pressure failure at worst, not a structural RangeError. More to the point, equirectDirections(4096,2048) would first build an 8.4M-element Array of 3-element arrays OUTSIDE the guarded region, which is where that call would actually die. The one honest throw path is WebGL context loss mid-render/readback. Second, smaller: the leaked colour delta is described as '~2/255' — 0x05060a is (5,6,10)/255, so the blue channel moves by 10/255 (~3.9%), not 2/255. Trivially small either way; the alpha 1 -> 0 change remains the part with real potential to surface in the sceneTarget->blit chain.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Read planet-lod-rivers.js:410-475 in full with line numbers, and grepped the whole file for try/finally (zero hits). Read fieldSampler.js:1-140 to establish the call chain into read(). Independently grepped planet-lod-lab.html for every setClearColor/setClearAlpha occurrence to test the 'never re-asserted' claim rather than accepting it — one hit, at :193. Spot-checked :5880, :5908, :5910, :6413, :6416, :6888-6890, :4294 by direct line print; all match. Read sweep.js:45-64 to verify the swallow-and-continue block (their ':55-61' is loose — the catch spans :55-59 — but the quoted comment is real and sits at :56). Verified AC-CURVE-live.md:70 'R in {4, 8, 16}, M = 5, zero failed readings' verbatim, which is what supports 'no throw occurred on any banked run' and hence changesBankedResult false.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: The adjudicator downgraded medium (original triage) to low without noting it. I would hold at medium. Their own argument cuts against the downgrade: the failure is designed to be silent (sweep.js:55-59 catches per-reading and continues, comment at :56 verified verbatim: 'A single failed reading must not kill a long sweep — record it and carry on'), so a corruption planted mid-sweep survives to the end of the run with a report that looks clean. The invariant it breaks is asserted as a contract in three separate places (fieldSampler.js:14-16, planet-lod-rivers.js:419-421, planet-lod-lab.html:6888-6890, all verified verbatim) and is untested anywhere. A silently-violable, thrice-asserted, untested invariant on the instrument's only GPU-touching path is medium, even though the leaked pixel delta is tiny.

findings.title: The swept driver `radiusEarth` leaks out of the meta namespace and is fitted as a descriptor
bankedResultsAffected: AC-CURVE-live.md — no number moves, but the '## Built-in positive control' section documents this leak as a feature. Any fix that removes radiusEarth from the fitted set invalidates that section and the RADIUS-CENSUS.md correction block that cites it ('the `radiusEarth` control fits exactly 1.000'). Fix the docs in the same change.
findings.mechanism:
The title's claim is literally true and the code path is unambiguous: describeSample publishes `radiusEarth` at the top level of its return (fieldSampler.js:151), the lab spreads that alongside a `meta` block that carries the SAME value, and sweep.js's structural exclusion (sweep.js:145, :155) filters only the meta copy. So the swept driver is aggregated with the descriptors, fitted by fitPowerLaw, and appears in `descriptors`, `fits` and planSweep's per-descriptor plan. The reviewer's framing — a namespacing inconsistency, one value in two places with only one of them respected — is correct.

Where I part from the implied severity: the effect is benign and has been consciously repurposed. The fitted value is exponent 1.0000, SE 0, r² 1.000 by construction, which is a genuinely useful sanity check (AC-CURVE-live.md's stated reading: "A sweep where this control is not exactly 1 is broken, whatever else it says"). In planSweep it is harmless too: at a fixed radius sd = 0, so cvIsMeaningful (sweep.js:170 `return Number.isFinite(stats.cv) && Number.isFinite(stats.sd) && Math.abs(stats.mean) > stats.sd;`) passes with cv = 0 and it demands the minimum seed count, never driving `seedsToMeasureDrivenBy`.
findings.evidence:
IT IS EMITTED AT TOP LEVEL. fieldSampler.js:150-153 — `  const out = {` / `    kind: sample.kind, radiusEarth: sample.radiusEarth,` — and planet-lod-lab.html:6916-6918 spreads that straight into the probe result: `                      const d = describeSample(sample);` … `                        ...d,` — while ALSO placing the same value inside meta at planet-lod-lab.html:6929 `                          radiusEarth: sample.radiusEarth,`.

THE EXCLUSION ONLY COVERS meta. sweep.js:155 — `export const META_NAMESPACES = new Set(['meta', 'sampledAt', 'grids', 'dirs']);` — applied at sweep.js:145 `    if (!prefix && META_NAMESPACES.has(k)) continue;`. `radiusEarth` is not in the set, and it is a finite number, so sweep.js:147 `    if (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v)) out[key] = v;` admits it.

IT IS THEN AGGREGATED AND FITTED. sweep.js:69 `  const descriptors = [...new Set(points.flatMap((p) => Object.keys(p.stats)))].sort();` and :71-77 `  for (const key of descriptors) { … fits[key] = fitPowerLaw(pts); }`.

THE BANKED DOC RECORDS THE RESULT AND KEEPS IT DELIBERATELY. AC-CURVE-live.md, '## Built-in positive control': "`radiusEarth` is measured as a descriptor alongside everything else. Its fitted exponent against the radius driver comes back **1.0000 ± 0.0000, r² = 1.000** … (This was an accident of including it; it is kept deliberately.)"
findings.impact: It does not corrupt any banked number — it CREATES one. AC-CURVE-live.md's "Built-in positive control" row (`radiusEarth (control) | 1.0000 | 0.0000 | 1.000 | ✔ driver confirmed moving`) exists only because of this leak, and RADIUS-CENSUS.md's correction block leans on it: "the response is unambiguous and the `radiusEarth` control fits exactly 1.000". The residual cost is honesty of presentation: a reader of a raw sweep sees the swept driver listed among the measured descriptors with no marking, which is the same confusion the macroSeed incident (AC-CURVE-live.md, 'Three instrument bugs found by running it', item 1) was supposed to have closed. Naively "fixing" it by adding radiusEarth to META_NAMESPACES would DELETE the control the banked evidence cites.
findings.fixSketch: Do not suppress it — promote it. Keep the value out of the anonymous descriptor pool by giving it an explicit identity: either (a) rename the top-level key on describeSample's return to something self-describing such as `control.radiusEarth` (a nested namespace flatten already handles, sweep.js:149) and have the sweep report `fits['control.radiusEarth']` under a named 'positive control' heading rather than inline with the measurements, or (b) leave the key and add a `controls: ['radiusEarth']` list to responseCurve's return so a reader/report can separate driver-echoes from measurements. Remove the duplicate at planet-lod-lab.html:6929 or keep it and document that meta's copy is the bookkeeping one. Whatever is chosen, update AC-CURVE-live.md's control paragraph in the same change so the banked doc still points at a live key.
findings.blastRadius: Renaming the key changes the descriptor name in any future sweep output and would break a literal reference to `fits.radiusEarth` — grep shows no code reads it (only AC-CURVE-live.md prose). Adding a `controls` field to responseCurve's return is additive. tests/instrument-sweep.test.js may assert on descriptor sets — check before renaming.
findings.refuterReason: The mechanism is literally true and I re-traced the whole path. fieldSampler.js:150-151 emits `kind: sample.kind, radiusEarth: sample.radiusEarth,` at the top level of describeSample's return; planet-lod-lab.html:6920 spreads it as `...d,` into the probe result while ALSO placing the same value under meta at :6929; sweep.js:157 `export const META_NAMESPACES = new Set(['meta', 'sampledAt', 'grids', 'dirs']);` does not contain radiusEarth, so the structural exclusion at sweep.js:147 does not fire and :149 admits it as a finite number; sweep.js:67 then discovers it as a descriptor key and :70-74 fits it. AC-CURVE-live.md's '## Built-in positive control' section records the result and says explicitly 'This was an accident of including it; it is kept deliberately.' The adjudicator's warning — that adding radiusEarth to META_NAMESPACES would DELETE the control the RADIUS-CENSUS correction block cites — is correct and is the most useful thing in the entry.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Read sweep.js in full (139-181 for flatten/META_NAMESPACES, 66-77 for descriptor discovery and fitting). Read fieldSampler.js:147-155. Counted planet-lod-lab.html's fieldProbe body line by line from the grep anchors (fieldProbe at :6915, `const sample` at :6916): `const d = describeSample(sample)` is :6917 and `...d,` is :6920 — the adjudicator's ':6916-6918' range does not actually contain the spread it quotes. meta.radiusEarth at :6929 is exact. Read stats.js:54-76 (meanSEM, requiredSeeds) to check the planSweep claim.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: Severity low stands and changesBankedResult:false is correct. TWO ARITHMETIC/BEHAVIOUR CORRECTIONS to the adjudicator's planSweep reasoning. (1) It says the leaked control 'demands the minimum seed count'. It does not: at a fixed radius sd = 0 so cv = 0, and stats.js:74 `if (!(cv > 0) || !(targetFraction > 0)) return NaN;` makes requiredSeeds return NaN, so plan['radiusEarth'].seedsToMeasure is NaN. The CONCLUSION still holds — sweep.js:115-116 guard with Number.isFinite, so NaN can never become seedsToMeasureDrivenBy — but the stated reason is wrong. (2) A weakness in the control itself that neither reviewer nor adjudicator names: the fitted radiusEarth comes from sample.radiusEarth, which fieldProbe reads back from the SAME state.planetRadiusEarth that setPoint just wrote (planet-lod-lab.html:6971). So AC-CURVE-live.md's phrase 'proof inside every sweep that the driver actually moved' is only proof that the STATE VARIABLE moved and that fitPowerLaw works — it cannot prove applyDrivers propagated radius into the field. That is a tautological control, and it is exactly the property finding [1] exploits: the driver moved, the display lever moved with it, and nothing in the control could have noticed that the relief writer never did.

findings.title: responseCurve/planSweep restore radius and seeds but not the camera distance the sweep pushed out
findings.mechanism:
The title asserts the save/restore set is incomplete. It is: `prev` captures three scalars and the camera is not one of them, while the sweep provably perturbs `state.distance` via two frame-loop writers.
Of the two writers only one is lossy. `holdApparentDistance` (planet-lod-lab-core.js:75-81) is a pure multiplication by `sVisNext/sVisPrev`, so an out-and-back across the sweep returns the original distance — self-healing. The min-distance clamp at :5846 is a one-way ratchet: at the default `values` ceiling of 16 R⊕, sVis = 4 and the floor is 4.4, so an operator sitting closer than 4.4 planet-radii has their camera shoved out to 4.4 and it is never put back. It does NOT fire at the shipped default `distance: 20.0` (planet-lod-lab.html:2000), which is why this is a zoomed-in-operator defect rather than an every-run one.
findings.evidence:
planet-lod-lab.html:6965 — `const prev = { R: state.planetRadiusEarth, macro: state.macroSeed, detail: state.detailSeed };` (identically at :6993 for planSweep). No `distance` field; the `finally` blocks at :6978-6982 / :7003-7007 restore only R + the two seeds.
The sweep DOES move the camera, from inside frame():
  planet-lod-lab.html:5846 — `if (state.distance < _minDist) state.distance = _minDist;` where `_minDist = minCameraDistance(sVis)` (:5845) and planet-lod-lab-core.js:55-57 `export function minCameraDistance(sVis) { return sVis * CAMERA_CLEARANCE; }` with `CAMERA_CLEARANCE = 1.1`. This clamp only ever RAISES.
  planet-lod-lab.html:5829 — `if (state.holdApparentSize) state.distance = holdApparentDistance(state.distance, _sVisPrev, sVis);`
The lab's other sweep does restore it: planet-lod-lab.html:5379 `const prevFreeze = _sweepFreeze, baseT = t, baseYaw = state.yaw, baseDist = state.distance;` and :5407 `t = baseT; state.yaw = baseYaw; state.distance = baseDist;     // restore clock + camera + zoom`.
findings.impact: State pollution, not measurement error, for the sweep the census actually ran. `state.distance` reaches the sampled field only through `uniforms.uLodRamp.value = lod` (:5881, keyed on `logicalDist = state.distance / sVis` at :5862) — `uOctaves` is pinned by the sampler itself (planet-lod-rivers.js:454 `uniforms.uOctaves.value = octavesDuringRead;`). And `uLodRamp` is consumed inside the sampled field by only two combiners: the facet second octave (planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2569 `float fctLod = smoothstep(0.45, 1.0, uLodRamp);`) and the ECU block frequency (:2793). Both are zero-strength on the Earth-like preset the AC-CURVE ran, so the banked exponents are untouched. The residual risk worth naming: because the ratchet is monotone in sVis, on a facet/ECU-live preset (Crystal, technogenic) with a zoomed-in camera, distance would climb WITH radius inside the sweep — a radius-correlated confound on the swept driver itself. That variant is unmeasured.
findings.fixSketch: Add `distance: state.distance` (and, for completeness, `hold: state.holdApparentSize`) to the `prev` literals at :6965 and :6993, and restore them in both `finally` blocks — the same three-line pattern renderDeltaSweep already uses at :5379/:5407. Lab-file only; no generation source touched; no fenced token introduced.
findings.blastRadius: planet-lod-lab.html :6965/:6978-6982 and :6993/:7003-7007. Restoring `distance` inside `finally` is safe against the :5846 clamp because the restore also puts sVis back, so the restored distance is legal again on the next frame. No test pins the current behaviour.
findings.claimAmbiguity: 'pushed out' does not say by what. The strongest reading — the one I adjudicated — is any sweep-induced increase in state.distance, which covers both the min-distance clamp and hold-apparent-size. A narrower reading ('responseCurve itself sets the camera') would be NOT_REAL: neither function contains a `state.distance` assignment; the pushing is done by frame() on the sweep's behalf. Note also that holdApparentSize (planet-lod-lab.html:2259) landed 2026-07-28, three days AFTER these findings were written, so the reviewer can only have meant the clamp.
findings.refuterReason: Citation integrity is clean. planet-lod-lab.html:6965 is verbatim 'const prev = { R: state.planetRadiusEarth, macro: state.macroSeed, detail: state.detailSeed };' with no distance field, and :6993 is the identical line for planSweep; the finally blocks at :6978-6982 / :7003-7007 restore only R plus the two seeds. planet-lod-lab-core.js:54-57 is exactly 'export const CAMERA_CLEARANCE = 1.1;' / 'export function minCameraDistance(sVis) { return sVis * CAMERA_CLEARANCE; }', and holdApparentDistance is at :75-80 (adjudicator said 75-81 - off by one line at the closing brace, immaterial). :5846 'if (state.distance < _minDist) state.distance = _minDist;' is verbatim and is one-way. Arithmetic verified independently: VIS_SCALE_EXP = 0.5 (planet-lod-lab-core.js:45), so at R = 16 sVis = 4.0 and the floor is 4.4 - the adjudicator's numbers are exactly right, and 4.4 < 20.0 confirms it does not fire at default. The contrasting restore at :5379/:5407 exists as quoted. I also independently verified the impact chain rather than trusting it: uOctaves is pinned by the sampler (planet-lod-rivers.js:454 'uniforms.uOctaves.value = octavesDuringRead;'), and grepping planet-lod-height.glsl.js for uLodRamp returns only two live consumers - :2569 'float fctLod = smoothstep(0.45, 1.0, uLodRamp);' inside facetCombiner (guarded by 'if (fctGrow <= 0.0) return;' at :2555) and :2793 inside ecuRelief (guarded by 'if (uEcuCoverage <= 0.0) return;' at :2789). Both dead on Earth-like, so the AC-CURVE exponents cannot move. Not fixed by any post-2026-07-25 commit.

findings.title: laws.js injects isImpactSurface as a dependency that no law can read and no stub can affect
findings.mechanism: The title asserts a dead dependency-injection seam. Confirmed both halves: no law reads it, and no stub could change any measured output if one did, because craterSchedule closes over the real function. The reason this matters is the file's own AC-POSCTRL discipline (tests/instrument-laws.test.js:8-15: defects are planted by injection, not by editing source, and the identity assertions exist to close the one gap injection leaves). A dep listed in defaultDeps() reads as a plantable seam; this one is decoration. Practically, the impact-surface gate — the predicate that decides whether ANY crater law has a domain at all — is the single input to the bombardment laws that has never been positive-controlled, and cannot be with the current wiring. NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault: laws.js is the pure-function drift-guard layer and never touches the shader, the height field, or reliefBakeStrength.
findings.evidence: laws.js:136 `return { craterSchedule, reliefEnvelope, isImpactSurface };`. Every `measure` in LAW_REGISTRY reads only the other two: laws.js:72 `measure: (c, deps) => deps.craterSchedule(c).sizeMul`, :87 `deps.craterSchedule(c).nAnalytic`, :97, :108, :118 (all deps.craterSchedule), :130 `deps.reliefEnvelope(c.radiusEarth, c.surfaceGravity)`. Grepping the repo for `deps.isImpactSurface` returns nothing. And the gate is hard-wired inside the callee: src/worldengine/base/bombardment.js:156 `if (!isImpactSurface(condition)) {` — a module-scope call inside craterSchedule, not a parameter — so an injected replacement is unreachable from the audit even indirectly. The one place the dep IS exercised is an identity assertion, tests/instrument-laws.test.js:31 `expect(deps.isImpactSurface).toBe(isImpactSurface);`, which passes precisely because the dep is inert.
findings.impact: No number in any banked artifact is wrong because of this. laws.js has no production consumer at all — grepping `auditLaws|defaultDeps|instrument/laws` across the repo returns only laws.js itself and tests/instrument-laws.test.js; planet-lod-lab.html never calls it. So the effect is on evidence STRENGTH, not on values: RADIUS-CENSUS.md's Bombardment row banks "✅ WIRED (strongest) | LAW-AUDITED | ... All 6 laws PASS exactly; 6 planted defects each caught by name", and "6 planted defects" is 6 corruptions of craterSchedule/reliefEnvelope OUTPUTS (tests/instrument-laws.test.js:100-165). None of them plants a gate regression, and the injection seam that advertises the ability to is inert. A real regression in isImpactSurface would drive nAnalytic / D_FLOOR_KM / D_HI_KM to zero for all 7 sweep points, fitPowerLaw would drop all of them (stats.js:98) and return n=0/NaN, and the audit would report UNRESOLVABLE — allPass would still go false, so CI does catch it, but with a diagnosis that names the wrong thing (see finding 32, which makes that report say `points: 7`).
findings.fixSketch: Pick one, don't leave it as-is. (a) Delete `isImpactSurface` from laws.js:136 and drop the identity assertion at tests/instrument-laws.test.js:31 — honest, minimal, removes the false seam. (b) Better, if the gate is worth guarding: register it as a law in its own right — a boolean/domain law over a T_eq or atmosphere.pressure driver measuring `deps.isImpactSurface(c) ? 1 : 0` against the CRATER_T_MAX = 450 / P_SURF_MAX = 200 edges (bombardment.js:80-81), so the dep becomes live AND a plantable defect (`isImpactSurface: () => false`) has a named law to fail. Note (b) alone still doesn't let a stub reach craterSchedule; making THAT plantable would require bombardment.js to accept the predicate as a parameter, which is a generation-code edit and is exactly what the instrument's read-only discipline forbids — so (b) guards the predicate directly rather than through the schedule, and the limitation should be stated in the laws.js header.
findings.blastRadius: laws.js:136 plus tests/instrument-laws.test.js:31 (option a), or laws.js LAW_REGISTRY plus one new test block (option b). No production caller exists, so nothing else moves. If option (b) lands, RADIUS-CENSUS.md's "6 planted defects each caught by name" line should be updated to the new count rather than left stale (Rule 3 doc-on-ship).

findings.title: The UNRESOLVABLE sweep fixture sits 0.7% inside the FAIL boundary — the verdict is a lucky LCG draw
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the verdict is decided by luck rather than by the property being demonstrated. Confirmed to three digits: the fixture is inside the FAIL boundary by 0.71%. The intended demonstration is that an interval swallows BOTH the claim and the null; what the fixture actually rides is the claim side, which the fit misses badly enough (measured exponent -0.255 against a true 0.34 — wrong sign) that it is within a rounding error of being called FAIL. Any change to the LCG constants, the Box-Muller draw order, the inverse-variance weighting in fitPowerLaw, or the fixture's seed count flips this test red, and it would flip red for a reason unrelated to the behaviour under test. A second, sharper point: the same fix round that landed tCritical95 gives this test a robust route it does not take — passing `dof: fit.dof` yields z = 12.706, tol = 3.807, dClaim/tol = 0.156, still UNRESOLVABLE with ~84% headroom. The test was left on the pre-fix z = 2 path.
findings.evidence: tests/instrument-sweep.test.js:178-186 — the fixture runs `values: [1, 2, 4], seeds: SEEDS(3), measure: makeWorld({ exponent: 0.34, noiseCV: 1.2 })`, then :183 `const v = lawVerdict({ measured: fit.exponent, measuredSE: fit.exponentSE, claimed: 0.34 });` and :184 `expect(v.verdict).toBe('UNRESOLVABLE');`. findings.title: cos(lat) area weighting — the module's stated rule #2 — is never exercised in a way that could fail
findings.mechanism: The title asserts that the cos(lat) area weighting is never tested in a way a defect could break. What the code actually does: cos(lat) enters at three separate places, and two of them ARE pinned — `cellAreaKm2` by the sphere-area quadrature test (tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:28-39, which asserts both the error magnitude and its O(dphi^2) convergence) and `cellSpacingKm` by the networkLength meridian/equator/anisotropy tests (:294-319). The third — the propagation of those areas into the area-WEIGHTED moments via `areaWeights` — is completely unpinned. A defect confined to areaWeights (e.g. `w[k] = 1`, or dropping the row loop) passes the entire suite: it cannot reach cellAreaKm2's own tests, and no test evaluates rmsRelief or hypsometricIntegral on an equirect grid with a non-constant field. Related and equally unpinned: `bandCount` (:552-571) does no area weighting at all — its longitudinal mean at :555-558 and its profile mean at :560-562 treat an 85-degree row as worth exactly as much as an equatorial one.
findings.evidence: The weighting exists and is real: `/home/ax/projects/well-dipper/src/worldengine/instrument/descriptors.js:57` `return R * R * Math.cos(rowLatDeg(j, grid.height) * DEG) * dPhi * dLambda;` feeding `/home/ax/projects/well-dipper/src/worldengine/instrument/descriptors.js:69` `export function areaWeights(grid) {`, consumed by `rmsReliefKm` (:157-161) and `hypsometricIntegral` (:168-174) and by `describeSample` at `/home/ax/projects/well-dipper/src/worldengine/instrument/fieldSampler.js:197` `const w = areaWeights(sample.grids.physical);`. Every test of those two descriptors uses a PATCH grid, where cellAreaKm2 is uniform and cos(lat) never runs: tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:54 `const g = patch(32, 32);`, :62 `const g = patch(16, 16);`, :72 `const g = patch(32, 32);`, :81 `const g = patch(8, 8);`. The one equirect test that touches weighted moments feeds a zero field — :107 `const s = slopeStats(new Float64Array(1024).fill(0), g);` — so every value is 0 and the weights cannot change the answer. I confirmed the weights genuinely bite on a latitude-varying field: rmsRelief cos-weighted 0.44665 vs uniform-weighted 0.61525 (a 27% difference), hypsometric 0.78016 vs 0.62774.
findings.impact: No wrong number today — I read areaWeights and believe it correct. The impact is that the instrument's own rule about area weighting is unguarded: the one line most likely to be 'simplified' during a refactor is invisible to CI, in a module whose whole premise is that it catches silent numeric drift. Any future whole-sphere census row (rmsRelief, hypsometry, elevation moments over a full equirect sample) would inherit an unverified weighting.
findings.fixSketch: Add two AC-MATH fixtures on an equirect grid with an analytically known answer: (a) a field that is constant within each hemisphere — cos(lat)-weighted mean must equal the arithmetic hemisphere mean while the unweighted row mean does not; (b) `hypsometricIntegral(h, equirect)` on h = sin(lat), whose area-weighted mean is exactly 0 by symmetry while a uniform-weight mean is not. Assert to 1e-9 so a uniform-weight regression cannot survive. Optionally assert `areaWeights(equirect).reduce(sum) === 1` and that row 0's weight is strictly less than the equatorial row's. Pure test addition — no generation source touched, so AC-POSCTRL discipline and the vis-scale fence are both untouched.
findings.blastRadius: Test-only. No src/ change, no goldens, no banked number moves.

findings.title: bandCount's noise-rejection claim is false, and the fixtures contain no noise to reject
findings.mechanism: The title makes two assertions and both hold. (1) Dropping a short run is not folding it: a single anomalous row inside a band splits that band into two same-sign runs plus one 1-row run; the filter removes the 1-row run but leaves the two halves counted separately, so the count goes UP by one — the exact inflation the docstring says is impossible. (2) `minRunRows = 2` only screens 1-row excursions at all, so a 2-row excursion survives untouched and inflates by two (2 -> 4 measured). The fixtures cannot detect either, because neither contains a short-run perturbation. Note this is the test-side twin of finding [6] (`bandCount discards short runs instead of folding them`), which is the same defect stated against descriptors.js — one fix closes both.
findings.evidence: The docstring at `/home/ax/projects/well-dipper/src/worldengine/instrument/descriptors.js:549-551` promises: "Runs shorter than `minRunRows` are folded into their neighbour so single-row noise cannot inflate the count." The code at :569 does not fold, it drops: `const kept = runs.filter((r) => r.len >= minRunRows);` then :570 `return { bands: kept.length, ... }`. Executed against the real module: a clean 2-band field returns 2; flip ONE row inside the first band and it returns 3 (runs 4); flip TWO adjacent rows and it returns 4. Both fixtures are noise-free by construction — tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:336-346 builds a pure sinusoid (`const v = Math.sin((2 * Math.PI * cycles * j) / g.height);`) and :348-351 a constant field (`bandCount(new Float64Array(512).fill(1), g)`).
findings.impact: The instrument's `bandCount` over-reports zonal bands on any field with per-row noise, and the failure is monotone upward, so it would read as a spurious positive radius response if the band count were ever swept. Crucially it is NOT the quantity in the banked atmosphere row: RADIUS-CENSUS.md's "band count 5 -> 14 across R = 3 -> 16, R^0.632 +/- 0.018" is `climate-e5.js:218` (`if ((u < 0) !== (prevU < 0)) bandCount++;`), a different function. The instrument's own bandCount is only computed on equirect samples (fieldSampler.js:180 `if (sample.kind === 'equirect') d.bandCount = bandCount(h, grid).bands;`) and every banked sweep ran the patch probe (planet-lod-lab.html:6963, 6991 default `probe = { mode: 'patch', ... }`), so it has never appeared in a banked number.
findings.fixSketch: Two changes. Source: implement the documented fold — walk `runs` and merge any run with `len < minRunRows` into the preceding run (absorbing its length and keeping the preceding sign), re-merging adjacent same-sign runs afterwards, then count. That makes the one-row-flip case return 2. Alternative, if dropping is actually wanted, correct the docstring to say what it does and state the inflation as a known limit. Test: add a fixture that takes the existing k-cycle sinusoid, flips one row and then two adjacent rows, and asserts the count is unchanged at 2k. Pure descriptor math — no generation source, no injection needed.
findings.blastRadius: descriptors.js:552-571 plus tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:335-352. No live consumer today (equirect-only, and no banked sweep uses the equirect probe), so nothing downstream re-runs. Fixing it before any whole-sphere census row is added is the cheap ordering.
findings.refuterReason: Both halves of the title reproduce exactly on my own run of the real module. (1) Clean 1-cycle equirect field -> bands 2, runs 3. Flip ONE row inside the first band -> bands 3, runs 4: the filter drops the 1-row run but leaves the two same-sign halves counted separately, so the count goes UP by one. That is precisely the inflation descriptors.js:549-550 promises is impossible. (2) Flip TWO adjacent rows -> bands 4: minRunRows=2 screens nothing at length 2, so a 2-row excursion inflates by two. Both fixtures are noise-free by construction, so neither can detect it. The banked-result reasoning is the strongest part and I verified it end to end: the census's atmosphere row ('band count 5 -> 14 across R = 3 -> 16', 'R^0.632 +/- 0.018') comes from climate-e5.js:218 `if ((u < 0) !== (prevU < 0)) bandCount++;` — a zero-crossing diagnostic on the jet profile — and the census itself flags the confusion in its own update block ('bandCount (a zero-crossing diagnostic) != rhinesWavenumber (the law)'). findings.title: The buried-form spectral test sits at 92% of its tolerance, one radial bin from failing
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the fixture is knife-edge. It is, and for a structural reason: the true radial wavenumber of a product sinusoid sin(16x)sin(16y) is 16*sqrt(2) = 22.63, which is not an integer, but `spectralExcessPeak` can only report `spanKm / k` for integer k (descriptors.js:392 `wavelength: spanKm / best.k`). No integer bin can land within 0.5 km of 28.284 except k = 23. So the assertion is not 'the metric is accurate to 0.5 km' — it is 'the argmax lands on exactly one specific bin', asserted through a tolerance that reads like an accuracy claim. Any change to the Hann window, the MAD noise scale, the sqrt(modes) weighting or the fixture's harmonic stack that moves the argmax one bin down turns a correct metric into a red test. This is the same integer-bin resolution limit that AC-CURVE-live already flags as its second qualification.
findings.evidence: tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:172-173: `const trueRadialWavelength = 640 / (cycles * Math.SQRT2);` / `expect(peak.wavelength).toBeCloseTo(trueRadialWavelength, 0);` — precision 0 means |diff| < 0.5. Executed against the real module: the peak lands on k = 23, wavelength 27.826 km, truth 28.2843, diff 0.4582 = 91.6% of the 0.5 tolerance. The adjacent bins are 640/22 = 29.091 (diff 0.807 -> FAIL) and 640/24 = 26.667 (diff 1.618 -> FAIL). The contest between bins is genuinely close: sigma at k=21/22/23/24 is 8.48 / 9.99 / 11.12 / 9.19, i.e. the runner-up k=22 is only 11% below the winner.
findings.impact: Test brittleness, not a wrong number. The metric is right; the assertion is mis-specified. The concrete cost is a future false alarm: a legitimate improvement to the noise scale would present as 'the form-size metric broke', and the reviewer's own house lesson is that a plausible-looking number is the failure mode here.
findings.fixSketch: Adopt the idiom the fix round already uses one file over — tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js:86-89 asserts a RELATIVE bound with an explicit comment that peaks land on integer bins: `expect(Math.abs(p.wavelength / truth - 1)).toBeLessThan(0.03)`. Here use `expect(Math.abs(peak.wavelength / trueRadialWavelength - 1)).toBeLessThan(0.05)`, which admits k = 22 (+2.85%) and k = 23 (-1.62%) and still rejects k = 21 (+7.8%) and k = 24 (-5.7%) — i.e. 'within one bin of truth', which is the strongest claim the metric's own resolution supports. Also assert `peak.detected === true` and `peak.peakSigma > 4.5` so the fixture keeps testing detection strength rather than only bin identity.
findings.blastRadius: One assertion in tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js. No src/ change.

Not carrier-off related, except very weakly: if the baked-relief crossover drives relief amplitude toward zero at large R, more descriptors could degenerate toward constants and widen this path. findings.evidence: Trace for sd = 0, mean != 0: stats.js:62 `cv: mean !== 0 ? sd / Math.abs(mean) : NaN` gives cv = 0. sweep.js:169 `Math.abs(stats.mean) > stats.sd` is then 0 finite / 0 finite / |mean| > 0 = TRUE, so cvIsMeaningful PASSES and the descriptor takes the normal branch. stats.js:74 `if (!(cv > 0) || !(targetFraction > 0)) return NaN;` — requiredSeeds(0, 0.15) = NaN; stats.js:83 the same for seedsToResolve. sweep.js:114 then writes `plan[key] = { cv: s.cv, sd: s.sd, mean: s.mean, noiseFloorFraction: s.cv, seedsToMeasure: toMeasure, seedsToResolve: toResolve };` — NaN counts with NO `relativeNoiseUndefined` flag and NO `reason`, and the key never reaches `unusable.push(key)` (sweep.js:109, the other branch), so it is absent from `descriptorsWithUndefinedRelativeNoise` at sweep.js:126. findings.title: The degeneracy guard in fitPowerLaw uses an absolute threshold on a weight-scaled quantity, so identical x values can produce a fabricated exponent
findings.mechanism: The title asserts that the 1e−15 cut-off at stats.js:121 is an ABSOLUTE bar applied to `denom`, a quantity whose magnitude scales as W²·(spread of ln x)², so it cannot detect degeneracy. Confirmed exactly. For a rank-deficient design (all x equal) `denom` is mathematically zero, but floating point leaves a residue proportional to the size of the terms being differenced: sw·swxx for three points at ln 8 is ~38.9, whose roundoff is ~9e−15 — already above the bar with UNIFORM weights (so the 'weight-scaled' framing is if anything understated; the bug bites even at W=1). With inverse-variance weights the terms are ~2.5e5 larger each, so denom's roundoff lands near 1e−4, five orders above the bar, and the guard is decorative. `b` is then a ratio of two roundoff residues — arbitrary. Measured fabrications: −1 and +2, both plausible-looking physical exponents. What limits the damage is downstream, not here: chi2/dof is then huge or sw/denom negative, so exponentSE comes back NaN or ~1e7, and lawVerdict's non-finite branch (stats.js:188-189) or its interval-swallows-both branch (:206) reports UNRESOLVABLE rather than a false PASS/FAIL. But `fits[key].exponent` and `r2` are returned raw and are exactly the fields the evidence tables print. No connection to the carrier-off / baked-vs-synth split — this is a linear-algebra conditioning bug.
findings.evidence:
src/worldengine/instrument/stats.js:120 — `const denom = sw * swxx - swx * swx;`
src/worldengine/instrument/stats.js:121 — `if (Math.abs(denom) < 1e-15) return { exponent: NaN, exponentSE: NaN, coefficient: NaN, r2: NaN, n, dropped: dropped.length, z };`
src/worldengine/instrument/stats.js:114 — `const W = weightingIsUniform ? usable.map(() => 1) : sigmas.map((s) => 1 / (s * s));` (the weights the threshold is being compared against; stats.js:107 itself notes 'real weights of ~4e5').
src/worldengine/instrument/stats.js:122 — `const b = (sw * swxy - swx * swy) / denom;`
Reproduced by calling the real module read-only (no files written): `fitPowerLaw([{x:8,y:10},{x:8,y:20},{x:8,y:15}])` → `{exponent:-1, exponentSE:NaN, r2:0, n:3, dof:1, t95:12.706}` — denom came out −7.105e−15, above the 1e−15 bar, so the guard did not fire and an exponent of exactly −1 was fabricated from roundoff. `fitPowerLaw([{x:3,y:10,sem:0.02},{x:3,y:21,sem:0.053},{x:3,y:15.7,sem:0.031}])` → `{exponent:2, exponentSE:1.766e7, r2:-2.2e-16}` — with inverse-variance weights (max W = 2.5e5) denom is ~1e−4, four orders above the bar, and the reported exponent is 2. `fitPowerLaw` on four identical x DID trip the guard (denom happened to be exactly 0) — whether the guard fires is luck of the roundoff, which is the finding's point.
Live callers, both with distinct x by construction: src/worldengine/instrument/sweep.js:74 `fits[key] = fitPowerLaw(pts);` fed from `p.value` over the sweep's `values`, default `const values = o.values || [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16];` (planet-lod-lab.html:6960); and src/worldengine/instrument/laws.js:159 `const fit = fitPowerLaw(points, { z });` over literal registries such as laws.js:104 `values: [0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0],`.
findings.impact: A caller who passes repeated (or near-repeated) driver values gets a confident-looking exponent invented from floating-point noise — measured at −1 and +2 in this repo's own code — with an r² of 0 sitting beside it. The verdict layer degrades to UNRESOLVABLE rather than lying outright, so nothing currently emits a false PASS. No banked number is affected: every live call site uses well-separated, distinct driver values (sweep default 0.5…16 with factor-2 spacing; the law registry's literal arrays), so no run of this instrument has ever entered the degenerate regime. The exposure is a latent trap for any future caller who repeats a driver value — e.g. running a sweep at one fixed value to check the noise floor, which is precisely what planSweep's pilot does, though planSweep does not call fitPowerLaw.
findings.fixSketch: Replace the absolute cut-off at stats.js:121 with a scale-relative conditioning test, e.g. `const scale = sw * swxx; if (!(Math.abs(denom) > 1e-10 * Math.abs(scale)))` — this is dimensionless in the weights and catches degeneracy at any weight magnitude. Belt-and-braces: add an explicit distinct-x precondition before the algebra (`new Set(X).size < 2` → return the NaN result with `reason: 'all driver values are identical — a log-log slope is undefined'`), which is cheaper to read and cannot be defeated by roundoff at all. Pure stats.js change; no generation code touched, no DI required, and the fix mentions none of `visScaleOf|sVis|VIS_SCALE_EXP` so the tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js grep is unaffected. Add a regression test with three identical x asserting NaN exponent, since the existing suite has no degenerate-x fixture.

With inverse-variance weights the terms are ~2.5e5 larger each and the residue lands near 1e-4, five orders above the bar. findings.title: cellAreaKm2 uses the midpoint rule but its docstring claims the sum is exactly 4πR²
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the docstring overclaims exactness for a quadrature approximation. Correct. The exact area of an equirect row is R²(sin φ_north − sin φ_south)dλ = R²·2·sin(dφ/2)·cos(lat_j)·dλ, whereas the code returns R²·dφ·cos(lat_j)·dλ. The ratio is dφ / (2 sin(dφ/2)) = x/sin x with x = π/(2H) — strictly greater than 1, so the sum always OVERSHOOTS 4πR², by ≈ 1 + (π/2H)²/6. The single most useful fact about this defect, which the title does not state: that ratio is INDEPENDENT of j. The error is one global scale factor, so it cancels identically in areaWeights (descriptors.js:69-79, which normalises to sum 1) and therefore in every weighted moment, in rmsRelief, in hypsometricIntegral and in slopeStats. The relative row weighting is EXACT, not approximate. Only absolute areas survive it: totalAreaKm2 and anything dividing by it (countDensity, drainageDensity, boundaryDensity). Nothing to do with the carrier-off fault.
findings.evidence: descriptors.js:47-48 (docstring) — 'Per-cell area in km^2 for row j. Equirect: dA = R^2 cos(lat) dphi dlambda, which sums to 4 pi R^2 over the whole grid.' descriptors.js:57 (code) — `return R * R * Math.cos(rowLatDeg(j, grid.height) * DEG) * dPhi * dLambda;` — the midpoint rule, evaluating cos at the row centre. descriptors.js:60 repeats the claim for the sum: 'Total area of the sampled domain, km^2. Equirect over a full sphere returns 4 pi R^2.' Measured against the shipped module: totalAreaKm2 / 4πR² = 1.0064545 at H=8, 1.0004017 at H=32, 1.0000251 at H=128 (the shipped equirect height, fieldSampler.js:90), 1.0000063 at H=256.
findings.impact: +0.0025% on `d.totalArea` for the shipped 256×128 equirect probe, and the same +0.0025% downward on any density that divides by it (none are currently computed — see finding [8]). Zero on every weighted descriptor, exactly, by the argument above. Patch grids are unaffected entirely (descriptors.js:62, `return grid.spanKmX * grid.spanKmY;`). This is a documentation-accuracy defect with a numerically irrelevant tail at the shipped resolution; it would only start to matter at H ≤ 16 (0.16%+), which nothing uses. Severity 'low' from 2026-07-25 was right and I would not raise it.
findings.fixSketch: Two lines, either order. (a) Make it exact: `return R * R * (Math.sin(latN) - Math.sin(latS)) * dLambda;` with latN/latS the row's bounding latitudes from rowLatDeg ± half-step — this makes totalAreaKm2 return 4πR² to floating-point and removes the caveat rather than documenting it. (b) If exactness is not wanted, weaken both docstrings to 'sums to 4πR² to within (π/2H)²/6 (2.5e-5 at the shipped H=128)' and say the row-relative weights are exact regardless. I would take (a): it is strictly simpler than the sentence explaining (b), and it makes the existing assertion in the module header (rule #1, PHYSICAL UNITS, descriptors.js:18-21) true as written. Pin with a test asserting totalAreaKm2 === 4πR² to 12 decimals at H = 8, 32 and 128 — note the CURRENT code fails that at H=8 by 0.65%, so the test is a real control and not a tautology.
findings.blastRadius: descriptors.js:47-58 and :60-66, plus one test. areaWeights output is unchanged to floating point under fix (a) (the constant cancels in the normalisation either way), so no weighted descriptor moves — worth asserting in the same test so the fix is provably inert where it should be. No live caller reads totalArea for a decision; fieldSampler.js:167 only reports it.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The docstring at :47-48 could be read as describing the CONTINUOUS integral (∫R²cos dφ dλ = 4πR², which is true) rather than the discrete sum. I rejected that reading because of the words 'over the whole grid' and, decisively, because descriptors.js:60 makes the same claim about the function that performs the discrete sum: 'Equirect over a full sphere returns 4 pi R^2.' That is a statement about the return value, and it is false by 2.5e-5 at the shipped resolution.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives as a documentation-accuracy defect, and I redid every number rather than accepting theirs. The exact area of an equirect row is R^2 (sin phi_N - sin phi_S) dlambda = R^2 * 2 sin(dphi/2) cos(lat_j) dlambda, while descriptors.js:57 returns `R * R * Math.cos(rowLatDeg(j, grid.height) * DEG) * dPhi * dLambda`, so the ratio is dphi / (2 sin(dphi/2)) = x/sin(x) with x = pi/(2H) — strictly > 1 (overshoot) and, as their sharpest observation states, INDEPENDENT of j. I recomputed x/sin(x) directly: H=8 gives 0.196350/0.1950903 = 1.0064558 (they said 1.0064545), H=32 gives 1.0004016 (they said 1.0004017), H=128 gives 1.0000251 (matches), H=256 gives 1.0000063 (matches). Docstrings confirmed verbatim at :47-48 and :60. NOT ALREADY_FIXED. One thing the adjudicator missed that makes the verdict sharper, not weaker: tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:28-39 ALREADY documents the overshoot explicitly ('The cos(lat) midpoint rule is a quadrature of the exact integral, so the sum sits slightly ABOVE 4 pi R^2 ... So the CODE is understood and pinned; the defect is purely that the two docstrings still assert an exactness the module's own test denies — which is precisely the finding.
