findings.title: radialPSD bins by cycles-per-domain and converts with the mean span, silently assuming an isotropic patch that physicalPatchGrid does not enforce
findings.mechanism: This is finding [7] restated from the contract end: [7] describes the wrong ANSWER, [27] describes the missing PRECONDITION. Both are the same three lines. The added substance in [27] is correct and worth keeping: radialPSD's radial bin index is in cycles-per-domain, so it is only meaningful when the domain is isotropic, and nothing in the type — neither physicalPatchGrid (sampling.js:68) nor angularPatchGrid (sampling.js:73) nor radialPSD's own guard (descriptors.js:279) — enforces that. The grid contract in the module header (descriptors.js:31-33, 'patch: { mode:"patch", width, height, spanKmX, spanKmY }') documents two independent spans and then the math assumes they are equal. Not connected to the carrier-off fault.
findings.evidence: Same lines as [7]: descriptors.js:300 `const r = Math.round(Math.hypot(kx, ky));` (binning on integer cycles-per-domain, which mixes the two axes), descriptors.js:314 and :377 `const spanKm = (grid.spanKmX + grid.spanKmY) / 2;`. The 'does not enforce' half is exact — sampling.js:68-70: `export function physicalPatchGrid(width, height, spanKmX, spanKmY) { return { mode: 'patch', width, height, spanKmX, spanKmY, frame: 'physical' }; }` — a plain object literal with no validation of any kind, and radialPSD's only precondition check is the mode test at descriptors.js:279.
findings.impact: None on any measurement taken, for the same reason as [7]: fieldSampler.js:125-126 passes the same scalar for both spans, so every live grid is isotropic in span. The real content is documentation/contract debt — a two-span type whose consumer only handles the one-span case, with no guard to say so. One genuinely adjacent and REACHABLE anisotropy this finding does NOT cover and should not be confused with: the sphere patch itself compresses its east-west spacing by cos(av) away from the centre row (sampling.js:141-146), ~4.8% at the corners for a 2000 km span at radiusEarth 0.5 — that is finding [28], sampling.js, a different cluster.
findings.fixSketch: Identical to [7] — one guard in radialPSD comparing spanKmX/width against spanKmY/height, which simultaneously enforces the precondition and makes the mean-span line unreachable. Optionally also assert it in physicalPatchGrid, but the guard belongs with the consumer that has the assumption, not the constructor that legitimately carries two spans (angularPatchGrid needs the two-span form for a future non-square window). Fix [7] and [27] together; they are one change.
findings.blastRadius: Same three lines as [7]. Mark one of the two as a duplicate in the triage ledger.
findings.claimAmbiguity: 'Bins by cycles-per-domain' could be read as an accusation that cycles-per-domain is itself the wrong unit. It is not — span/k is exactly right for an isotropic patch and is what makes the wavelength conversion at :320/:392 dimensionally correct. I adjudicated the reading the second clause makes plain: the binning is only valid under an isotropy assumption that nothing enforces.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives; it is [7] stated from the precondition side and both are the same three lines. The 'does not enforce' half is exact — sampling.js:68-70 is a bare object literal (`export function physicalPatchGrid(width, height, spanKmX, spanKmY) { return { mode: 'patch', width, height, spanKmX, spanKmY, frame: 'physical' }; }`) with no validation, angularPatchGrid at :73 likewise, and radialPSD's only precondition test is the mode check at descriptors.js:279. The module header at descriptors.js:31-33 does document two independent spans (`patch: { mode:'patch', width, height, spanKmX, spanKmY }`) that the math then assumes equal — I confirmed that line reads as quoted. I also independently redid the one piece of arithmetic in this row, the adjacent-but-distinct anisotropy they warn not to confuse it with: at radiusEarth 0.5 the sphere radius is 3185.5 km, so a 2000 km span subtends 0.6279 rad, half-span 0.31395 rad, and cos(0.31395) = 0.9511 — a 4.89% east-west compression at the corner rows, so their '~4.8%' is right and correctly attributed to sampling.js:141-146 (which I read: `const ca = Math.cos(au), sa = Math.sin(au), cb = Math.cos(av), sb = Math.sin(av);` and the direction construction that follows) and correctly routed to a different cluster.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Read sampling.js:60-80 and :127-150 directly. Read descriptors.js:26-33 (the grid contract), :278-321, :343-401. Recomputed the cos(av) corner compression from the actual constants rather than accepting the quoted percentage. Confirmed via git show 0744fa4 hunk headers that none of these lines were touched by the fix round.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: LOW is correct and matches the banked record. Should be merged with [7] as one fix, not two — same three lines (descriptors.js:300, :314, :377).

findings.title: The patch's "no gnomonic stretch" km-scale claim is tested at 400 km but the lab's default sweep runs 2000 km down to radiusEarth 0.5, where the column spacing compresses ~4.8%
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the header's projection claim is validated only at a span where the effect is ~20x below the test's own tolerance, while the shipped default sweep runs at a span/radius where it is ~5x ABOVE it. Both halves check out. The header's error is one of sign and scope, not of kind: this construction is not gnomonic and does not stretch by 1/cos^2, but it is not equidistant either — it COMPRESSES columns by cos(av), reaching -4.81% at the top/bottom rows and -1.61% averaged over rows at R=0.5. The grids handed to the descriptors declare a flat spanKmX (sampling.js:68-70, fieldSampler.js:125), so radialPSD/spectralExcessPeak convert bin k with spanKm/k while the true row-local span is spanKm·cos(av) — reported wavelengths are OVERSTATED by 1/cos(av). NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault: this is sample-point geometry, independent of whether the sampled body is baked relief or LEGACY synth.
findings.evidence: The claim: sampling.js:120-123 — "which reproduces the angular offset EXACTLY along both axes through the centre and departs only in the cross terms. A plain gnomonic tangent-plane projection would stretch the km scale by 1/cos^2 out at the corners; this does not, which is why patch-measured wavelengths can be quoted in km without a projection caveat at the spans this instrument uses." The test: tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:116 `const base = { latDeg: 20, lonDeg: -45, spanKmX: 400, spanKmY: 400, radiusEarth: 1, width: 32, height: 32 };` and :140-149 `it('keeps the km scale honest to the corners (no gnomonic stretch)' ... expect(Math.abs(corner / centre - 1)).toBeLessThan(0.01);`. The default sweep: planet-lod-lab.html:6959 `const values = o.values || [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16];` and :6961 `const probe = o.probe || { mode: 'patch', latDeg: 10, lonDeg: 20, spanKm: 2000, width: 128, height: 128 };`. Geometry: sampling.js:142-146 builds p = n·ca·cb + east·sa·cb + north·sb, which in the rotated frame (east, north, n) is exactly an equirect grid with lat' = av, lon' = au — so the arc between adjacent columns in row j is cos(av_j)·Δau·R, i.e. small-circle convergence. I evaluated the ratio corner/centre: the 400 km / R=1 / h=32 fixture gives 0.999538 (0.046% — the 1% bar is ~20x slack), while 2000 km / R=0.5 / h=128 gives 0.951887, i.e. 4.81% compression at av = 17.85 deg. That reproduces the title's "~4.8%" to two digits.
findings.impact: Quantified, and below reporting precision everywhere it has actually been used. AC-CURVE-live.md:70 ran R ∈ {4, 8, 16} at 2000 km, where the row-averaged bias is 0.025% / 0.006% / 0.002% — the fitted physical exponent +0.4583 ± 0.0148 (AC-CURVE-live.md:82) would move by ~4e-4, i.e. 3% of the quoted SE and 0.2% of the corrected ±0.19 t-interval. AC-SAMPLE-live.md's single-seed table hits R = 0.5 (mean bias +1.64%) and R = 1 (+0.41%), but those two rows are already formally withdrawn as window-scale false positives by that document's own correction block (AC-SAMPLE-live.md:3-24), so there is no surviving number to move. The real cost is a false assurance in the docs: AC-SAMPLE-live.md:41 banks "PASS — sphere geometry; patch spacing verified to 1% corner-to-centre headlessly", which is true at the fixture and false at the shipped default sweep's low-radius end. Also second-order: because the compression varies by row, a monochromatic feature is slightly chirped across bins, broadening the excess peak at R ≤ 1.
findings.fixSketch: Two separable, both cheap. (1) Honesty: reword sampling.js:120-125 to state the actual distortion law — column arc = cos(av)·Δau·R, corner compression 1 - cos(halfSpanAng), which is 0.05% at 400 km/R=1 and 4.8% at 2000 km/R=0.5 — and drop "without a projection caveat." (2) Test: re-point tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:140-149 at the shipped default geometry (spanKmX/Y 2000, radiusEarth 0.5, width/height 128) and assert the measured ratio against the closed form cos(halfSpanAng) rather than a 1% constant, so the test measures the mechanism instead of clearing it by 20x. If the bias is ever wanted gone rather than documented, scale each row's au by 1/cos(av) in sampling.js:140 — that makes column arc length uniform at the cost of the rows no longer being a rotated equirect; do NOT do that without re-running any patch measurement banked before it.
findings.blastRadius: Option (1) + (2) touch only sampling.js comments and one test — zero numeric change, nothing to re-run. Option (3), the geometry change, alters every patch sample point and would invalidate byte-comparison of any future patch determinism hash; it is not needed to close this finding. Note sampling.js is under src/worldengine/**, so any new comment must avoid the visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP tokens that tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:29 greps for including comments — describe the disc scale by name, don't write sVis.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The title says "compresses", which is correct but is the opposite sense from the header's own gnomonic-stretch framing; I read the claim as "the km-scale-honesty assertion is untested at the geometry the lab actually runs" rather than "the construction is secretly gnomonic" (it is not gnomonic). The rejected stronger reading — that the 4.8% figure invalidates a banked wavelength — does not survive: the only banked rows at R ≤ 1 are already withdrawn for an unrelated reason.
findings.refuterReason: Core verdict survives; I re-derived the geometry from scratch. In the rotated frame (n, east, north) the point built at sampling.js:142-146 is exactly (cos au cos av, sin au cos av, sin av), i.e. an equirect grid with lat'=av and lon'=au about the `north` pole — so the arc between adjacent columns in row j is cos(av_j)*d(au)*R. That is small-circle CONVERGENCE (compression), not gnomonic stretch, so the header's error is one of scope and sign as claimed. I reproduced both magnitudes independently: the test fixture (400 km, R=1, h=32) gives row-0 av = 0.030411 rad and corner/centre = 0.999538 (0.046% — the 1% bar at tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:148 has ~20x slack); the shipped default sweep at 2000 km / R=0.5 / h=128 gives row-0 av = 0.311467 rad = 17.845 deg and cos = 0.951887, i.e. 4.81% compression. Both match the adjudicator to the digit, and 4.81% reproduces the title's '~4.8%'. Row-averaged biases also reproduce exactly: E[1-cos av] = a^2/6 - a^4/120 gives 1.61% at R=0.5, 0.40% at R=1, 0.101% at R=2, 0.0253% at R=4, 0.0063% at R=8, 0.0016% at R=16. Direction of the wavelength error is right: the grid declares a flat spanKmX (sampling.js:68-70 physicalPatchGrid, called at fieldSampler.js:125), while the true row-local span is spanKm*cos(av), so reported wavelengths are OVERSTATED by 1/cos(av). NOT already fixed (no commits to sampling.js since 2026-07-25; the fix-round test never imports it). NOT downstream of carrier-off — correct, same reasoning as [14]. WHAT I REFUTE: three misattributed line numbers and one arithmetic overstatement. (a) 'planet-lod-lab.html:6959 `const values = o.values || [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16];`' — :6959 is `async responseCurve(opts){`; the values line is :6961. (b) '`:6961 const probe = ...`' — the probe line is :6964. (c) 'AC-SAMPLE-live.md:41 banks PASS — sphere geometry; patch spacing verified to 1% corner-to-centre headlessly' — that row is at :40. The quoted TEXT is real in all three cases, so this is misattribution, not fabrication, but every one of them is off. (d) The arithmetic claim 'the fitted physical exponent +0.4583 +/- 0.0148 would move by ~4e-4, i.e. 3% of the quoted SE' is overstated by ~2.4x. Regressing the three biases (2.53e-4, 6.32e-5, 1.58e-5) on ln R over {4,8,16} gives a slope of -1.71e-4, and the analytic check (b ~ R^-2 so db/dlnR = -2b, -1.26e-4 at the midpoint) agrees. So the true shift is ~1.3-1.7e-4, i.e. ~1.2% of the SE, not 3%. The error is in the direction that makes the finding look worse than it is, so the 'negligible' conclusion is if anything strengthened. (e) Incomplete rather than wrong: 'those two rows are already formally withdrawn ... so there is no surviving number to move' overlooks that AC-SAMPLE-live.md:109-111 (R = 2, 4, 8) DO survive the correction block and DO carry bias — but at 0.101%/0.025%/0.006% against values printed to 3 sig figs (35.1, 51.3, 71.4 km), the bias is below the last printed digit, so the conclusion stands.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Re-read sampling.js:113-150 (the docstring claim at :120-123 verified verbatim, including the 'at the spans this instrument uses' escape clause the finding turns on), tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:115-149 (fixture at :116 with spanKmX 400 / radiusEarth 1 verified verbatim; the 1% assertion at :148 verified), planet-lod-lab.html:6959-6983 with true line numbers, fieldSampler.js:113-130 (samplePatch -> physicalPatchGrid(width, height, spanKm, spanKm) at :125), and the banked artifacts: AC-CURVE-live.md:70 'R in {4, 8, 16}, M = 5, zero failed readings' verified verbatim, :82 '+0.4583 | 0.0148 | 0.999' verified, AC-SAMPLE-live.md:3-24 correction block and :40 PASS row and :105-111 single-seed table all read directly. Redid every percentage myself from the code's own constants (R_EARTH_KM = 6371 at sampling.js:32) rather than accepting any of the adjudicator's figures. Also checked the R1 statusNote in docs/WORKSTREAMS/world-engine-radius-live-feed-2026-07-25/contract.json: its measured quantity is the rendered BELT COUNT (G4), which comes from bandCount — equirect-only (fieldSampler.js:181), never patch — so the patch compression cannot touch it.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: Severity low is correct and matches the original triage severity (low). No downgrade occurred here. If anything the adjudicator's own arithmetic error inflated the apparent stakes; corrected, the effect on the only banked exponent is ~1.2% of its standard error.

findings.title: physical and angular rmsRelief / hypsometricIntegral are the same number by construction, so the frame split duplicates them into the sweep
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the two frames produce identical values for the vertical-only descriptors, and that is exactly what the normalisation does. rmsRelief and hypsometricIntegral are functions of the height array and the normalised area weights alone; the frame changes the weights only by a constant factor per cell, which cancels in the normalisation. So `physical.rmsRelief === angular.rmsRelief` and `physical.hypsometricIntegral === angular.hypsometricIntegral` to floating-point residue, and `slopeExcludedFraction` likewise. This is CORRECT physics — a vertical statistic has no business changing when you relabel the horizontal axis — but the code presents it as two independent measurements, and sweep.js's dynamic key discovery (sweep.js:69) turns them into two independent descriptors with two independent noise floors and two independent fitted exponents. Contrast the descriptors that legitimately differ per frame: `autocorrWavelength`, `formWavelength`, `totalArea`, and the slope/gradient family, which is exactly why the frame loop exists.
findings.evidence:
BOTH ARE COMPUTED INSIDE THE FRAME LOOP. fieldSampler.js:158 `  for (const frame of ['physical', 'angular']) {`, :165 `    d.hypsometricIntegral = hypsometricIntegral(h, grid);        // a ratio: scale-invariant`, :183 `    d.rmsRelief = rmsReliefKm(h, grid);`.

BOTH DEPEND ON THE GRID ONLY THROUGH NORMALISED AREA WEIGHTS. descriptors.js:157-160 `export function rmsReliefKm(heightsKm, grid) {` / `  const w = areaWeights(grid);` / `  const m = distributionMoments(heightsKm, w);` / `  return m.sd;`; descriptors.js:168-173 the same for hypsometricIntegral.

THE WEIGHTS ARE SCALE-INVARIANT. descriptors.js:69-79 `export function areaWeights(grid) {` … `  if (sum > 0) for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) w[k] /= sum;` — normalised to sum 1. The only frame difference is a CONSTANT multiplier on every cell: equirect, descriptors.js:54-57 `  const R = grid.radiusKm;` … `  return R * R * Math.cos(rowLatDeg(j, grid.height) * DEG) * dPhi * dLambda;` with R = radiusEarth*6371 (sampling.js:55) vs R = 180/pi (sampling.js:64) — the R² factor divides out. Patch, descriptors.js:51-53 `  if (grid.mode === 'patch') { return (grid.spanKmX / grid.width) * (grid.spanKmY / grid.height); }` — constant across cells in BOTH frames (sampling.js:69 vs :77-78 differ only by the constant 1/R * RAD_TO_DEG), so both normalise to a uniform 1/n.

A THIRD KEY IS DUPLICATED TOO: fieldSampler.js:185 `    d.slopeExcludedFraction = s.excludedFraction;` — descriptors.js:209 `    excludedFraction: excluded / (W * H),` depends only on grid.mode/width/height, identical in both frames.
findings.impact: No banked number is wrong; two of them are the same number written twice. AC-CURVE-live.md's noise-floor table lists `hypsometric integral | 17.5%` and `RMS relief (uncalibrated vertical) | 30.7%` once each, so the doc author already de-duplicated by hand. The residual cost is that every raw sweep output carries three redundant keys, they inflate the descriptor count that planSweep reports over, and a reader who does not know the construction could read agreement between the two frames as corroboration when it is a tautology.
findings.fixSketch: Hoist the frame-invariant descriptors out of the loop. Compute `hypsometricIntegral`, `rmsRelief` and `slopeExcludedFraction` ONCE against `sample.grids.physical` and put them on `out` beside the existing `out.elevation` block (fieldSampler.js:197-199 already does exactly this for the distribution moments, using the physical weights only — follow that precedent). Leave in the loop only what genuinely varies: autocorrWavelength, totalArea, the spectral block, bandCount, and the slope/gradient family. Add a one-line note saying WHY they are frame-invariant (normalised area weights), so a future reader does not 'restore' them.
findings.blastRadius: Renames three keys from `physical.X`/`angular.X` to `X` in every sweep output. Nothing in code reads them by name (sweep.js discovers keys dynamically at sweep.js:69); AC-CURVE-live.md's noise-floor table names them in prose only. Check tests/instrument-sweep.test.js for any hard-coded descriptor key before landing.
findings.refuterReason: I re-derived the construction rather than accepting it, and it holds exactly. rmsReliefKm (descriptors.js:157-160) and hypsometricIntegral (:168-173) depend on the grid ONLY through areaWeights, and areaWeights (:69-79) normalises to sum 1 at :77. Equirect: cellAreaKm2 (:50-57) returns R^2 * cos(lat) * dPhi * dLambda, and the ONLY frame difference is R — radiusEarth*6371 (sampling.js:55) versus 180/pi (sampling.js:64) — a constant R^2 factor that divides out of the normalisation exactly. Patch: cellAreaKm2 (:51-53) returns (spanKmX/W)*(spanKmY/H), constant across cells, so BOTH frames normalise to a uniform 1/n regardless of whether the spans are km (sampling.js:69) or degrees (sampling.js:77-78). Hypsometric integral is (mean - min)/(max - min) with min/max weight-independent, so it too is frame-identical. The third duplicated key is confirmed: fieldSampler.js:185 emits slopeExcludedFraction from descriptors.js:209 `excludedFraction: excluded / (W * H),` which depends only on grid.mode/width/height and the latitude pole guard — identical in both frames. findings.title: Sampler cache never evicts and its dispose() is unreachable from the lab — GPU memory grows monotonically for the page's lifetime
findings.mechanism: Both clauses are true as written. The Map is insert-only with no bound; the only release path is a `dispose` that the sole caller never wires up and cannot reach, because `_fieldSampler` is a closure-local and the `_lab` surface exposes only the two sampling entry points. One correction to the title's implied scale: growth is per DISTINCT CACHE KEY, not per call. fieldSampler.js:92 keys equirect as `const key = \`eq:${width}x${height}\`;` — a single entry for the whole session at the default 256x128 — while fieldSampler.js:114 keys patches as `const key = \`patch:${latDeg},${lonDeg},${spanKm},${width}x${height},${radiusEarth}\`;`, so a new entry appears per unique (location, span, resolution, radius) tuple. Sizing: a default patch (128x128 = 16384 points → W = Hh = 128) costs ~262 KB of float render target plus ~393 KB of vertex attributes, so ~0.65 MB per key; the default 256x128 equirect (32768 points → 182x181) costs ~1.3 MB. A six-value radius sweep therefore parks ~4 MB and holds it. It is a genuine unbounded-growth defect, not a leak that will exhaust a session quickly.
findings.evidence:
NO EVICTION. fieldSampler.js:74 `  const cache = new Map();   // key -> { sampler, dirs } ; height samplers own a geometry + render target`; fieldSampler.js:76-83 `  function samplerFor(key, dirs) {` / `    let entry = cache.get(key);` / `    if (!entry) { entry = { sampler: createHeightSampler(…), dirs }; cache.set(key, entry); }` — insert-only, no size cap, no LRU, no delete anywhere in the file.

EACH ENTRY OWNS REAL GPU OBJECTS. planet-lod-rivers.js:437-444 build a BufferGeometry with two Float32Array attributes, and :447-451 allocate `new THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(W, Hh, { type: THREE.FloatType, format: THREE.RGBAFormat, … })`. planet-lod-rivers.js:472 `  function dispose() { geo.dispose(); mat.dispose(); target.dispose(); }` — the only release path.

DISPOSE IS EXPORTED BUT UNREACHABLE. fieldSampler.js:131-134 `  function dispose() {` / `    for (const { sampler } of cache.values()) sampler.dispose();` / `    cache.clear();` and :136 `  return { sampleEquirect, samplePatch, dispose, get cacheSize() { return cache.size; } };`. In the lab, `grep -n "_fieldSampler" planet-lod-lab.html` returns exactly three lines — 1528 `    let _fieldSampler = null;`, 1530 `      if (!_fieldSampler) _fieldSampler = createFieldSampler({ renderer, uniforms, octavesDuringRead: 9 });`, 1531 `      return _fieldSampler;`. The handle is module-private; the `_lab` console API exposes `sampleField` and `fieldProbe` (planet-lod-lab.html:6907, :6916) and neither dispose nor cacheSize.
findings.impact: No banked number is affected — nothing in the census, AC-CURVE or AC-SAMPLE depends on memory state, and the caching is functionally correct (the cached `dirs` are exactly the ones the key describes). The cost is operational: a long exploratory session that sweeps many radii and patch locations accumulates float render targets with no way to release them short of reloading the page, and the operator has no visibility (`cacheSize` is on the returned object but not on `_lab`). Worth noting the caching is doing real work — rebuilding a 16k-point geometry per reading would make sweeps materially slower — so the answer is bounding, not removing it.
findings.fixSketch: Two small changes. (1) Expose the handle: add `disposeFieldSampler()` and a `fieldSamplerCacheSize()` (or fold both into the existing probe return) to the `_lab` API next to sampleField/fieldProbe at planet-lod-lab.html:6907-6913, calling `_fieldSampler?.dispose()` and nulling `_fieldSampler` so the next probe rebuilds lazily as the comment at :1525-1527 intends. (2) Bound the map: give createFieldSampler a `maxCached` option (default ~8, which covers a 6-value sweep plus the equirect) and evict least-recently-used on insert, calling `entry.sampler.dispose()` on the evicted entry. Both are pure additions to fieldSampler.js's own bookkeeping — no generation code, no shader, no uniform.
findings.blastRadius: fieldSampler.js and one `_lab` entry in planet-lod-lab.html. LRU eviction can cost a geometry rebuild mid-sweep if maxCached is set below the sweep's value count, so the default must exceed the lab's default 6-value sweep (planet-lod-lab.html:6963 `const values = o.values || [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16];`). No test currently touches this (zero tests reference fieldSampler); the new tests/instrument-fieldsampler.test.js from [4]/[5] can pin eviction with a stub renderer that counts dispose() calls.
findings.refuterReason: Both clauses hold and the sizing arithmetic checks out when I redo it. fieldSampler.js:74 declares `const cache = new Map();` and :76-83 is insert-only — no cap, no LRU, and no `delete` anywhere in the file (I read all 214 lines). dispose() at :131-134 is returned at :136 alongside a cacheSize getter, and I ran the grep myself: `grep -n '_fieldSampler' planet-lod-lab.html` returns exactly three lines — 1528 (`let _fieldSampler = null;`), 1530, 1531 — so the handle never escapes the module closure, and the _lab surface exposes only sampleField (:6904) and fieldProbe (:6915). Neither dispose nor cacheSize is reachable from the console. MEMORY ARITHMETIC, redone from planet-lod-rivers.js:423 `const W = Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(N));`: equirect 256x128 = 32768 points -> W = 182, Hh = 181, RTT = 182*181*16 bytes = 527 KB, plus two Float32Array(N*3) attributes = 2*393 KB = 786 KB, total 1.31 MB — the adjudicator's '~1.3 MB' is right. Patch 128x128 = 16384 -> W = Hh = 128, RTT = 262 KB + 393 KB attributes = 0.655 MB — '~0.65 MB' right. Six-value default sweep = 3.9 MB — '~4 MB' right. The correction the adjudicator added to the title (growth is per distinct cache KEY, not per call, because fieldSampler.js:92 keys equirect only on WxH) is itself correct and improves the finding.

The adjudicator's closing judgement (bound it, do not remove it, because rebuilding a 16k-point geometry per reading would make sweeps materially slower) is sound and consistent with instrument discipline: a bound plus an exposed cacheSize/dispose on _lab is a fix outside src/worldengine/, so it does not touch generation code and cannot trip the vis-scale fence.

findings.title: responseCurve and planSweep have no in-flight guard — concurrent invocations corrupt each other's measurements and their save/restore of radius and seeds
findings.mechanism: The title asserts two distinct corruptions from missing re-entrancy control, and both hold. (1) Save/restore: if B starts while A is mid-sweep, B's `prev` snapshot at :6993 captures A's swept radius/seed as if it were the operator's world; whichever `finally` runs last writes that sweep value back as the 'restored' state, so the lab is silently left on a sweep point. (2) Measurement: A's `setPoint` sets (R=4, seed=1) and yields at :6973; B's `setPoint` sets (R=16, seed=3) during that window; A's `measure` at :6975 then reads the R=16/seed-3 field and `responseCurve` files it under `{ value: 4, seed: 1 }` (sweep.js:52-54). No error is raised — sweep.js only catches throws (:55-59), and a wrong-but-finite descriptor is not a throw. Not related to the carrier-off split.
findings.evidence:
planet-lod-lab.html:6959 `async responseCurve(opts){` … :6965 `const prev = { R: state.planetRadiusEarth, macro: state.macroSeed, detail: state.detailSeed };` … :6978 `} finally {` :6979 `state.planetRadiusEarth = prev.R;` — and the identical shape at :6987/:6993/:7003. There is no re-entrancy flag anywhere: `grep -n "_sweepBusy\|inFlight\|_busy\|_curveRunning" planet-lod-lab.html` returns nothing.
The interleaving window is explicit: :6973 `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, settleMs));` inside setPoint, and :6975 `measure: async () => window._lab.fieldProbe(probe),` — both awaits yield the event loop while `state.planetRadiusEarth` and the seeds are globals.
The documented usage block shows the intended sequential shape but nothing enforces it: :6957 `//   await _lab.planSweep({ seeds:[1,2,3,4,5] })        // how many seeds do I need?` :6958 `//   await _lab.responseCurve({ values:[2,4,8], seeds:[1,2,3,4,5] })`.
findings.impact: A silently mislabelled ensemble: points get sample means drawn from the wrong radius, which flattens or scrambles the fitted exponent while every quality indicator (n per point, SEM, `failures: []`) still reads healthy. Plus a lab left on a sweep radius/seed the operator never chose, which then contaminates whatever they do next. Reachability is operator-dependent — a console user who fires `_lab.planSweep({...})` without `await` and then types `_lab.responseCurve(...)` triggers it, and both calls take ~M×700 ms to ~N×M×700 ms, so the window is long in human terms.
findings.fixSketch: One module-scope flag guarding both entry points: `let _sweepInFlight = false;` then at the top of each `if (_sweepInFlight) throw new Error('a sweep is already running — await it before starting another');  _sweepInFlight = true;` and clear it in the existing `finally`. Throwing (not queueing) is the right call for an instrument: a second concurrent sweep is an operator error, and silently serialising it would hide the mistake. Lab-file only.
findings.blastRadius: planet-lod-lab.html :6959-6983 and :6987-7009. Behaviour change is limited to the previously-corrupt case. No test or evidence document depends on concurrent invocation.
findings.refuterReason: I could not break this one. Both asserted corruptions reconstruct from source. Save/restore: prev is captured at :6965 and :6993 from live globals, and the finally blocks write back unconditionally, so a later-finishing finally overwrites with a sweep-point value. Measurement: sweep.js:52-54 is verbatim 'await setPoint({ value, seed, index: ... }); const m = await measure({ value, seed }); samples.push(flatten(m));' - the measure result is filed under the loop's own {value, seed}, never under anything read back from the world, and the catch at :55-59 only records thrown errors, so a wrong-but-finite descriptor passes silently. The two yield points are exactly where claimed (:6973 setTimeout, :6975 measure). I independently re-ran the guard grep across the whole file for _sweepBusy|inFlight|_busy|_curveRunning|isRunning and got zero hits, so the 'no re-entrancy flag anywhere' claim survives. Duration arithmetic also checks: planSweep at 5 seeds is ~3.5 s and responseCurve at 6 values x 3 seeds is ~12.6 s, so the interleaving window is long in human terms as claimed. Nothing in tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js or the single post-07-25 lab commit (8be13ab) adds a guard.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Re-read planet-lod-lab.html:6957-7010 including the usage comment block at :6957-6958, and src/worldengine/instrument/sweep.js:40-64. Ran the guard grep myself rather than trusting the adjudicator's reported empty result. Verified sweep.js:52-54 and :55-59 line-for-line; verified the responseCurve probe is a single object reused across every point ('const probe = o.probe || {...}' at :6964, closed over by 'measure: async () => window._lab.fieldProbe(probe)' at :6975).
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: None. low is correct - console-only reachability, requires an operator to fire a second sweep without awaiting the first.

findings.title: auditLaw's reported `points` count overstates how many points the fit actually used
findings.mechanism: The title asserts `points` is the pre-fit count, not the count the fit used. Confirmed: it is exactly `points.length` after only a finiteness filter, while fitPowerLaw additionally drops every point with y <= 0 or x <= 0 and reports that in `n`/`dropped`, both thrown away at laws.js:164-171. The divergence is precisely the set {y <= 0}. Reachable two ways: (1) an AC-POSCTRL plant that zeroes a coupling — the most natural shape of a 'coupling removed' defect — e.g. `craterSchedule: brokenSchedule(() => ({ nAnalytic: 0 }))`; (2) a caller-supplied condition that closes the impact-surface gate, since auditLaws takes one (laws.js:175 `condition = {}`) and craterSchedule returns nAnalytic/D_FLOOR_KM/D_HI_KM = 0 when the gate is shut (bombardment.js:156-158). With T_eq > CRATER_T_MAX = 450 (bombardment.js:80), all 7 y values are 0, fitPowerLaw drops all 7, n = 0 < 2 so it returns NaN exponent and NaN SE (stats.js:102), lawVerdict reports UNRESOLVABLE — and the audit row says `points: 7`. NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault: laws.js is the pure-function layer, never reads the shader.
findings.evidence: laws.js:157 `if (Number.isFinite(y)) points.push({ x: value, y });` — auditLaw's own filter is finiteness only. laws.js:159 `const fit = fitPowerLaw(points, { z });`. laws.js:168 `measuredExponent: fit.exponent, measuredSE: fit.exponentSE, r2: fit.r2, points: points.length,` — the reported count is the array handed IN. fitPowerLaw applies a second, stricter filter: stats.js:96-99 `const usable = [], dropped = []; for (const p of points) { if (p.x > 0 && p.y > 0 && Number.isFinite(p.x) && Number.isFinite(p.y)) usable.push(p); else dropped.push(p); }` and returns both `n` (stats.js:153 `n, dropped: dropped.length, z,`) and `dropped`. auditLaw discards both. Nothing in tests/instrument-laws.test.js asserts on `points`, and the post-findings fix round (tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js) does not touch laws.js at all.
findings.impact: No banked number changes; laws.js has no production consumer (grep for auditLaws finds only laws.js and its test — planet-lod-lab.html never calls it), so nothing shipped emits this field. The cost is diagnostic: the one report an operator reads when a law goes UNRESOLVABLE tells them the sweep had 7 points when it had 0 usable ones, which points the investigation at 'the exponent is noisy / the sweep is too small' instead of at 'the measured quantity collapsed to zero'. That is the same class of overstated-confidence defect the review already confirmed twice in this instrument (fitPowerLaw's fabricated dof, shiftSignificance's NaN→0 coercion) — a plausible number where the honest answer is 'this did not measure anything'. It compounds with finding 19: a genuine isImpactSurface regression is the exact scenario that produces 'UNRESOLVABLE, points: 7'.
findings.fixSketch: Report the fit's own bookkeeping instead of the caller's. laws.js:168 becomes `... r2: fit.r2, points: fit.n, pointsOffered: points.length, pointsDropped: fit.dropped, nonFiniteSkipped: law.values.length - points.length,` — four numbers that already exist, zero new computation. Optionally promote a collapse to a named verdict: if `fit.n < 2`, return verdict UNRESOLVABLE with reason `'only ' + fit.n + ' of ' + law.values.length + ' sweep points were usable (non-positive or non-finite measurements)'` rather than falling through to lawVerdict's generic 'fit did not converge' (stats.js:~137). Add a test that plants `nAnalytic: 0` and asserts the reported points is 0, not 7.
findings.blastRadius: laws.js:164-171 and one new test block. `points` is a display-only field with no in-repo reader other than a human, so renaming/adding siblings breaks nothing. No banked artifact quotes it.
findings.claimAmbiguity: "Overstates" could mean (a) points.length > fit.n because of the y<=0 drop, or (b) `points` is reported even on the early-return paths where no fit happened. I adjudicated (a), the mechanically specific reading, and verified the exact filter divergence. (b) is a subset of the same fix.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives; I re-read both filters and every cited line is exact. laws.js:157 `if (Number.isFinite(y)) points.push({ x: value, y });` — finiteness only. laws.js:159 `const fit = fitPowerLaw(points, { z });`. laws.js:168 `measuredExponent: fit.exponent, measuredSE: fit.exponentSE, r2: fit.r2, points: points.length,` — verbatim, and it reports the array handed IN. stats.js:96-99 verified verbatim including the strictly stronger predicate `p.x > 0 && p.y > 0 && Number.isFinite(p.x) && Number.isFinite(p.y)`, and stats.js:153 `n, dropped: dropped.length, z,` — both discarded by auditLaw. The divergence set is exactly {y <= 0}, as claimed. Reachability chain re-verified end to end: laws.js:175 does default `condition = {}` and passes it through to baselineCondition, bombardment.js:80 does define `CRATER_T_MAX = 450`, bombardment.js:146 reads `const cold = (condition.T_eq ?? 288) < CRATER_T_MAX;`, and bombardment.js:156-158 returns nAnalytic/D_FLOOR_KM/D_HI_KM = 0 when the gate is shut — so a caller-supplied T_eq > 450 zeroes all 7 y values, fitPowerLaw drops all 7, stats.js:102 returns NaN exponent AND NaN SE at n=0, and stats.js:188-189 turns that into UNRESOLVABLE while laws.js:168 still prints `points: 7`. I confirmed this is the y<=0 path and NOT the throw path: a throw returns early at laws.js:152-155, an object that has no `points` field at all, so the two paths are correctly distinguished. Nothing in tests/instrument-laws.test.js asserts on `points` (verified by reading the file). NOT already fixed. NOT downstream of the carrier-off fault — correct, same pure-function argument as [19]. findings.title: sampleField's radiusEarth override changes the reporting frame without changing the field it reports on
findings.mechanism:
The title asserts the option relabels rather than re-worlds. Confirmed. In equirect mode the sampled directions are identical and only the km-per-degree scale changes, so the option literally re-prices the radius-1 field in radius-8 kilometres. In patch mode it additionally narrows the angular window as 1/R (sampling.js:135) — the sample is zoomed, but the world generating it is still the old one, so the claim 'without changing the field it reports on' is exact in both modes.
The sharp consequence the terse title does not spell out: `describeSample` emits `radiusEarth` as a TOP-LEVEL key (fieldSampler.js:151 `kind: sample.kind, radiusEarth: sample.radiusEarth,`) and `flatten` only strips the `meta` namespace (sweep.js:147, META_NAMESPACES :157). That top-level key IS the sweep's built-in positive control — the one AC-CURVE-live.md:85 reports as `1.0000 ± 0.0000, r² = 1.000` and calls 'proof inside every sweep that the driver actually moved'. Because `probe` is caller-supplied and passed straight through (planet-lod-lab.html:6964 → :6975 → :6916 → :6906), `_lab.responseCurve({ probe: { …, radiusEarth: v } })` is not even expressible — but `radiusEarth` fixed in the probe, or a caller that varies it, makes the control agree with a driver the shader never saw. The instrument's own integrity check is defeatable by an argument. Not a carrier-off alias — this is a plumbing/frame defect on the reporting side, orthogonal to the baked-vs-synth split.
findings.evidence:
planet-lod-lab.html:6906 — `const radiusEarth = o.radiusEarth != null ? +o.radiusEarth : state.planetRadiusEarth;` then :6909-6911 hand that value to `s.samplePatch({... radiusEarth })` / `s.sampleEquirect({... radiusEarth })`.
Inside the sampler the value is used ONLY for geometry/reporting, never for generation:
  fieldSampler.js:103 — `grids: { physical: physicalGrid(width, height, radiusEarth), angular: angularGrid(width, height) },`  → sampling.js:55 `return { mode: 'equirect', …, radiusKm: radiusEarth * R_EARTH_KM, frame: 'physical' };`
  fieldSampler.js:93 — `const dirs = cache.has(key) ? cache.get(key).dirs : equirectDirections(width, height);`  ← equirect directions do NOT take radiusEarth (sampling.js:101)
  fieldSampler.js:117 — patch mode DOES pass it to `patchDirections({ …, radiusEarth, … })` → sampling.js:128 `const R = radiusEarth * R_EARTH_KM;` :135 `const spanAngX = spanKmX / R, spanAngY = spanKmY / R;`
Meanwhile every radius→shader write keys on the real state: planet-lod-lab.html:5821 `sVis = visScaleOf(state.planetRadiusEarth);`, :5888 `uniforms.uDispDomainScale.value = sVis;`, :6258, :6274. The override reaches none of them.
And it propagates into the display frame too: planet-lod-lab.html:6918 — `const sVisNow = visScaleOf(sample.radiusEarth);` feeding `screenWavelengthProxy` and `meta.visScale` (:6930).
findings.impact: Any caller who reads `sampleField({radiusEarth: X})` as 'measure an X-Earth-radii planet' gets a fully self-consistent, entirely wrong physical answer: form wavelengths, RMS relief, total area and the on-screen proxy all scale as if the body were X, with `verticalCalibrated`, `formDetected` and the radiusEarth control all reporting normally. Nothing in the lab or the instrument warns. No banked number is affected — the default probe (planet-lod-lab.html:6964) omits `radiusEarth`, so both the census and AC-CURVE used `state.planetRadiusEarth`, and grepping the workstream evidence for a radiusEarth override finds none.
findings.fixSketch: Two options, both lab-side. Minimal: make the reporting frame honest by naming it — return `reportedAsRadiusEarth` alongside `radiusEarth` whenever the override differs from `state.planetRadiusEarth`, and have `describeSample`/`fieldProbe` carry a `frameOverridden: true` flag that `sweep.js` refuses to fit a control against. Stronger and probably right for an instrument: make the override actually set the world — `if (o.radiusEarth != null) { state.planetRadiusEarth = +o.radiusEarth; applyDrivers(); await settle; }` — or delete the parameter entirely, since nothing in the repo passes it and its only honest use (a deliberately planted reporting-frame defect) belongs behind an explicitly named control API, not a silent option on the main read path. Note the discipline constraint: this must be a lab-side change; do not push a radius argument into src/worldengine generation code.
findings.blastRadius: planet-lod-lab.html :6904-6912 and :6915-6918; fieldSampler.js :90-129 signature if the flag route is taken. Nothing in the repo currently passes `radiusEarth`, so removing or gating it breaks no caller and no test. If the 'actually set the world' route is chosen, `sampleField` becomes async and mutating — a real API break for `fieldProbe` (:6916 calls it synchronously) and worth the smaller flag fix instead.
findings.claimAmbiguity: 'without changing the field' admits a weaker reading — that patch mode's dependence on radiusEarth (sampling.js:135) does change WHICH directions are sampled, so the field-under-measurement is not literally identical. I adjudicated the stronger and intended reading: the GENERATED field (the shader state) is untouched in both modes, and patch mode's window change is a zoom, not a different world — which if anything makes the option more misleading, not less.
findings.refuterReason: Refuted on the load-bearing sub-claims, not on the headline. Every file:line the adjudicator quoted is genuine and verbatim - :6906 'const radiusEarth = o.radiusEarth != null ? +o.radiusEarth : state.planetRadiusEarth;', :6909-6911 handing it to samplePatch/sampleEquirect, :6918 'const sVisNow = visScaleOf(sample.radiusEarth);', :6930 'visScale: sVisNow,', fieldSampler.js:93 (equirect dirs ignore radiusEarth), :103 (physicalGrid consumes it), :117 (patchDirections consumes it), :151 'kind: sample.kind, radiusEarth: sample.radiusEarth,', sweep.js:147 and :157, sampling.js:55/101/128/135, and AC-CURVE-live.md:85 really is the '1.0000 +/- 0.0000, r2 = 1.000' control row. So the frame-vs-field split is exactly as described and the option is undocumented in the API's own usage block (:6901-6903 lists no radiusEarth). That is a real API footgun. But the adjudicator built its medium severity on the integrity-check-defeat story, and that story inverts under the shipped call shape, and on an impact list that includes a quantity the weighting provably makes scale-invariant. Reachability is also nil in practice: no shipped caller passes radiusEarth, and I grepped the workstream evidence directory myself - no radiusEarth override appears anywhere.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Re-read planet-lod-lab.html:6887-6935 with exact offsets (I recomputed line numbers by offsetting a sed window rather than trusting the quotes), src/worldengine/instrument/fieldSampler.js:73-160, sampling.js:50-56/98-106/125-140, sweep.js:139-157, descriptors.js:69-79 (areaWeights) and :157-161 (rmsReliefKm), and AC-CURVE-live.md:80-85. The one substantive divergence found: the adjudicator's fieldSampler.js:121 gloss for the patch return is on line 121 for the field list but line 120 for the 'return {' - cosmetic. The substantive errors are the two reasoning failures above, not citation fabrication.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: medium -> low. The core mechanism survives, but the two claims the adjudicator used to lift it to medium do not. (a) 'the instrument's own integrity check is defeatable by an argument' is wrong for the shipped path. The adjudicator itself concedes a per-point radiusEarth is 'not even expressible' through responseCurve, then asserts that 'radiusEarth fixed in the probe' also defeats the control. It does the opposite: probe is a single object reused at every point (:6964 closed over by :6975), so sample.radiusEarth would be CONSTANT across the sweep and the control would fit exponent 0, not 1 - a loud, unmissable failure of the very check it is claimed to defeat. The only genuine defeat needs a bespoke harness that varies radiusEarth per point, which no shipped caller can do. (b) The impact list is arithmetically wrong on RMS relief. descriptors.js:157-160 computes it via areaWeights(grid), and areaWeights normalises ('if (sum > 0) for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) w[k] /= sum;' at :77), so RMS relief is INVARIANT to radiusKm in equirect mode; in patch mode the physical grid never sees radiusEarth at all (fieldSampler.js:125 physicalPatchGrid(width,height,spanKm,spanKm)). 'total area' does scale as R^2 and the wavelengths and on-screen proxy do move, so the mechanism holds - but the blast radius is smaller than stated.

findings.title: The patch sampler cache is keyed on radiusEarth and the lab exposes no way to dispose it
findings.mechanism: Both halves are confirmed, and the causal join the title is making is right: because radiusEarth is (correctly) part of the patch key, the cache necessarily grows by one entry per swept radius, and because dispose() is unreachable, nothing ever gives those entries back. Neither half is a bug on its own — the keying is required for correctness (a 2000 km patch on a 0.5 R⊕ body spans four times the arc it does on an 8 R⊕ body, so reusing directions across radii would silently sample the wrong footprint), and a cache that never evicts is only a problem if it can be fed. It is the combination that makes a radius sweep the natural growth driver. This is the same underlying defect as finding [30], stated from the key-cardinality side rather than the eviction side.
findings.evidence:
THE KEY INCLUDES radiusEarth. fieldSampler.js:114 — `    const key = \`patch:${latDeg},${lonDeg},${spanKm},${width}x${height},${radiusEarth}\`;` — and fieldSampler.js:115-117 recompute directions on a miss: `    const dirs = cache.has(key)` / `      ? cache.get(key).dirs` / `      : patchDirections({ latDeg, lonDeg, spanKmX: spanKm, spanKmY: spanKm, radiusEarth, width, height });`.

RADIUS GENUINELY BELONGS IN THE KEY. sampling.js:127-135 — `export function patchDirections({ latDeg, lonDeg, spanKmX, spanKmY, radiusEarth, width, height }) {` / `  const R = radiusEarth * R_EARTH_KM;` … `  const spanAngX = spanKmX / R, spanAngY = spanKmY / R;` — a fixed km span subtends a different angle on a different body, so the directions really do depend on radius. Contrast fieldSampler.js:92-93, where the equirect key correctly omits it because equirectDirections(width, height) does not use radius.

NO DISPOSE PATH. Same evidence as finding [30]: fieldSampler.js:131-136 returns `dispose`; `grep -n "_fieldSampler" planet-lod-lab.html` yields only :1528, :1530, :1531 — the handle never escapes, and the `_lab` API at planet-lod-lab.html:6907/:6916 exposes only sampleField and fieldProbe.

THE SWEEP MULTIPLIES THE KEYS. planet-lod-lab.html:6963 `                      const values = o.values || [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16];` with :6969-6970 setting `state.planetRadiusEarth = value;` and :6976 measuring via `window._lab.fieldProbe(probe)` at a fixed patch geometry — one distinct cache key per radius.
findings.impact: No banked number is affected. The keying is correct, so every reading in AC-CURVE-live.md and AC-SAMPLE-live.md used directions matching its own radius — importantly, a defect in the OPPOSITE direction (caching directions across radii) would have corrupted the whole radius sweep, and it does not exist. The cost is the same bounded accumulation as [30]: the banked six-value default sweep parks about six patch entries (~4 MB) that survive for the page's life.
findings.fixSketch: Same fix as [30] — there is one change to make, not two. Expose dispose (and cacheSize) on the `_lab` surface beside sampleField/fieldProbe, and give the Map an LRU bound sized above the default 6-value sweep. Do NOT 'fix' the key by dropping radiusEarth: fieldSampler.js:114 is correct and sampling.js:128-135 is the reason. Add a comment at :114 saying so, since the key looks like over-specification and is the exact thing a future simplification pass would strip.
findings.blastRadius: Identical to [30] — fieldSampler.js plus one `_lab` entry. Treat [30] and [34] as a single fix so the eviction bound and the dispose exposure land together.
findings.claimAmbiguity: The title juxtaposes the radius keying and the missing dispose without stating the connection. I adjudicated the reading in which the keying is the growth DRIVER for the un-disposable cache (which is coherent and correct). I explicitly rejected the alternative reading — that keying on radiusEarth is itself the defect — because sampling.js:128-135 shows the directions genuinely depend on radius, so omitting it would be the real bug.
findings.refuterReason: Both halves confirmed and the causal join is right. fieldSampler.js:114 is verbatim `const key = \`patch:${latDeg},${lonDeg},${spanKm},${width}x${height},${radiusEarth}\`;` and :115-117 recompute directions on a miss. Radius genuinely belongs in that key: sampling.js:127-135 computes `const R = radiusEarth * R_EARTH_KM;` then `const spanAngX = spanKmX / R, spanAngY = spanKmY / R;`, so a fixed-km span subtends a different arc on a different body — the contrast with fieldSampler.js:92-93, where the equirect key correctly omits radius because equirectDirections(width, height) never uses it, is exact and is the sharpest part of the entry. The dispose half is the same evidence as [30], which I re-verified independently. The sweep really does multiply the keys: the default radius list is [0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16] at a fixed patch geometry, so exactly six distinct keys accumulate.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: Read fieldSampler.js:107-137 and sampling.js:113-150 in full. Ran the _fieldSampler grep myself. Grepped exact line numbers for the sweep: the default values array is planet-lod-lab.html:6961 (adjudicator cited :6963), `state.planetRadiusEarth = value;` is :6971 (cited :6969-6970), and `measure: async () => window._lab.fieldProbe(probe),` is :6975 (cited :6976). All three are off by roughly two lines in a consistent direction — the quoted TEXT is verbatim and correct, so this is systematic counting drift, not fabrication, but it is the same drift pattern I found in [17] and [30] and it should be flagged to whoever consumes these entries.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: None. Severity low and changesBankedResult:false stand. The adjudicator's strongest observation is one worth preserving: a defect in the OPPOSITE direction — caching directions ACROSS radii — would have silently corrupted every row of AC-CURVE-live.md and AC-SAMPLE-live.md by sampling a different physical footprint at each radius, and that defect does not exist. This finding is [30] restated from the key-cardinality side; the two should be fixed as one change (bound the cache, expose dispose/cacheSize on _lab) rather than tracked separately.

findings.title: shiftSignificance on single-sample ensembles reports sigma = Infinity, and no test covers it
findings.mechanism: The title asserts (a) single-sample ensembles produce sigma = Infinity and (b) no test covers it. Both were true at 399d2f3 and both are now false. This finding is the low-severity duplicate of the review's own CONFIRMED medium finding 'shiftSignificance coerces a NaN standard error to zero, so single-sample ensembles report significant movement' (same file, same line region) — the confirmed one carried the full body and got the fix; this notVerified title is the same defect stated from the symptom side. The fix rewrote the NaN-coercion (`a.sem || 0`, where NaN is falsy) into an explicit undecidable branch. One residual worth naming, but it is NOT what the title claims: stats.js:244-247 still returns `sigma: Infinity` for the case where BOTH ensembles have n>=2 and genuinely measured sd = 0 with a non-zero delta (`shiftSignificance([10,10],[11,11])` → `{moved:true, sigma:Infinity}`). That branch is deliberate and documented in place (:245 'Genuinely zero MEASURED spread on both sides (n>=2, sd===0) — a real, if unusual, certainty'), and it is not a single-sample ensemble — but it is genuinely uncovered by any test (grep for Infinity across tests/instrument-*.test.js returns only a comment at instrument-review-fixes.test.js:186). No link to the carrier-off / LEGACY-synth split.
findings.evidence:
Pre-fix code, `git show 399d2f3:src/worldengine/instrument/stats.js` — `const combined = Math.sqrt((a.sem || 0) ** 2 + (b.sem || 0) ** 2);` … `if (!(combined > 0)) { return { moved: delta !== 0, delta, sigma: delta === 0 ? 0 : Infinity, … }; }` — exactly the reported behaviour.
Current code, src/worldengine/instrument/stats.js:236-242 — `if (!Number.isFinite(a.sem) || !Number.isFinite(b.sem)) {` / `return { moved: null, delta, sigma: NaN, baseline: a, current: b, z,` / `reason: 'at least one ensemble has fewer than 2 samples, so its uncertainty is unknown — a shift cannot be tested (this is undecidable, NOT "no shift" and NOT "shifted")',`. This guard sits BEFORE the `!(combined > 0)` branch at :244, so a single-sample ensemble (meanSEM returns `sem: NaN` for n<2 at stats.js:59) can no longer reach the Infinity path.
The test that pins it: tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js:187-191 — `const s = shiftSignificance([10.0], [10.0000001]);` / `expect(s.moved).toBe(null);` / `expect(Number.isNaN(s.sigma)).toBe(true);` / `expect(s.reason).toMatch(/fewer than 2 samples|undecidable/i);`, plus the mixed case at :194 `expect(s.moved).toBe(null);        // previously moved:true at sigma 4.39`.
Fix commit: `git log -1 0744fa4` → `2026-07-25 02:54:20 -0400  nonvisual-analysis-channel: fix 7 defects found by adversarial review + correct 3 evidence docs` — landed after the findings were written.
Verified by running the current module read-only: `shiftSignificance([10.0],[10.0000001])` → `{moved:null, sigma:NaN, reason:'at least one ensemble has fewer than 2 samples…'}`.
findings.impact: None today. The claimed defect is gone from current source and pinned against regression. Even before the fix the blast radius was zero on shipped output — shiftSignificance has no production caller (it is not referenced from planet-lod-lab.html, sweep.js or laws.js; the only non-test reference is its own definition), which is why the reviewer downgraded the confirmed twin from high to medium. No banked number was ever produced by this function.
findings.fixSketch: Nothing to fix for the claim as stated. If the residual matters to the owner, the cheap addition is a test pinning stats.js:244-247 explicitly — assert `shiftSignificance([10,10],[10,10])` gives `{moved:false, sigma:0}` and `shiftSignificance([10,10],[11,11])` gives `{moved:true, sigma:Infinity}` — so that the one remaining Infinity path is a documented, tested choice rather than an untested corner. Pure test addition; no src/ change, no DI, no fence risk.

findings.title: The planted-defect tests prove containment, not specificity — each defect is surgically confined to one output by construction
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the specificity assertions are true by construction. Broadly yes: `expect(audit.summary.fail).toEqual(['crater-count-independent-of-gravity'])` (:118), `toEqual(['crater-size-vs-gravity'])` (:127), `toEqual(['relief-envelope-vs-gravity'])` (:153, :162) cannot fail, because the corrupted key is read by only one law whose driver the corruption depends on. One partial defence for the suite, which I checked rather than assumed: the g^0.34 defect DOES touch `nAnalytic`, which two laws read, and it correctly trips only the gravity one — because `crater-count-vs-radius` sweeps R at fixed g, so the corruption is a constant the log-log fit absorbs into the intercept. That is a genuine (small) discrimination, not pure construction. But no planted defect in the suite perturbs a quantity that varies across two laws' driver ranges, so the audit's ability to avoid a false alarm on an unrelated law has never actually been tested against a defect capable of causing one. Separately worth naming for Max's lead: this whole layer audits pure functions and says so (laws.js:185-188, 'a drift guard, not an independent physical validation, and not evidence that the law reaches the render'). No amount of strengthening these positive controls would catch the carrier-off fault, which is precisely a law-does-not-reach-the-render fault owned by the field layer.
findings.evidence: Every planted defect goes through one wrapper — tests/instrument-laws.test.js:89-92: `const brokenSchedule = (corrupt) => (c) => { const s = craterSchedule(c); return { ...s, ...corrupt(s, c) }; };` — and each `corrupt` overwrites exactly one key: `nAnalytic` (:97-99), `sizeMul: 1` (:125), `D_FLOOR_KM: 42` (:142), `nAnalytic / radiusEarth` (:133), plus a whole-function swap of `reliefEnvelope` (:150, :160). The registry (src/worldengine/instrument/laws.js:63-132) reads exactly one output per law: `.sizeMul` (:72), `.nAnalytic` (:87, :97), `.D_FLOOR_KM` (:108), `.D_HI_KM` (:118), `reliefEnvelope(...)` (:130). I executed all four schedule defects: each produces `FAIL: [one law]`. Then I planted a defect of the shape a real bug takes — one wrong shared INPUT, `craterSchedule({...c, radiusEarth: Math.sqrt(c.radiusEarth)})` — and it fails three laws at once: `["crater-count-vs-radius","mesh-floor-vs-radius","basin-cap-vs-radius"]`. The suite contains no defect of that class.
findings.impact: It qualifies how much the banked bombardment row's confidence tag is worth. RADIUS-CENSUS.md marks bombardment '✅ WIRED (strongest) | LAW-AUDITED' on the strength of '6 planted defects each caught by name'. The defects were caught by name, but naming was pre-guaranteed by the injection shape, so the row demonstrates that the audit fires, not that it discriminates. No exponent in the row moves.
findings.fixSketch: Add one positive control of the cross-cutting class: inject `craterSchedule: (c) => craterSchedule({ ...c, radiusEarth: Math.sqrt(c.radiusEarth) })` and assert `audit.summary.fail` equals exactly the three radius-driven laws and that the two gravity-driven laws still PASS. That tests discrimination in the direction it can actually fail (an alarm that spreads too wide, and one that stays correctly narrow) rather than in the direction the construction already guarantees. A second useful control: corrupt a value one law reads with a perturbation keyed on the OTHER law's driver (e.g. scale `D_FLOOR_KM` by g^0.2) and assert mesh-floor-vs-radius still PASSes — proving the audit does not alarm on an off-driver change. Both are dependency injection only; no generation source is edited, so AC-POSCTRL discipline holds.
findings.blastRadius: tests/instrument-laws.test.js only. If the new cross-cutting control turns up an unexpected extra FAIL, that is a finding about the registry's driver ranges, not a test bug — treat it as a result.
findings.refuterReason: The verdict survives — but ONE LOAD-BEARING PIECE OF THE ADJUDICATOR'S REASONING IS WRONG, in the direction that makes the finding STRONGER. The adjudicator offered a partial defence of the suite: 'the g^0.34 defect DOES touch nAnalytic, which two laws read, and it correctly trips only the gravity one — because crater-count-vs-radius sweeps R at fixed g, so the corruption is a constant the log-log fit absorbs into the intercept ... That is a genuine (small) discrimination, not pure construction.' It is NOT a genuine discrimination. baselineCondition() sets surfaceGravity: G_REF (I printed it: 0.5, and G_REF = 0.5), so for the radius laws the injected factor is Math.pow(G_REF/G_REF, 0.34) = EXACTLY 1. The corruption is a strict no-op on those laws, not a constant the fit has to absorb. So the one case the adjudicator credited as evidence of discrimination is pure construction after all, and the finding's core claim ('each defect is surgically confined to one output by construction') is more completely true than the adjudicator allowed. Everything else reproduces: I ran all four schedule defects (each -> FAIL on exactly one law), and I ran the shared-INPUT defect craterSchedule({...c, radiusEarth: Math.sqrt(c.radiusEarth)}) and got summary.fail = ['crater-count-vs-radius','mesh-floor-vs-radius','basin-cap-vs-radius'] — three at once, exactly as claimed, and the suite contains no defect of that class.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: tests/instrument-laws.test.js:89-92 brokenSchedule wrapper EXACT. Specificity assertions :118, :127, :153, :162 all EXACT (`toEqual(['crater-count-independent-of-gravity'])`, `toEqual(['crater-size-vs-gravity'])`, `toEqual(['relief-envelope-vs-gravity'])` twice). Corruption sites :97-99 (nAnalytic * (g/G_REF)^0.34), :125 (sizeMul: 1), :133 (nAnalytic / radiusEarth), :142 (D_FLOOR_KM: 42), :150 (-0.3) and :160 (-0.52) all EXACT. laws.js registry :63-132 read in full; single-output reads confirmed at :72 (.sizeMul), :87 and :97 (.nAnalytic), :108 (.D_FLOOR_KM), :118 (.D_HI_KM), :130 (reliefEnvelope(...)). laws.js:185-188 layerNote EXACT, including 'a drift guard, not an independent physical validation, and not evidence that the law reaches the render.' RADIUS-CENSUS.md bombardment row verified verbatim including 'All 6 laws PASS exactly; 6 planted defects each caught by name.' Executed: baselineCondition({radiusEarth:2}).surfaceGravity = 0.5, G_REF = 0.5, factor = 1 — this is the check that refutes the adjudicator's partial defence.
findings.refuterSeverityCorrection: LOW stands as the severity, but the adjudicator's mechanism narrative needs correcting before it is carried forward: the g^0.34 defect is a literal no-op on the two radius laws (multiplier exactly 1.0), so the suite demonstrates ZERO cross-law discrimination, not 'a genuine (small) discrimination'. The finding is stronger than adjudicated, not weaker. Its impact framing is right and I endorse it: the census row 'WIRED (strongest) | LAW-AUDITED' rests on defects whose by-name naming was pre-guaranteed by the injection shape, so the row shows the audit FIRES, not that it DISCRIMINATES. No exponent in the row moves.

findings.title: The crater-SFD shallow-slope test admits any answer above -1.8 for a population whose true slope is -1.5
findings.mechanism: The title asserts the assertion is unbounded above. It is. `craterSFD` recovers the input exponent to within 0.4% (-1.4940 against -1.5), so a two-sided bracket of [-1.6, -1.4] would be comfortable — the loose bound buys nothing. The companion ordering assertion `steep < shallow` is also weak: steep measures -2.988, which is below anything the shallow bound admits, so ordering is satisfied by any shallow value greater than -2.988. A planted defect that flattened the SFD fit (e.g. dropping the log10 on the diameter axis, or fitting count instead of cumulative count) would pass this test while failing the -2 test — asymmetric coverage in a suite whose stated premise (file header, :4-7) is 'every fixture here is analytic: ... a crater population built to an exact -2 cumulative slope'.
findings.evidence: tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:272-277 — `const shallow = craterSFD(population(1.5, 4000), 1e6).slope;` then :275 `expect(shallow).toBeGreaterThan(-1.8);` and :276 `expect(steep).toBeLessThan(shallow);`. One-sided, with no upper bound at all. Executed: b=1.5 recovers -1.4940, b=1.0 recovers -0.9960, b=0.5 recovers -0.4980, b=3 recovers -2.9880. So the assertion cannot distinguish the -1.5 population from a -1.0 or a -0.5 one, nor from a slope of 0 or +5. Contrast the sibling test at :266-270, which brackets the -2 case on both sides: `expect(sfd.slope).toBeLessThan(-1.8); expect(sfd.slope).toBeGreaterThan(-2.2);`.
findings.impact: Test-only, and on a descriptor with no live caller. `craterSFD` is referenced nowhere outside tests — grep over src/, planet-lod-lab.html and planet-lod-*.js returns only tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js. The banked bombardment row in RADIUS-CENSUS.md ('All 6 laws PASS exactly') comes from laws.js auditing bombardment.js pure functions, not from craterSFD. So this is dormant-code test weakness.
findings.fixSketch: Bracket it like the -2 case: `expect(shallow).toBeLessThan(-1.3); expect(shallow).toBeGreaterThan(-1.7);` (measured -1.4940 sits mid-band), and keep `steep < shallow` as an ordering check. Optionally tighten steep to [-3.2, -2.8] too, since it measures -2.9880.
findings.blastRadius: One test block. Nothing else.
findings.refuterReason: Verdict survives on my own execution. I ran craterSFD against the exact fixture population and reproduced every recovered slope to the digit: b=3 -> -2.98804795086103, b=2 -> -1.9920319672406863, b=1.5 -> -1.494023975430515, b=1 -> -0.9960159836203432, b=0.5 -> -0.4980079918101716. So the metric recovers -1.5 to 0.40% and the assertion `shallow > -1.8` admits -1.0, -0.5, 0, or +5 alike. The companion `steep < shallow` is satisfied by anything above -2.988, which the -1.8 bound already dominates, so it adds exactly nothing. The asymmetry against the sibling test at :266-270 (which brackets on both sides) is real. Dormancy is verified rather than asserted: grep over src/, planet-lod-lab.html and every planet-lod-*.js returns craterSFD only in descriptors.js:484 (the definition) and tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js — zero live callers.
findings.refuterEvidenceChecked: tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:274 = `const shallow = craterSFD(population(1.5, 4000), 1e6).slope;`, :275 = `expect(shallow).toBeGreaterThan(-1.8);`, :276 = `expect(steep).toBeLessThan(shallow);          // steeper population = more negative slope` — all EXACT. Sibling :268-269 = `expect(sfd.slope).toBeLessThan(-1.8); expect(sfd.slope).toBeGreaterThan(-2.2);` EXACT. All 6 laws PASS exactly; 6 planted defects each caught by name.' — that row is sourced from laws.js auditing bombardment.js, and craterSFD appears nowhere in laws.js (I read the whole registry, :63-132). git log shows no post-2026-07-25 commits to either file, so ALREADY_FIXED is excluded.
