The one illustrative claim I could not fully verify is 'a defect that flattened the SFD fit ... would pass this test while failing the -2 test'; it is plausible from the fit's structure but the adjudicator did not plant it, so treat that sentence as reasoning rather than measurement.

clusterNotes.stats:
Three findings, three different dispositions, and only one of them is worth acting on before the next sweep.

ORDER OF WORK. [10] first (it moves a banked column and an upstream doc), [25] second (cheap, latent, no banked impact), [35] not at all beyond an optional test.

[10] IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, AND IT REACHES FURTHER BACK THAN stats.js. The 2x under-size is not a coding slip — stats.js:82-85 faithfully reproduces DIAGNOSIS.md:208's published arithmetic, and tests/instrument-descriptors.test.js:451-453 pins that arithmetic to DIAGNOSIS.md's text verbatim ("M(2-sigma resolve 15%): cons 10.7 -> >=11"). So the error originates in the read-gate post-mortem and was promoted into the instrument on purpose. That means fixing stats.js makes the module disagree with the document it cites as its source; DIAGNOSIS.md needs an erratum in the same change or the next reader will "fix" it back. The internal contradiction is exact and inside one file: stats.js:243 combines two ensembles' SEMs in quadrature (`Math.hypot(a.sem, b.sem)`) while stats.js:84 sizes M against a single SEM, and DIAGNOSIS.md:181-182 describes the intended procedure as comparing per-radius means and checking CI overlap — i.e. the two-ensemble case. The module contains two definitions of "resolve" and ships the looser one in the planning function.

WHAT [10] DOES AND DOES NOT INVALIDATE. It moves the last column of AC-CURVE-live.md:52-60 (every entry roughly doubles) and DIAGNOSIS.md's 11/19 → 22/38. It does NOT move a single measured exponent: the AC-CURVE sweep ran M=5, and the descriptor carrying the headline result (form wavelength, CV 8.8%) needs 3 seeds under the corrected rule versus 2 under the current one. The corrected numbers still clear the seeds actually used, so "the 15% bar is measurable" survives — with a 1.7x margin instead of 2.5x. No re-run of the sweep is required; a re-derivation of one printed column and one erratum are. RADIUS-CENSUS.md and the R1 statusNote contain no seedsToResolve figures and are untouched.

[25] IS REAL AND UNREACHABLE, WHICH IS THE HONEST SUMMARY. I reproduced fabricated exponents of exactly −1 and exactly +2 from degenerate x by calling the real module, and the guard's absolute 1e−15 bar fails even at uniform weight 1 (the finding's "weight-scaled" framing understates it). But every live caller passes distinct, factor-2-spaced driver values, so no banked number has ever entered the regime. Two mitigations bound it further: with n=2 the dof=0 guard (stats.js:133-136) already returns NaN SE, and with n>=3 degenerate x the resulting SE is NaN or ~1e7, so lawVerdict reports UNRESOLVABLE rather than a false PASS/FAIL. Fix it because it is four lines and the instrument's whole thesis is that plausible numbers are the enemy — not because anything measured is wrong.

[35] IS A DUPLICATE, NOT A SURVIVOR. It is the symptom-side restatement of the review's own CONFIRMED finding "shiftSignificance coerces a NaN standard error to zero"; that one carried a body, got fixed in 0744fa4 (2026-07-25 02:54), and is pinned at tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js:187-196. Both halves of the title ("reports sigma = Infinity" and "no test covers it") are now false. Expect other notVerified titles in the 38 to be similar aliases of the 7 confirmed — checking each against instrument-review-fixes.test.js first is the cheapest triage move available.

CARRIER-OFF LEAD: NEGATIVE FOR THIS CLUSTER. None of the three is downstream of, masked by, or an alias of the carrier-off / LEGACY-synth split. stats.js is field-agnostic — it consumes numbers and returns numbers, and would produce identically-shaped defects on any input. The one indirect contact point is worth naming so it is not double-counted: the CVs that AC-CURVE-live.md's noise-floor table feeds into seedsToResolve were measured on whatever field fieldSampler actually reads, which is finding [1]'s territory. If [1] is real, those CVs are measured on the synth body rather than the rendered relief and the whole table's INPUTS are wrong — but that is [1]'s fault propagating, independent of and compounding with [10]'s formula error. If both are real, the seeds-to-resolve column is wrong twice over, for unrelated reasons, and re-deriving it needs [1] settled first.
clusterNotes.sweep:
All three findings are REAL and all three live in the same 40-line function (sweep.js:90-132) plus its one predicate (sweep.js:168-170). None is downstream of the carrier-off / LEGACY-synth fault: planSweep is frame-agnostic arithmetic over whatever descriptors arrive, so if finding [1] is right and the instrument is measuring the synth body rather than the baked relief, these three describe the noise of the wrong field but are not themselves caused by that split. Nothing here was touched by the 2026-07-25 fix round — tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js covers descriptors.js and stats.js only (spectralExcessPeak, fitPowerLaw dof, mixed weights, tCritical95, shiftSignificance) and never imports sweep.js. So no ALREADY_FIXED verdicts are available in this cluster.

THE ONE RESULT WORTH ESCALATING — [11] and [12] compound, and the compounding is demonstrable on a banked number. The banked AC-CURVE-live noise-floor table's headline of 26 seeds is driven by elevation max at CV 75.9%. Because cvIsMeaningful's cut-off is exactly cv = 1 (sweep.js:169 with stats.js:62), and because an 8-seed pilot estimates cv to a 95% range of [0.330, 1.724] at that true value, Monte-Carlo (400k trials) puts P(that descriptor is silently censored from the headline on any given pilot) at 21.1% — 24.8% at the lab's default 5 seeds. Had it landed on the wrong side, the banked headline would have read 5 seeds instead of 26 (a 5x under-size), the plan would have shown no sign that anything was missing beyond a key in a list, and elevation max would have been captioned 'mean sits within one standard deviation of zero' — false for a positive-definite quantity. That is the read-gate failure mode (a bar set below the instrument's own floor) reproduced inside the very function written to prevent it.

WHAT IS NOT AT RISK, stated plainly so the escalation is not over-read: the banked radius exponents survive untouched. Every fitted number in AC-CURVE-live.md and the RADIUS-CENSUS substrate/relief row rides form wavelength, whose CV is 0.088; simulated at the pilot size actually used, its seedsToMeasure is 1 with a 95% range of [1, 1], so the M = 5 sweep was correctly sized by a wide margin. Only the seed-count COLUMNS of the noise-floor table need a correction block (finding [12]), and no exponent, no r-squared, and no census verdict moves. Nothing in the R1 contract statusNote depends on a planSweep seed count.

SUGGESTED ORDER OF FIXES, all inside sweep.js (plus a chi-square table in stats.js), all honouring the read-only-on-generation-code discipline: (1) [11] first — it is the one with a live failure mode, and re-basing the predicate on |mean| vs z*sem rather than vs sd is what makes the headline mean what its name says; (2) [12] second — it is additive (new interval fields, no existing value changes) and it is what makes the [11] fix legible, since the interval is precisely what tells a reader that a cv of 0.76 from 8 seeds could have been 1.7; (3) [24] last, and consider fixing the upstream `radiusEarth` / `verticalCalibrated` namespace leak (a separate finding on this list) BEFORE it, because that removes two of [24]'s three guaranteed live instances and may shrink the fix to a one-branch addition. One shared constraint on all three: sweep.js sits under src/worldengine/, which tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:64-66 greps with /visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP/ including comments — a fix that merely mentions those tokens in a new comment breaks the fence.
clusterNotes.lab-api:
All four are REAL; none of them moves a banked number; none is `ALREADY_FIXED` by the post-findings round. `tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js` covers only `descriptors.js` and `stats.js` — it does not touch `planet-lod-lab.html` at all, so no lab-API finding could have been retired by it.

SHARED ROOT CAUSE — the lab API's sweep functions treat the lab as if its state were a pure function of `state`, when in fact the lab is a rAF state machine. Every one of [2], [18], [31] is a variant of that single mistake:
- [2] assumes writing `state.planetRadiusEarth` + `applyDrivers()` puts the world in that state, when the actual GPU write happens later, in `frame()`.
- [18] assumes only what the sweep explicitly wrote needs restoring, when `frame()` also mutates `state.distance` on the sweep's behalf.
- [31] assumes single-threaded exclusivity over that same global state.
A single structural fix retires all three: give the sweeps one shared preamble/epilogue that (a) takes an in-flight lock, (b) snapshots the full mutable view state (R, seeds, distance, holdApparentSize), and (c) settles on `await nextFrame()` — the exact three things `renderDeltaSweep` (planet-lod-lab.html:5376-5410) already does correctly. FIX ORDER: [2] first (it is the only one that can produce a wrong number), then [18]+[31] together as part of the shared preamble. [33] is independent and can be done any time.

THE HIGHEST-VALUE OBSERVATION, and it cuts across [2], [31] and [33] together: **the sweep's built-in positive control is weaker than the AC-CURVE document claims.** AC-CURVE-live.md:41-44 calls the `radiusEarth` fit at 1.0000 'proof inside every sweep that the driver actually moved… a sweep where this control is not exactly 1 is broken.' But that descriptor is copied out of JS state (planet-lod-lab.html:6906 → fieldSampler.js:97/121 → describeSample:151), never read back from the GPU. It therefore proves only that `state.planetRadiusEarth` moved — it is blind to whether the shader ever saw the move ([2]), and it is settable by an argument ([33]). It does happen to catch [31], because interleaving would desynchronise set-radius from read-radius. Recommend the control be upgraded to something GPU-observable (e.g. read back a uniform-derived scalar in the same RTT pass) before it is quoted as proof again.

WHY THE BANKED NUMBERS STAND ANYWAY, positively rather than by assumption: the AC-CURVE physical exponent 0.4583 ± 0.0148 is itself the receipt that the rAF loop ran during that sweep. With frames running, `uDispDomainScale = sVis = √R` makes the analytic body's angular wavelength ∝ R^-0.5, and physical λ = angular λ × R gives R^+0.5 — which is what was measured. With frames suspended (the [2] failure) the field would be angularly frozen while `patchDirections` narrowed the window as 1/R, yielding R^+1.0. The banked value is unambiguously the frames-ran branch. Independently, the exact 1.0000 control rules out the [31] interleaving, and no banked evidence passes a `radiusEarth` override, ruling out [33]. So: fix the bugs, but do NOT re-run the census or AC-CURVE on account of this cluster.

CARRIER-OFF LEAD: none of the four is downstream of it, and I want to be precise about why, because [2] sits one line away from looking like it. `uReliefBakeStrength = grainCarveUI.reliefBakeStrength * bakeReliefCrossover(sVis)` is written at planet-lod-lab.html:5898, in the same frame-loop block as the radius couplings — so the carrier-off state is also rAF-established. But the instrument's field is `ROUTER_MAIN` (planet-lod-rivers.js:317-357), whose `main()` calls `fbmd(vPos, uOctaves, fwBase)` directly and never touches `uReliefBakeStrength` or the relief cube; the baked/synth blend exists only in the lab's own planet shader at planet-lod-lab.html:381-385. So finding [1] is structurally true independent of the frame loop — the instrument samples the synth body at ALL sVis, including sVis = 1 where the crossover is exactly 1 and the planet is fully baked. That strengthens Max's lead rather than weakening it: the split is not a radius-dependent fade in the instrument, it is a permanent architectural divergence between the router field and the render field.
clusterNotes.instrument-tests:
SHAPE OF THE CLUSTER. All 7 are test-quality findings, and none of them changes a banked number. Every one of RADIUS-CENSUS.md, AC-CURVE-live.md and AC-SAMPLE-live.md survives this cluster intact — the defective quantities either have no live caller at all (craterSFD, networkLengthKm, drainageDensity: grep over src/, planet-lod-lab.html and planet-lod-*.js returns only test references), or are computed on a grid mode the banked sweeps never used (descriptors.js bandCount and areaWeights fire only on equirect samples, while planet-lod-lab.html:6963 and :6991 both default `probe = { mode: 'patch', ... }`), or are synthetic headless fixtures with no lab path at all ([20], [36]). Nothing here is a reason to re-run a measurement. That is the headline, and I state it plainly because the cluster reads scarier than it is.

WHAT SURVIVED AND WHAT DID NOT. One ALREADY_FIXED ([3], verified by executing the fixture at shipped defaults — 1.502 sigma against a 4.5 bar, so the override is now vestigial). Six REAL, all confidence high, all substantiated by execution against the real modules rather than by inspection. Three of the titles quote a number and all three reproduced to the digit: [20]'s "0.7% inside the FAIL boundary" measured 0.71% (dClaim/tol = 0.9929), [23]'s "92% of its tolerance" measured 91.6% (0.4582 of 0.5), and [22]'s inflation reproduced as 2 bands -> 3 on a single flipped row. Whoever wrote these terse titles had actually run the code; they should be read as measured claims, not as impressions.

CARRIER-OFF LEAD. None of the 7 is downstream of, masked by, or an alias of the carrier-off / LEGACY-synth split. That fault lives in WHAT FIELD gets sampled (fieldSampler.js / the lab probe), which is finding [1]'s territory; this cluster is entirely about what the tests assert once a field is in hand. One structural observation that is relevant to Max's lead even though it is not a verdict: [36] sits on a layer that is constitutionally blind to the fault. laws.js:185-188 says so itself — "a drift guard, not an independent physical validation, and not evidence that the law reaches the render." So strengthening the planted-defect controls, however worth doing, buys zero progress on the carrier-off question. The claim "the law reaches the render" is owned by fieldSampler + sweep, and that is where the carrier-off work has to land.

DUPLICATE ACROSS CLUSTERS. [22] (test side) and finding [6] (`bandCount discards short runs instead of folding them`, filed against descriptors.js) are one defect seen from two ends. Fix once: implement the documented fold at descriptors.js:569 and add the noise fixture in the same commit. Do not let them be scheduled as two items.

SUGGESTED ORDER, IF ANY OF THIS IS DONE. (1) [22] — it is the only one with a real source defect behind it, and it should land before any whole-sphere census row is added, because bandCount inflates monotonically upward and would read as a spurious positive radius response. (2) [21] — same reasoning, same precondition: the equirect area weighting is the load-bearing arithmetic for every future whole-sphere row and is currently invisible to CI. (3) [20] and [23] — both are one-line assertion changes that convert knife-edge passes into stated margins, and [20] additionally migrates the fixture onto the dof-aware coverage the fix round already shipped (z = 12.706 at dof 1 gives ~84% headroom where z = 2 gives 0.71%). (4) [36] and [37] — genuine but low-value; [37] in particular guards a descriptor with no caller. (5) [3] — optional hygiene only.

ONE THING TO WATCH IN THE FIX. [20]'s fix touches the same convention the AC-CURVE-live correction block is about: the test renders its verdict via `lawVerdict({ ... claimed: 0.34 })` with neither z nor dof, so it silently takes DEFAULT_Z = 2 — exactly the overstated certainty that forced the census's "0.458 is measurably different from sqrt(R)" claim to be withdrawn. Worth a sweep of every remaining lawVerdict call site for the same omission while the fix is open; that is a broader question than this cluster and I did not audit it.
clusterNotes.descriptors:
SHAPE OF THE CLUSTER. Seven titles, five distinct defects — [0] and [9] are one bug seen from two ends (the equirect autocorrelation), and [7] and [27] are one bug seen from two ends (the mean-of-spans / isotropy precondition in radialPSD). Whoever schedules the fix round should treat them as 5 items, not 7, or the round will look twice as productive as it is.

NONE ARE ALREADY_FIXED. The post-findings fix commit is 0744fa4 and its only touches inside descriptors.js are the `modes` field added to radialPSD's spectrum (:311) and the rewrite of spectralExcessPeak (:343-401). `git show 0744fa4 -- src/worldengine/instrument/descriptors.js` shows no hunk anywhere near autocorrWavelengthKm, bandCount, networkLengthKm, cellAreaKm2 or the spanKm conversions. tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js pins only spectralExcessPeak, fitPowerLaw, lawVerdict/tCritical95 and shiftSignificance. So the cheap-win column is empty for this cluster.

NOT ONE OF THE SEVEN MOVES A BANKED NUMBER, and I checked this per-finding rather than assuming it. Every banked figure — AC-CURVE-live.md's exponents (+0.4583 physical, −0.5417 angular, −0.0417 on-screen, 1.0000 control), its noise-floor table, AC-SAMPLE-live.md's first radius table, the RADIUS-CENSUS substrate/relief row, and the R1 statusNote's band-count numbers — comes from one of three sources, and none of them route through the seven defects: (i) spectralExcessPeak on a SQUARE PATCH grid, whose span conversion is exact because fieldSampler.js:125-126 passes the same scalar twice; (ii) climate-e5.js:218's own zero-crossing counter surfaced as state.e5BandCount, which shares no code with descriptors.bandCount; (iii) the rendered-disc spectral estimator used for the re-UAT. The default sweep probe is a patch (planet-lod-lab.html:6960), so the equirect descriptors — bandCount and the equirect branch of autocorrWavelengthKm — have never run inside a responseCurve or planSweep at all.

THE LIVE-EXPOSURE RANKING, which is what I would act on. [0]/[9] is the only one of the five that a user can hit today by doing the obvious thing: `_lab.fieldProbe()` with no arguments takes the equirect branch (planet-lod-lab.html:6911), that is the first usage the lab's own comment advertises (:6893), and the returned autocorrWavelength is inflated by a large, field-dependent factor — I measured ×1.8 to ×4.2 attributable to the latitude pooling alone on an isotropic control field at the shipped 256×128 geometry, against an equatorial-band control built from the same field. It also silently feeds screenWavelengthProxy on that path (:6939), because `undefined != null` is false and the fallback fires. That is a wrong number presented as a measurement, which is the exact failure class this workstream exists to prevent (feedback_measurement-channels-need-planted-defects). Fix it first. [6] (bandCount) is next: a real over-count, small on the current smooth profiles, and it is the descriptor the atmosphere work will reach for. [8] (networkLengthKm diagonals) is dead code today but is the measurement the census itself names as the next slice (RADIUS-CENSUS.md:145-147, 'a plate-boundary mask… wired into describeSample') — fix it BEFORE the masks land, or the first tectonics measurement carries an orientation bias that will read as signal. [7]/[27] and [26] are contract/documentation debt with no reachable numeric consequence; they are one-line guards and can ride along.

THE '~12%' IN [0] IS THE ONE NUMBER I COULD NOT REPRODUCE. My measurement says the pooling bias is far larger than 12%, but it is field-dependent by construction (it is set by how the field's variance is distributed in latitude), and I measured it on a synthetic isotropic field rather than the lab's actual height field. Direction (inflation) is structural and certain; magnitude on the live field is unmeasured. If anyone wants the live number, the measurement is cheap and specific: probe the same body twice at a fixed seed — once whole-sphere, once as a series of patches tiled along the equator at the equatorial spacing — and compare autocorrWavelength. That is the only NEEDS_MEASUREMENT-shaped question in the cluster, and it affects only how the fix is prioritised, not whether it is real.

CARRIER-OFF LEAD: NEGATIVE ACROSS ALL SEVEN, and I want to be plain about why rather than just ticking false. descriptors.js is field-agnostic — it measures whatever array it is handed and never asks where the field came from. Max's suspicion (and finding [1]) is about WHICH field reaches the instrument: bakeReliefCrossover driving reliefBakeStrength to zero at R ≥ 4 means the sampled body is analytic fBm rather than the baked plate-Voronoi relief. Every defect in this cluster is a grid-geometry or bookkeeping error in the ruler, present identically on either field. There is one interaction worth naming even though it is not a linkage: the carrier-off field is scale-free red noise dominated by the largest scales, which is the regime in which the equirect autocorrelation is most likely to return NaN or a window-scale answer (I saw 3/12 NaN on the full sphere vs 0/12 on the equatorial band). So fixing [0]/[9] would make the instrument's whole-sphere read more informative ABOUT the carrier-off question, but the defect is not caused by it. Verifying Max's lead needs finding [1] and the fieldSampler cluster, not this one.

FIX-ORDER CONSTRAINT worth passing on: descriptors.js sits under src/worldengine/**, so tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js:28 greps it for /visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP/ including comments. The natural way to explain the [0] fix ('this is the physical frame, the other frame is what the display scale keys') would break that fence on a comment alone. Say 'display frame' and name no tokens.
clusterNotes.sampling-laws-rivers:
Headline: all five are REAL, none is ALREADY_FIXED, and NONE changes a banked result. The post-findings fix round (tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js, commit 0744fa4) touches descriptors.js and stats.js only — it does not reach sampling.js, laws.js or planet-lod-rivers.js, so no cheap ALREADY_FIXED wins exist in this cluster. I also corrected severity DOWN on four of the five (14 medium→low, 19 medium→low, 16 medium→low; 28 and 32 stay low), because in each case the defective quantity either cancels out of every descriptor currently computed (14), is quantitatively below the banked numbers' own precision (28), or lives in a layer with no production consumer (19, 32).

CARRIER-OFF LEAD: this cluster is clean of it. All five defects are upstream of, or orthogonal to, the baked-vs-synth split — 14 and 28 are sample-point geometry (true whichever body is being sampled), 19 and 32 are the pure-function drift-guard layer that never touches the shader, and 16 is renderer state hygiene that never reads uReliefBakeStrength or heightSource. I did confirm the anchor while tracing: planet-lod-lab.html:5898 `uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength.value = grainCarveUI.reliefBakeStrength * bakeReliefCrossover(sVis);` drives the UNIFORM to zero as the disc departs, while planet-lod-lab.html:4289 `const carrierOn = grainCarveUI.reliefBakeStrength > 0 && riverOverlay.heightSource === 'carrier';` reads the raw UI value, not the crossover-multiplied uniform — so the World Engine panel can print "relief: writer carrier" while the shader is running at effective bake strength 0. That is evidence for findings [1]/[2], not mine, but it is worth handing to whoever owns them: the panel's own carrier-on readout is not a witness for what the shader is doing at R != 1.

TWO PAIRS THAT SHOULD BE FIXED TOGETHER:
- 19 + 32 compound into one bad diagnostic. If isImpactSurface ever regresses, every crater law's measured quantity collapses to exactly zero, fitPowerLaw (stats.js:98) drops all 7 points, the verdict comes back UNRESOLVABLE — and thanks to 32 the report says `points: 7`. CI still goes red (tests/instrument-laws.test.js:66 asserts allPass), but the operator is told "the sweep was too small" when the truth is "the domain gate stopped firing". Fix 32 first (four existing numbers, laws.js:168), then decide 19 (delete the dead dep, or register the gate as a law of its own).
- 14 + 28 are both patchDirections contract defects and both fixable in the same one-file pass, with the same missing-test shape: the suite pins row order (tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:173) but never column order, and pins corner/centre scale at a fixture 20x easier than the shipped default (:116 vs planet-lod-lab.html:6959-6961). Land the sign fix and the re-pointed scale test together and add the two assertions.

ONE THING I FOUND WHILE TRIAGING THAT IS NOT IN MY FIVE, and I think matters more than three of them: auditLaw passes an explicit `z` into lawVerdict — laws.js:144 `{ deps = defaultDeps(), condition = {}, z = DEFAULT_Z } = {}` and :160-163 `lawVerdict({ ..., nullValue: law.nullValue, z, label: law.id })` — and lawVerdict's coverage selector (stats.js:~176 `const effZ = z != null ? z : (dof != null ? tCritical95(dof) : DEFAULT_Z);`) treats an explicit z as an override. So the tCritical95 fix banked by the review round is structurally unreachable from the law layer: auditLaw never passes `fit.dof`, and always quotes z = 2. It happens to be harmless today because law fits are exact (SE ~ 0, the verdict is decided by the 1e-9 float floor), which is exactly why nobody would notice — and it silently arms itself the moment any law's measure becomes non-deterministic or a field-layer descriptor is registered. Suggest: pass `dof: fit.dof` instead of `z`, and let the caller override only deliberately. Worth routing to whichever cluster owns stats.js/sweep.js.

METHOD NOTE ON EVIDENCE STRENGTH: 14 and 28 I verified numerically (dot(code-east, true-east) = -1.000000 at three lat/lons; corner/centre ratio 0.999538 at the fixture vs 0.951887 at 2000 km / R=0.5, reproducing the title's 4.8% to two digits). 19, 32 and 16 I verified by source-tracing every consumer, including the negative results that bound their blast radius — grep for `auditLaws|defaultDeps|instrument/laws` finds no production caller, and planet-lod-lab.html:5880/:5910/:6413/:6416 re-assert three of the four pieces of state that 16 leaks, leaving only the clear colour (which planet-lod-lab.html:193 sets exactly once). I ran no vitest suite; none of the five verdicts hinged on observed runtime behaviour.
clusterNotes.fieldSampler:
ANCHOR VERDICT: [1] IS REAL AND IT IS MAX'S SUSPICION, WITH A TWIST WORTH TELLING HIM PLAINLY. The legacy synth path is not un-wired from the procgen model — it is wired into the MEASURING INSTRUMENT rather than into the render. planet-lod-rivers.js:323 (`vec4 hd = fbmd(vPos, uOctaves, fwBase);`) is the instrument's entire macro body and has no `uReliefBakeStrength` branch at all; planet-lod-lab.html:381-386 is the planet's, and at the boot default (reliefBakeStrength 1.0, radius 1.0, crossover exactly 1) it weights the synth term by exactly zero. So at the live default the field probe measures a body that contributes literally nothing to the rendered surface, while the World Engine panel simultaneously prints `relief: writer carrier`. The river router was explicitly re-pointed to the carrier in a prior slice (tests/relief-router-repoint.test.js pins it, and pins the createHeightSampler RTT as the "strength-0 fallback"); the instrument was built on that fallback three days later and its header (fieldSampler.js:9-12) still claims the router uses it live. That is the miss.

THE CROSSOVER IS WHY THIS DID NOT SHOW UP IN THE BANKED NUMBERS. bakeReliefCrossover(sVis) with sVis = sqrt(R) zeroes the bake at R >= 4, so at the AC-CURVE sweep radii (4/8/16) the render had ALREADY been handed to the same fbmd body the instrument reads. Instrument and render agree there by accident. They disagree completely at R = 1, the default, and half-disagree at R = 2 and R = 0.5. This means the banked exponent +0.4583 is arithmetically fine but MISATTRIBUTED: RADIUS-CENSUS.md credits the World Engine relief writer with a measured radius response, when what was measured is the legacy analytic body re-keyed by uDispDomainScale = sVis = R^0.5 — which predicts exactly the +0.5 that was found. The writer carrier body has never been sampled at any radius by any banked run, and the census's own tectonics row (five modules with no radius or gravity reference at all) suggests it might show no response. That is the one row in the cluster that should be re-run, and it is a real reason to re-run work rather than a bug-list entry.

ONLY [1] MOVES A BANKED RESULT. The other eight are instrument hygiene. Ranked by what I would actually do:
1. [1] — build a readback that can see the baked body (or resample riverOverlay.reliefCarrier.height directly, which needs no shader work at all), and in the meantime make every sample REPORT the live blend gate so a probe can never again silently describe the wrong field.
2. [4] + [5] together — one new tests/instrument-fieldsampler.test.js. This is the cheapest high-value work in the cluster: fieldSampler.js has ZERO tests of any kind (verified by grep across tests/), so its two headline promises — "changes nothing about the rendered frame" and "no km without kmPerUnit" — are enforced by comments. describeSample is pure and imports headlessly; a fake renderer + fake uniforms object covers the read-only invariant too. Note the perverse detail supporting [5]: heightUnitsToKm, the exact 200x-wrong conversion the workstream withdrew, is still exported and still has GREEN TESTS (tests/instrument-sampling.test.js:23,29,35) while having no live caller.
3. [15] + [4]'s try/finally + [13] — three one-line-ish edits, two of them in the same read() function.
4. [29], [30]+[34], [17] — cosmetic/bookkeeping.

Every PRIMARY citation into src/worldengine/instrument/stats.js is exact: :59, :82, :84, :107, :114, :120, :121, :122, :236-242, :243, :244-247, :250 all say precisely what was claimed, verbatim.   [10] 'stats.js:81 docstring' -> text is at :79-80 (:81 is ` */`)
  [10] 'planet-lod-lab.html:7007' -> the _sweepPlan return is at :7008
  [10] 'instrument-descriptors.test.js:451 comment' -> comment is at :450
  [25] 'planet-lod-lab.html:6960 values array' -> :6961
  [25] 'laws.js:104 values: [...]' -> :104 is `driver: 'radiusEarth'`; values is :105
  [35] 'instrument-review-fixes.test.js:194 expect' -> :195

Not disqualifying, but the pattern is worth flagging to whoever consumes these verdicts, because it is the exact signature that would look identical if a citation HAD been fabricated. I checked all six by grep -n rather than assuming.

ARITHMETIC — redone from the code's own constants, not accepted. For [10] I recomputed ceil((2*cv/0.15)^2) for all seven CVs in the banked table and reproduced the printed column to the digit (1,2,2,4,6,17,103), which independently PROVES that column is a seedsToResolve output rather than a hand-typed figure. For [25] I did not accept the reproduction: I imported the real module read-only and got denom = -7.105427357601002e-15 and exponent -1 for the identical-x case and exponent 2 / SE 1.7657e7 for the weighted case, matching to every digit.

WHERE I PUSHED BACK. [10] is the only one that needed correction, and it needed three. (1) Its headline framing — 'the module's OWN two-ensemble comparison rule' — points at shiftSignificance, which I verified by repo-wide grep has NO production caller anywhere. (2) 'The factor is exactly 2, algebraically, not approximately' is over-confident: DIAGNOSIS.md:182 literally specifies 'check CI overlap', which for equal SEMs requires |delta| > z*(sem_a+sem_b) = 2*z*sem, i.e. M = 4x the one-sample figure. Neither formulation carries a power/beta term, so at the corrected M a true effect of exactly the stated size still clears the bar only ~50% of the time. The honest statement is 2x-to-4x-plus, and the ROOT defect is that the column header 'seeds to resolve 15% at 2σ' names no comparison at all — the fix must choose one before it can pick a number. (3) The adjudicator's third banked-result bullet misreads AC-CURVE-live.md:62-63: 'That is why a 15% bar is now MEASURABLE' maps to seedsToMeasure (column 3, value 1), not to the resolve column. That sentence is untouched; the proposed '2.5x -> 1.7x margin' restatement should be struck. Bullets 1 and 2 stand, so bankedResultClaimHolds is still true.

BANKED-RESULT CLAIMS — checked in BOTH directions, since a missed impact is worse than a false alarm. I grepped all of docs/WORKSTREAMS for seeds-to-resolve language: exactly two carriers exist, AC-CURVE-live.md:52-60 and DIAGNOSIS.md:208, and the adjudicator named both. RADIUS-CENSUS.md, AC-SAMPLE-live.md and the R1 contract statusNote carry none — so [10]'s scope is neither over- nor under-claimed on WHICH documents move. For [25]'s changesBankedResult: false I did not take the negative on trust — I enumerated every fit feeding a banked number (AC-CURVE R in {4,8,16}; the six laws.js literal registries at :69/:79/:94/:105/:115/:127, all strictly increasing; the census's 40-radius dof-38 fit and its 401-log-spaced-radii sweep) and confirmed none repeats a driver value, and separately confirmed that planSweep — the one path that HOLDS a driver fixed — never calls fitPowerLaw. [10] is sample-size algebra, [25] is linear-algebra conditioning, [35] is a NaN-coercion guard; none of the three touches the height-source selection, reliefBakeStrength, or bakeReliefCrossover, and none reads a field sample. verifierNotes.sweep:
All three adjudications SURVIVE. I went in expecting to refute and could not, because the citations are almost entirely exact and the arithmetic reproduces under my own independent simulation rather than theirs.

WHAT I CHECKED INDEPENDENTLY
- Read src/worldengine/instrument/sweep.js (181 lines) and stats.js (254 lines) in full, plus fieldSampler.js:108-214, descriptors.js:55-70, tests/instrument-sweep.test.js:215-240, tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js in full, and both banked evidence docs (AC-CURVE-live.md, RADIUS-CENSUS.md) in full.
- Ran my own 200k-trial Monte Carlo across six (cv, n) combinations instead of trusting the adjudicator's numbers. Its figures reproduced to within Monte-Carlo error in every case: P(drop)=20.9% vs 21.1% claimed; cv-hat 95% [0.331,1.731] vs [0.330,1.724]; seedsToMeasure at n=8 [5,134] vs [5,133]; at n=5 [3,251] exactly as claimed; RMS relief [1,11] as claimed; form wavelength [1,1] as claimed.
- Re-derived every cell of the banked noise-floor table from the shipped formulas (26, 103, 5, 17, 1, 2) — all match, so code and evidence are mutually consistent and the CV inputs are trustworthy.

CITATION INTEGRITY: 3 errors found, all in [24], all non-material
Findings [11] and [12] are citation-clean — every quoted line is verbatim at the stated number, including the non-obvious tests/instrument-sweep.test.js:227. Finding [24] has two off-by-N lab citations (`...d,` is :6920 not :6919; `state.planetRadiusEarth = at;` is :6998 not :6996). The quoted text exists verbatim within the same block, so this is drift rather than fabrication — not grounds to refute, but fix before banking.

ALREADY_FIXED RULED OUT DECISIVELY (the cheap win is not available here)
`git show 0744fa4 -- src/worldengine/instrument/sweep.js` returns an EMPTY diff. The 7-fix round touched stats.js and descriptors.js only; sweep.js was never modified, and tests/instrument-review-fixes.test.js imports nothing from it. `git log --since=2026-07-24` shows no later commit on any of the three instrument files. All three findings live in code the fix round did not reach. This is worth flagging structurally: planSweep is the one module of the instrument that the adversarial fix round left entirely untouched, and all three of these findings are in it.

CARRIER-OFF: all three `false` attributions are CORRECT, and I looked for a reason to disagree
planSweep is frame-agnostic arithmetic over whatever descriptor objects arrive; it never touches reliefBakeStrength, heightSource, or sVis. I confirmed the carrier-off site is real (planet-lod-lab.html:4289 `const carrierOn = grainCarveUI.reliefBakeStrength > 0 && riverOverlay.heightSource === 'carrier';` and :4294 the 'relief: LEGACY synth (carrier off)' print), but it sits in the lab's status panel, four layers away from anything in this cluster. If the carrier-off fault is real it changes WHAT the descriptors measure — which would shift the CV inputs and therefore the seed counts — but that is finding [1]'s claim, not these three. Attributing it here would be exactly the decorative linkage I was told to hunt. Correctly declined by the adjudicator.

TWO CORRECTIONS I AM ADDING THAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED
1. [11] understates its own severity: at the SHIPPED lab default of n=5 (planet-lod-lab.html:6989) the silent-drop probability for the elevation-max row is 25.0%, not the 21.1% quoted for n=8. One re-run in four, not one in five.
2. [11]'s implied fix does not eliminate the defect it names. Replacing `|mean| > sd` with `|mean| > z*sem` moves the censor from cv >= 1 to cv >= sqrt(n)/z = 1.414 at n=8, raising the hard ceiling from 45 to 89 rather than removing it. The 'ceiling independent of actual instrument noise' criticism survives the proposed fix, so the fixSketch needs to say what replaces the ceiling.
Also: [12]'s '0.6x-2.9x' sub-claim is a mislabelled chi-square CI for sigma-given-s, not the sampling range of cv-hat-given-truth; the true sampling range is 0.31x-3.13x at n=5. Right magnitude, wrong conditioning direction, optimistic lower bound. Recorded, not verdict-changing.

BANKED-RESULT CLAIMS — the field I attacked hardest
[11] false: HOLDS, and I strengthened it. Every one of the 7 banked rows sits at CV <= 0.759, so nothing was actually censored in the banked run. Better: the one descriptor that WAS censored (elevation.min, cv 4.84) stays censored under the finding's own proposed corrected predicate, since |mean| 0.006 <= z*sem 0.021. The banked '1040 -> 26' headline is bit-identical under both predicates.
[24] false: HOLDS. radiusEarth and totalArea appear in no banked table, and sweep.js:115-116's Number.isFinite guards make contamination of the headline structurally impossible.
[12] true: HOLDS, but only because the adjudicator states the reading honestly — no point estimate moves, the CLAIMED PRECISION changes. I nearly refuted this on the instruction's strict wording ('name the direction/rough magnitude of the move'), and decided against it on this workstream's own precedent: the tCritical95 correction forced CORRECTION banners onto both AC-CURVE-live.md and RADIUS-CENSUS.md while explicitly preserving 'the point estimates and their SEMs'. Identical class, identical documents. If the triage owner wants 'changesBankedResult' to mean strictly 'a printed number moves', this one should flip to false — flagging the definitional fork rather than deciding it silently.
Critically, the negative half of [12] is the part that matters most and it verifies cleanly: the banked exponents are NOT at risk. Form wavelength at cv 0.088 requires 1 seed with a 95% range of [1, 1] at both n=5 and n=8, so the M=5 radius sweep was comfortably over-sized, and RADIUS-CENSUS.md's own correction block says the same thing from the other direction ('Tightening it needs more driver values (dof scales as N - 2), not more seeds').

NET: 0 of 3 refuted. Confidence high on [11] and [24] (pure code-trace plus reproduced arithmetic, no measurement needed). Confidence high on [12]'s mechanism, medium on whether its banked-result impact meets this triage's bar for 'changes a banked result' — that is a definitional call for the owner, not a source question.

verifierNotes.instrument-tests:
STANCE AND OUTCOME. I attacked all seven and could not overturn any verdict. All seven survive: [3] ALREADY_FIXED, [20][21][22][23][36][37] REAL. But I found four substantive defects in the adjudicator's evidence, one of which is a genuine measurement error, and I recovered banked-result reasoning that all seven got right.

WHAT I DID INDEPENDENTLY. Read in full: descriptors.js, laws.js, fieldSampler.js:155-205, stats.js:150-219, all three attacked test files, instrument-review-fixes.test.js, instrument-sampling.test.js imports, RADIUS-CENSUS.md, AC-CURVE-live.md, AC-SAMPLE-live.md. Re-executed against the shipped modules (read-only, no files written): the null-detection fixture at defaults and with the override; bandCount under 0/1/2-row perturbation; the buried-form spectral fixture including a from-scratch reimplementation of the sigma statistic; the craterSFD population at five slopes; the full UNRESOLVABLE sweep fixture including tol/dClaim/dNull arithmetic on both the z=2 and dof paths; all four planted law defects plus a fifth shared-input defect of my own. Ran `git log --since=2026-07-25` over every implicated file to rule out ALREADY_FIXED for the six REAL verdicts — no commit has touched src/worldengine/instrument or any instrument-*.test.js since 2026-07-25 02:54 (the fix-round commit), which cleanly excludes ALREADY_FIXED for [20][21][22][23][36][37] and confirms it for [3].

DEFECTS FOUND IN THE ADJUDICATOR'S EVIDENCE.
1. [23] MEASUREMENT ERROR, not just a slip. The per-bin sigma table (k=21/22/23/24 -> 8.48/9.99/11.12/9.19) does not reproduce. The correct values are 8.760/10.316/11.482/9.492, and I cross-checked the winner against the module's own returned peakSigma = 11.48176255837236 — matching mine, not theirs. The conclusion drawn from the table survives (runner-up 10.2% below the winner vs their stated 11%), but those four numbers must not be carried forward.
2. [36] REASONING ERROR that inverts a credited defence. The adjudicator claimed to have CHECKED that the g^0.34 defect gives the suite 'a genuine (small) discrimination'. It does not: baselineCondition sets surfaceGravity = G_REF = 0.5, so the injected factor is exactly 1.0 on the radius laws — a strict no-op, not a constant absorbed into an intercept. The finding is stronger than adjudicated.
3. FIVE OFF-BY-ONE LINE CITATIONS, all immaterial to substance but a consistent pattern worth flagging: [3] cited :75 for what is at :76; [21] cited :54 and :72 for what are at :55 and :73; [22] cited planet-lod-lab.html:6963 and :6991 for what are at :6964 and :6992. Every quoted line's CONTENT was accurate — the drift is purely in the numbers, which suggests the adjudicator was reading from an offset view rather than fabricating.
4. [21] ONE UNSOURCED NUMBER PAIR. The '0.44665 vs 0.61525' / '0.78016 vs 0.62774' weighting comparison names no field, so it is unreproducible. I substituted my own latitude-varying equirect field and independently established the qualitative claim (rms 0.23953 cos-weighted vs 0.28853 uniform; hypsometric 0.35911 vs 0.50000). The finding does not depend on their decimals.

BANKED-RESULT AUDIT — the highest-stakes column, and all seven false calls hold. I checked this as a positive search for a MISSED impact, not as a rubber stamp. The decisive fact, which I verified rather than accepted: every banked live measurement ran the PATCH probe. planet-lod-lab.html:6964 (responseCurve) and :6992 (planSweep) both default to `{ mode: 'patch', latDeg: 10, lonDeg: 20, spanKm: 2000, width: 128, height: 128 }`, and both AC-CURVE-live and AC-SAMPLE-live record '2000 km patch at (10 deg, 20 deg)'. That single fact closes [21] and [22] simultaneously: the instrument's bandCount fires ONLY on equirect (fieldSampler.js:180), and areaWeights' cos(lat) term is identically uniform on a patch, so neither defective quantity has ever been an input to a published number. [22]'s census attribution is likewise correct at source — the banked 'band count 5 -> 14, R^0.632' is climate-e5.js:218's zero-crossing counter, and the census's own update block already warns not to confuse it with the law. [37] is dormant code (craterSFD has zero callers repo-wide). [23] and [20] are test-fixture brittleness with no numeric output. [3]'s historical banked impact — the false-positive 1000 km rows at R = 0.5 and R = 1 — is already withdrawn by AC-SAMPLE-live's correction block, so the number is banked-as-corrected and does not move again. [36] correctly qualifies the CONFIDENCE TAG on the bombardment row without moving any exponent in it; that is exactly the right distinction and I would have flagged it as a missed impact had it been called otherwise.

CARRIER-OFF LEAD. All seven set downstreamOfCarrierOffFault: false and all seven are right. I traced each: none of these defects is caused by, masked by, or an alias of the baked-vs-synth split. [3] is a threshold defect that would fire identically on any red-noise field regardless of which field is fed. [21][22][23][37] are coverage/tolerance gaps in descriptor math. [20] is a sweep fixture. [36] is the one that ENGAGES the lead correctly without over-claiming: it observes that laws.js audits pure functions and says so at :185-188, so no amount of strengthening those positive controls could catch a law-does-not-reach-the-render fault — that is a field-layer question owned by fieldSampler. Naming the linkage in the negative while setting the flag false is the correct handling, and I found no decorative attributions to refute.

CLUSTER-LEVEL READ. This cluster is the test-suite half of the review, and its honest summary is that the instrument's descriptor MATH is in better shape than its GUARDS. Nothing here is a wrong number in a banked result. What it is: three unpinned or under-pinned quantities (areaWeights' cos(lat) propagation, bandCount's unweighted latitude profile, the one-sided SFD bracket), two knife-edge fixtures that will produce false alarms on legitimate changes ([20] at 0.71% margin, [23] at 91.6% of tolerance), one live upward-biased defect in shipped code that no banked run happened to exercise ([22]), and one positive-control suite that proves containment rather than discrimination ([36]). Highest-value fixes by ratio of risk-removed to effort: [20] (pass `dof: fit.dof`, one argument, moves the margin from 0.7% to 84%), [23] (assert the bin index or a relative tolerance instead of toBeCloseTo(x, 0)), [37] (add the upper bracket). [22] is the only one requiring a source change, and per the instrument's AC-POSCTRL discipline the fold-vs-drop fix belongs in descriptors.js's own bandCount rather than anywhere in the generation path — note also that tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js greps src/worldengine/** for visScaleOf|sVis|VIS_SCALE_EXP INCLUDING COMMENTS, so any fix comment must avoid those tokens.

BANKED-RESULT AUDIT — the highest-stakes field, and I checked it in the direction the prompt warns about (a missed impact is worse than a false alarm). I read RADIUS-CENSUS.md, AC-CURVE-live.md, AC-SAMPLE-live.md and the R1 contract statusNote in full, then grepped every WORKSTREAMS doc for 'autocorr', 'fieldProbe' and 'totalArea'. Findings:

MAX'S CARRIER-OFF LEAD: all seven `downstreamOfCarrierOffFault: false` calls survive, and I think they are right rather than merely unrefuted. Every one of these seven is a defect in the MEASURING half — grid quadrature, latitude pooling, run-folding, span conversion, neighbour connectivity — and each bites whatever field is handed to it, baked relief or LEGACY synth alike. None is caused by, masked by, or an alias of the baked-vs-synth split. I found no decorative attributions to strike (they attributed none). One genuine INTERACTION worth filing that nobody stated, though it does not warrant flipping the flag: if the sampled field really is LEGACY synth fBm — scale-free red noise with no characteristic wavelength — then autocorrWavelengthKm has no true repeat scale to recover in the first place, so [0]/[9]'s inflation would be riding on top of a quantity that is already meaningless. That compounds the carrier-off fault's consequences without being downstream of it, and it is the same failure shape as AC-SAMPLE finding 2 (the retired 'most energetic bin' metric returning the window size on red noise). Worth a line in the R2 scope.

THE ONE PLACE THE ADJUDICATOR UNDER-CLAIMED, and the most important thing in this report. On [1] it wrote that AC-SAMPLE-live.md's "R = 0.5 / 1 / 2 rows" are already withdrawn. Only R = 0.5 and R = 1 are — the correction block names exactly those two, on the spectralExcessPeak false-positive ground. The R = 2 row (form size 35.1 km, 0.158 deg, excess ratio 1.86) is NOT withdrawn; it sits inside the surviving "R >= 2, where a feature population is actually resolved" reading and anchors the 35 -> 51 -> 71 km / ~sqrt(2) conclusion. At R = 2, bakeReliefCrossover(sqrt(2)) = smoothstep(0, 1, 0.5) = 0.5, so the planet rendered a 50/50 carrier/synth body while the instrument read 100% synth. That is a live, standing banked number taken on a field the planet was only half rendering, and it belongs in [1]'s changesBankedResult list.

THE ONE PLACE IT OVER-CLAIMED. [1]'s changesBankedResult:true is true at the CLAIM level, not the VALUE level, and the entry does not say so plainly enough. No banked number moves — the adjudicator concedes this. What must change is RADIUS-CENSUS.md's `Substrate / relief | WIRED | MEASURED | ∝ R^0.458` attribution, because the measured exponent is fully accounted for by the display lever (uDispDomainScale = sVis feeding planet-lod-height.glsl.js:755) and the World Engine relief writer was never in the sampled field at any radius. The adjudicator's further inference that the carrier "would be nearer exponent 0 than 0.5" is unmeasured; it should carry NEEDS_MEASUREMENT, not be asserted. The measurement that would settle it: force uReliefBakeStrength high across the sweep (freeze bakeReliefCrossover to 1 via a lab-side injection, never by editing src/worldengine/), re-run responseCurve at R = 4/8/16, and compare the fitted physical exponent against the current +0.458. CARRIER-OFF ATTRIBUTIONS. Only [1] carries downstreamOfCarrierOffFault:true, and it earns it with a traced mechanism. I checked [15] specifically for decorative attribution — it is the same CLASS (an unpinned live uniform silently deciding what the instrument measures) but a different uniform and an unrelated cause, and the adjudicator correctly declined to mark it. No over-attribution found anywhere in this cluster.

REACHABILITY ATTACK I RAN THAT COULD HAVE KILLED [15], AND DIDN'T. If the instrument sweep rescaled the camera with the disc, logicalDist would be constant and the "monotone in the swept driver" claim collapses. `grep -n 'state\.distance *='` returns five write sites; :5381 (SWEEP_DISTANCE * sVis) belongs to renderDeltaSweep, the visual golden sweep, NOT responseCurve; :5829 is gated on holdApparentSize, default false; :5846 is a floor of 1.1*sVis = 4.4 at R=16, far below the default 20. Distance stays 20 and [15] survives.

REACHABILITY CHECK THAT STRENGTHENED [1]. I confirmed the baked path is live at boot rather than a dormant branch: planet-lod-lab.html:6430 fires `ensureNetworkRouted('initial')` in a setTimeout, which runs route(), which bakes heightCube. So at the shipped default the planet really is shading from the carrier while the probe reads fbmd.

TWO DEFECTS NEITHER THE REVIEWER NOR THE ADJUDICATOR NAMED, surfaced while verifying, offered for the backlog:
1. fieldSampler.js:191-192 computes `Math.tan((s.meanDeg * Math.PI) / 180)` — the tangent of the mean ANGLE, not the mean gradient. tan(mean(atan(r))) != mean(r). This is the branch that IS live, and it feeds AC-CURVE-live.md's surviving `gradient (mean) | 9.4%` row. Monotone, so the CV survives as a noise measure and no banked number is invalidated, but `meanGradientUnitsPerHorizontal` is not what the code computes. Same mislabelling class as finding [13].
2. The `radiusEarth` positive control is tautological. fieldProbe echoes sample.radiusEarth, which is the same state.planetRadiusEarth that setPoint wrote (planet-lod-lab.html:6971). AC-CURVE-live.md calls it "proof inside every sweep that the driver actually moved"; it is proof the state variable moved and that fitPowerLaw works, and it is structurally incapable of detecting that the driver failed to reach the field. That is precisely the gap finding [1] occupies, so the two should be read together.

No files were written, no source touched, no server started.
